    (hτ : 0<τ) (hb : 0<b) (hζ : ζ≤1/48)
    (e : ℝ) (he : 0<e) (he' : e<1/1000)
    (S : Finset (Ideal O)) (hS : SourceExclusions S) (hmax : ∀P∈S,P.IsMaximal)
    (hfirst : FirstTail (4*e) S)
    (W0 W1 : SchwartzMap ℝ ℂ) (a0 b0 a1 b1 : ℝ) (ha0 : 0<a0) (ha1 : 0<a1)
    (hW0 : Function.support W0⊆Icc a0 b0) (hW1 : Function.support W1⊆Icc a1 b1) :
    ∃C : ℝ,0≤C ∧ ∀(η : Character) (u : FreeRow),u.val≠1 →
      ∀(P : Fin K→PrimeIdeal),Function.Injective P → ∀hPS : ∀j,(P j).val∉S,
      ∀ψ : ι→Character,∀Z : ℝ,1≤Z →
      ((Ideal.span {u.val}:Ideal O).absNorm:ℝ)≤Z^((25/33:ℝ)+ζ) →
      ∀length : Fin K→ℝ,(∑j,length j)=(5/33:ℝ) →
      (∀j,((P j).val.absNorm:ℝ)≤b*Z^(length j)) →
      ∀a B H : ℝ,∀i : ℕ,(51/100:ℝ)≤a → a≤1 → 2<B → Z^τ≤H → H≤(3*i+2:ℕ)*B →
      detectorMaximum (sourceDetectorFamily S hS.prime η u ψ) (3*(i+1:ℕ)*B)<a+2*e →
      ‖rowIntegral η S (calibrationForSet S hmax) (fun j=>CompletedGauss.primaryGenerator (P j).val)
          W0 W1 (Z^(13/33:ℝ)) (Z^(15/33:ℝ)) Z u-
        centralCubeIntegral S hS hmax P hPS η u W0 W1 (Z^(13/33:ℝ)) (Z^(15/33:ℝ)) Z a e H‖≤
        C*(η.modulus.absNorm:ℝ)^2*Z^(-saving)

statement:
def SameDataTransportAt
    {Delta : ℝ} (D : HighDataPerturbed Delta)
    (hfine : ∀j, D.ell j ≤ detectorMesh D.t / 200)
    (F : PerturbedSourceData (momentGeometryOfPerturbed D hfine))
    (theta : ℝ) : Prop :=
  letI : NeZero (∏P∈F.S, P) := ⟨fixedPrimeProduct_ne_zero F.S F.exclusions.prime⟩
  ∃n : ℕ, 0 < n ∧ ∀eta : Character, ∃Ct : ℝ, 0 < Ct ∧ ∀ᶠZ : ℝ in atTop,
    let Y : Fin D.N → ℝ := fun j => Z ^ (D.ell j)
    let T : Fin D.N → Finset PrimeIdeal := fun j =>
      pool (RayQuotient.identityClass F.modulus ⊤) F.S 1 2 (Y j)
    let hT := transportPoolOutside (M := F.modulus) (⊤) F.S D.N 1 2 Y
    let normer := sourceResidueConstant F.W F.W (∏P∈F.S, P) *
      (Probe.principalScalar Finset.univ Z totalE
        (slotMass T (residueWeights (fun _ => F.w) Y)) : ℂ)
    normer ≠ 0 ∧ ∃idx grid : FreeRow → ℕ,
    (∀u, 1 ≤ idx u ∧ idx u ≤ n ∧ grid u ≤ ⌊(49 / 100 : ℝ) / D.e⌋₊ ∧
      ((3 * idx u + 1 : ℕ) : ℝ) * Z ^ theta + Z ^ theta / 2 ≤
        (3 * idx u + 2 : ℕ) * Z ^ theta) ∧
    (∀u, let alpha : ℝ := 51 / 100 + D.e * grid u
      (51 / 100 : ℝ) ≤ alpha ∧ alpha ≤ 1 ∧
      alpha ≤ detectorMaximum
        (sourceDetectorFamily F.S F.exclusions.prime eta u
          (rayCubeFamily F.modulus ⊤ le_top u))
        (3 * idx u * Z ^ theta) ∧
      detectorMaximum
        (sourceDetectorFamily F.S F.exclusions.prime eta u
          (rayCubeFamily F.modulus ⊤ le_top u))
        (3 * idx u * Z ^ theta) < alpha + D.e ∧
      detectorMaximum
        (sourceDetectorFamily F.S F.exclusions.prime eta u
          (rayCubeFamily F.modulus ⊤ le_top u))
        (3 * (idx u + 1 : ℕ) * Z ^ theta) < alpha + 2 * D.e ∧
      ((51 / 100 : ℝ) < alpha → ∃j s,
        LFunction
          (sourceDetectorFamily F.S F.exclusions.prime eta u
            (rayCubeFamily F.modulus ⊤ le_top u) j) s = 0 ∧
        ¬((sourceDetectorFamily F.S F.exclusions.prime eta u
            (rayCubeFamily F.modulus ⊤ le_top u) j).residue = 1 ∧ s = 1) ∧
        alpha ≤ s.re ∧ s.re < alpha + D.e ∧
        |s.im| ≤ 3 * idx u * Z ^ theta)) ∧
    (∀u∈rowBand (Z ^ (1 / 100 : ℝ)) (Z ^ (physicalHeight + D.t)),
      (calibrationForSet F.S F.maximal).residueMonoid u.val ≠ 0 →
      (∀chi, (rayCubeFamily F.modulus ⊤ le_top u chi).residue ≠ 1) ∧
      (∀chi, (rayCubeFamily F.modulus ⊤ le_top u chi).modulus.absNorm ≤
        conductorConstant * F.modulus.absNorm *
          (Ideal.span {u.val} : Ideal O).absNorm) ∧
      ∀hnp : ∀chi, (rayCubeFamily F.modulus ⊤ le_top u chi).residue ≠ 1,
        HeckeDetectorZeros.zeroMaximum (rayCubeFamily F.modulus ⊤ le_top u) hnp
          (3 * (idx u + 1 : ℕ) * Z ^ theta) <
            51 / 100 + D.e * grid u + 2 * D.e) ∧
    let rows := rowBand (Z ^ (1 / 100 : ℝ)) (Z ^ (physicalHeight + D.t))
    let alpha : FreeRow → ℝ := fun u => 51 / 100 + D.e * grid u
    let height : FreeRow → ℝ := fun u => (3 * idx u + 1 : ℕ) * Z ^ theta
    ‖HighFrontierTargets.normalizedProbeAt F.modulus ⊤ F.S F.exclusions
        F.maximal D.ell 1 2 (fun _ => F.w) F.W F.W totalE sourceLx sourceLy eta Z -
      HeckeSignal.signal (eta.excludePrimes F.S F.exclusions.prime)
        (sourceCorrection eta F.S) (-11 / 16) Z -
      finiteCentralCubeRows F.S F.exclusions F.maximal eta rows T hT
        (fun _ y => (F.w y : ℂ)) Y F.W F.W
        (Z ^ sourceLx) (Z ^ sourceLy) Z D.e alpha height / normer‖ ≤
      Ct * Z ^ (HeckeZeroSupremum.beta - 11 / 16 - D.sigma)

theorem all_natural_mixed_join (a b radial B Bfixed L Mcap ε : ℝ)
    (ha : 0 < a) (hb : 0 ≤ b) (hBfixed : 0 ≤ Bfixed) (hε : 0 < ε)
    (Q : Ideal O) (hQ : Q ≠ 0) (Jn : ℕ) (Sn : Finset (ℕ × ℕ)) (Cn : ℝ) :
    ∃ Jf : ℕ, ∃ Sf : Finset (ℕ × ℕ), ∃ Cf : ℝ, 0 < Cf ∧
      ∀ Z : ℝ, NonfixedMixedAt Q a b radial B L Mcap ε Z Jn Sn Cn →
      ∀ s : NaturalPlainState Z B radial 1, s.width ≤ Mcap →
      (s.puncture.absNorm : ℝ) ≤ Z ^ B →
      (∀ z, s.radial.keep z →
        ((excluded (naturalPlainCharacter s.character z) s.puncture).modulus.radical.absNorm : ℝ) ≤ Z ^ Bfixed) →
      ∀ W₁ W₂ : 𝓢(ℝ, ℂ), Function.support (W₁ : ℝ → ℂ) ⊆ Set.Icc a b →
        Function.support (W₂ : ℝ → ℂ) ⊆ Set.Icc a b →
      ∀ X₁ X₂ t₁ t₂ : ℝ, 0 < X₁ → 0 < X₂ → X₁ ≤ Z ^ L → X₂ ≤ Z ^ L →
      s.energy W₁ W₂ X₁ X₂ t₁ t₂ ≤
        Cn * diagonalControl s.radial.profile *
          ((Sn.sup (schwartzSeminormFamily ℝ ℝ ℂ) W₁) *
           (Sn.sup (schwartzSeminormFamily ℝ ℝ ℂ) W₂)) ^ 2 *
          (1 + ‖t₁‖) ^ Jn * (1 + ‖t₂‖) ^ Jn * Z ^ (s.width + ε) +
        Cf * diagonalControl s.radial.profile *
          ((Sf.sup (schwartzSeminormFamily ℝ ℝ ℂ) W₁) *
           (Sf.sup (schwartzSeminormFamily ℝ ℝ ℂ) W₂)) ^ 2 *
          (1 + ‖t₁‖) ^ Jf * (1 + ‖t₂‖) ^ Jf * Z ^ (s.rowWidth + ε)
title: all_natural_mixed_join

statement:
\begin{theorem}\label{main}
All finite-order Hecke $L$-functions over $F$, and all
Dirichlet $L$-functions, are zero-free in the strict half-plane
\[
             \Rea s>\frac{3499999}{4000000}.
\]
The pole at $s=1$ for a principal character is allowed. The boundary is
$1/4000000$ smaller than $7/8$; no assertion is made about zeros on the
boundary line.
\end{theorem}

theorem actual_uniform_cube_arithmetic_saving {Δ:ℝ}{D:Parameters.HighData Δ}
    (S:SourceData D)(nslots:ℕ)(lengths:Fin nslots→ℝ)(hpos:∀s,0<lengths s)(hinj:Function.Injective lengths)
    (hsum:∑j,lengths j=QRH.ell)(hsmall:∀j,lengths j≤D.t/200)
    (hmin:∀j,(7/8:ℝ)*D.rmin≤lengths j)
    (hbeta:(51/100:ℝ)≤HeckeZeroSupremum.beta)
    (hfine:∀j,lengths j≤dynamicMesh D.t/200):
    ∃J:ℕ,∀(n:ℕ)(τ logCost heightCost loss ν ζ μ saving:ℝ),
      0<τ→τ<(1/200:ℝ)/2→4*τ<(1/200:ℝ)*D.cost→
      0<logCost→τ<heightCost→τ*(2+4*D.eps)<loss→0<ν→0≤ζ→0≤μ→0<saving→
      159*D.ε+D.t+D.t+7*ν≤1/32→
      QRH.h*(159*D.ε+D.t+D.t+7*ν)+2*ζ+(3/2)*μ+
        (26*D.e+(nslots+8)*D.eps+loss+D.t*QRH.ell)+
        (logCost+heightCost+heightCost*(J:ℝ))+saving≤Δ/4→
    ∀η:Character,∃C:ℝ,0<C ∧ ∀ᶠZ:ℝ in atTop,
    1<Z ∧ ∀gap:ℝ,0≤gap→Δ≤gap→gap≤(1-QRH.kappa0)/2→
      2*HeckeZeroSupremum.beta-1≤QRH.kappa0+2*gap→
    ∀d:ℝ,(1/200:ℝ)≤d→d≤7/8→∀(v a:ℝ)(i:ℕ),i≤n→
      0≤v→v≤QRH.h+ζ→v≤1→d-v≤μ→51/100<a→a≤1→
    ∀rows:Finset FreeRow,rows.Nonempty→
    (∀u∈rows,u.val≠1 ∧ Z^(1/100:ℝ)≤rowNorm u ∧
      (calibrationForSet S.S S.maximal).residueMonoid u.val≠0 ∧ rowNorm u≤Z^(d-D.t))→
    (∀u∈rows,Z^v≤rowNorm u ∧ rowNorm u≤2*Z^v)→
    (∀u∈rows,detectorMaximum (sourceDetectorFamily S.S S.exclusions.prime η u
      (rayCubeFamily S.modulus ⊤ le_top u)) (3*(i+1:ℕ)*Z^τ)<a+2*D.e)→
    (∀u∈rows,a≤detectorMaximum (sourceDetectorFamily S.S S.exclusions.prime η u
      (rayCubeFamily S.modulus ⊤ le_top u)) ((3*i:ℕ)*Z^τ))→
    ∀t:ProbeMellinBoundary.HeightSpace,
      ((|t.1.1|≤(3*i+1:ℕ)*Z^τ ∧ |t.2|≤(3*i+1:ℕ)*Z^τ) ∧ |t.1.2|≤(3*i+1:ℕ)*Z^τ)→
      |t.1.2|≤Z^heightCost→
    let Y:Fin nslots→ℝ

      ∀(G : ι → 𝓢(ℝ,ℂ)) (χ : ι → Character) (P : ι → ℂ)
        (s X : ι → ℝ) (lo hi D E : ℝ),
      lo ≤ hi → (∀i, 0 < s i) → (∀i, 0 < X i) →
      (∀i, Real.log (X i) ∈ Set.Icc lo hi) → 0 < D → 0 ≤ E →
      (∀i, H.sup (schwartzSeminormFamily ℝ ℝ ℂ) (G i) ≤ D) →
      (∀v w : ℝ, ∀j k : Fin 2, ∀x ∈ Set.Icc lo hi, ∀y ∈ Set.Icc lo hi,
        (∑i, ‖polynomial (χ i) false (scaleTest (fun z : ℝ => (annulus z:ℂ)) j)

## Pins

- Lean 4.34.1 (`leanprover/lean4:v4.34.1`, commit
  `5045d0056413266e57c625dcd7c365b10e377c52`), `formalization/lean-toolchain`.
- Original development: `github.com/akashlevy/math` at
  `c388e88e6519d139ad2ca5571ef0c7fbf0e245b5` (branch `qrh-23-24-pruned`; tag
  `qrh-weighted-10499-12000-base`),
  which is `github.com/openai/math` at `fd4aeeb2ee4fc729c18d98444fed42fd0529eeeb`
  with unused declarations pruned in place; its added 23/24 modules are not
  imported by this proof.
- Mathlib `d13f23b723b8a846827a245b89c10fc7d3f11612`; PrimeNumberTheoremAnd
  `c39a751132c88b6e8080b74c74023fd95b3d8be0` and rellich-kondrachov
  `70f85d4c1bf99c6e7d61e8be4daa6f3664d08d23`, each with the fork's
  `lean/patches/<name>-lean4341.patch`; all packages in
  `formalization/lake-manifest.json`.
- Three-kernel judge: `lake comparator`, `leanchecker` (Lean default kernel),
  `nanoda_bin` and `con-ron` from the official Lean v4.35.0-rc2
  `lean-4.35.0-rc2-darwin_aarch64.tar.zst` (SHA-256
  `e721cf30671d3830fa6120c7b1a4e6b22624650ce1d618c0ca28a4889f5ef324`, equal to

statement:
### 5.1. The intermediate rows and the square certificate

For \(U=Z^d\), \(d_{\min}\le d\le h+\zeta_0\), fix the bins of §3 before moving contours. In the compensated identity (2.8), first move \(z\) to \(z_0=17/50\), with \(s,w\) on absolute lines. Move \(s\) to \(\beta_*+20e\), then \(w\) to \(1-a-6e\). The paths lie in \(\mathcal B\): \(\Re(s+w)>1\), the numerator is nonprincipal, and the reciprocal remains global. Truncate heights while that reciprocal is still global. Move only the retained \(s\)-segment to \(a+16e\), within its buffered zero-free rectangle. The horizontal joins have the same buffer. Use (2.15) only on the resulting central contour.

The row count (3.15), buffered reciprocal bound (3.10), reflected numerator bound, prime estimate (3.12), and Lemma 2.1 give, for a nonfloor bin,
\[
 \sum_{u\in\mathcal B_a}
 \left|q_u^{-z}\frac{L_K^S(w,\psi_u)}{L_K^S(s,\eta\overline{\psi_u})}
 \mathcal H_{\eta,u,Z}\right|
 \ll(1+T)^A U^{R_0(\delta)+\delta/2-z_0+\varepsilon}
 Z^{\ell(z_0-1/2)+\ell\delta/2+\varepsilon}.
\tag{5.1}
\]
The geometric Mellin factors make its exponent, relative to \(\beta_*-k\),
\[
 \mathcal E(d)=a-\beta_*+h(z_0-1/6)-ay-\ell/2+\ell\delta/2
 +d\{R_0(\delta)+\delta/2-z_0\},
\tag{5.2}
\]
before small losses. The slope is positive, since
\(R_0(\delta)+\delta/2-z_0\ge1-\delta/2-17/50\ge73/300\).
At \(d=h\), (2.1) reduces the exponent to \(F_0(\delta)-\beta_*\), where
\[
 F_0(\delta)=\frac{16}{11}\frac{1+\delta}{2}
       +\frac{25}{33}\left(R_0(\delta)-\frac23\right)-\frac5{33},\qquad
 \boxed{\frac{29}{33}-F_0(\delta)=
 \frac{(12\delta-5)^2}{99(5-2\delta)}\ge0}
 \quad(0\le\delta\le5/6).
\tag{5.3}
\]
Thus every shorter dyad saves at least \(\mu\); the extension to \(h+\zeta_0\) costs \(O(\zeta_0)\). The floor uses count exponent one at \(a=51/100\), and its boundary is below \(b\) by \(89/2475\). Choose \(\zeta_0\) and the real losses much smaller than \(\mu\). Equality in (5.3) occurs only at \(\delta=5/12\), but still gives a strict saving under the contradiction hypothesis.
title: 5.1. The intermediate rows and the square certificate

statement:
### B1.2. Prime Gauss sums and squarefree coefficients

Write \(g_\chi(p,h)=\sum_{x\bmod p}\chi(x)e(hx/p)\), and \(Q=q_p\). The finite Gauss–Jacobi identity, obtained by grouping the double Gauss sum according to \(x+y\), is
\[
g_A(p,1)g_B(p,1)=J(A,B)g_{AB}(p,1),\quad
J(A,B)=\sum_xA(x)B(1-x),
\tag{B1.6}
\]
when \(A,B,AB\) are nonprincipal. Also \(g_Ag_{\bar A}=A(-1)Q\).

For \(\psi=\chi_p^2\), reduction of \(J(\psi,\psi)\) modulo \(p\) gives the sum of \(x^{(Q-1)/3}(1-x)^{(Q-1)/3}\), a polynomial of degree less than \(Q-1\), so \(p\mid J\). Its absolute value is \(\sqrt Q\). The order-three map \(x\mapsto1/(1-x)\) preserves the summand; its two fixed points have \(x(1-x)=1\), and every other orbit has size three. Therefore \(J\equiv-1\pmod{3\mathcal O}\). Since \(p\) is primary, the unit \(J/p\) is \(-1\), and \(J=-p\). Applying (B1.6) gives
\[
\gamma_2(p)^3=-\alpha(p).
\tag{B1.7}
\]
The changes of variable \(x=(1+y)/2\) and \(y\mapsto y/(y-1)\), with zero extensions at the omitted points, give
\[
J(\chi^2,\chi^2)=\overline{\chi(4)}^{\,2}J(\chi^3,\chi^2)
=\overline{\chi(4)}^{\,2}J(\chi,\chi^2),\qquad \chi=\chi_p.
\]
Since \(\chi(4)^3=1\), (B1.6) now yields
\[
\gamma_1(p)\gamma_2(p)=-\alpha(p)G(p).
\tag{B1.8}
\]
CRT gives, for coprime squarefree \(a,b\),
\[
\gamma_j(ab)=\gamma_j(a)\gamma_j(b)\chi_a(b)^j\chi_b(a)^j.
\tag{B1.9}
\]
Cubing this formula, and using (B1.4)–(B1.8), proves
\[
\gamma_2(c)^3=\mu(c)\alpha(c),\qquad
\gamma_1(c)\gamma_2(c)=\mu(c)\alpha(c)G(c),
\]
\[
\mu(c)\gamma_{-1}(c)=\chi_c(-1)G(c)^{-1}\overline{\alpha(c)}\gamma_2(c).
\tag{B1.10}
\]
The last formula also follows directly from \(\gamma_1(c)\gamma_{-1}(c)=\chi_c(-1)\). Finally, for \(a_\nu(c)=\overline{\alpha(c)}\gamma_2(c)\nu(c)\), reciprocity in (B1.9) gives
\[
a_\nu(ab)=a_\nu(a)a_\nu(b)\chi_b(a)^4.
\tag{B1.11}
\]
title: B1.2. Prime Gauss sums and squarefree coefficients

statement:
## Packaging repair and attribution

The pinned author repository omitted all 2,925 vendor modules declared in its
closure manifest, omitted `vendor/LICENSE`, and laid out several proof modules
outside their import namespaces. Our `prepare.py` restores the layout and reads
the exact vendor git objects at OpenAI/math
`adc7f1241b42e322a6451854ab7e4b4c146bf78a`. All declared SHA256 values and git blob
IDs match. No proof text was edited. Those 2,925 source hashes also match the
public accepted OpenAI/math revision `fd4aeeb2ee4fc729c18d98444fed42fd0529eeeb`.

No LICENSE or redistribution grant was found in Liu's pinned repository or
README. This package therefore contains our reproduction tools and verification
evidence, with links to upstream. It contains no copied Liu Lean source or
exported proof data. The scripts fetch the source directly from its author.
The native dependency audit checks both pinned revisions and the exact
compatibility patches supplied by Liu; all 19 selected files from the two
patched dependencies match that reconstruction.
title: Packaging repair and attribution

statement:
\begin{lemma}[Pointwise dyadic estimates]\label{lem:detector-dyads}
Fix bounded nonnegative ranges for \(r,m\), and let
\[
 M_r=M_\psi(r;W_M),\qquad S_m=S_\psi(m;W_S)
\]
denote the two polynomials in \eqref{own:central-polynomials},
now at base \(U\).  Suppose
\(\psi\in\mathcal X_u\), the untwisted profiles have uniformly
bounded smooth seminorms on a fixed annulus, and any pure norm twist
has height at most \((3i+1)T_1\).  All additional Mellin frequencies
entering the same \(L\)-argument are required to have total absolute
value at most \(T_1/2\).

For every \(\epsilon>0\), there are \(e_0>0\), depending only on
\(\epsilon\) and the bounded length ranges, and a finite height
order \(A_{\mathcal A}\), uniform in the moving rows and profiles,
such that, when
\[
 0<e<e_0,\qquad (1+T_1)^{A_{\mathcal A}}\le U^{\epsilon/10},
\]
the following estimates hold for sufficiently large \(Z\):
\begin{equation}
 |M_r|^2\ll_{\mathcal A,\epsilon}U^{\delta r+\epsilon},
 \label{old-eq:6.2}
\end{equation}
\begin{equation}
 |S_m|^2\ll_{\mathcal A,\epsilon}
       U^{\delta\min(m,1-m)+\epsilon}.
 \label{old-eq:6.3}
\end{equation}
The external tail order may be chosen after the positive number
\(\tau\).  It does not change \(A_{\mathcal A}\).
\end{lemma}
title: lem:detector-dyads

statement:
### B2.3. Common profiles and whole-series tails

For \(A,B\ge0\), with \(B\) an integer, set
\[
\mathcal M_{A,B}(V)=
\sup_{-A\le\eta\le1/4}\int_{\mathbb R}
(1+|t|)^B|\widehat V(\eta+it)|\,dt.
\]
The first negative numerator pole of \(\mathcal R\) is \(-5/6\), and on \(-1/4\le\sigma\le A\),
\(|\mathcal R(\sigma+it)|\ll_A(1+|t|)^{4\sigma}\).
Shifting (B2.12) to \(-1/4,0,A\) therefore proves
\[
|(x\partial_x)^jV^\sharp(x)|
\ll_{A,j}\min\{x^{1/4},(1+x)^{-A}\}
\mathcal M_{A,\lceil4A\rceil+j+2}(V).
\tag{B2.21}
\]
These are finite seminorms: \(B+2\) integrations by parts bound \(\mathcal M_{A,B}\) by
\[
\ll_{A,B}\int_0^\infty
(1+x^{-A}+x^{1/4})\bigl(|V(x)|+|(x\partial_x)^{B+2}V(x)|\bigr)\frac{dx}{x}.
\]
Replacing \(V\) by \(x^{it_0}V\) costs at most \((1+|t_0|)^B\).

On a fixed compact logarithmic box, let
\(F_Y(\mathbf y)=W(\mathbf y)V^\sharp(Y\prod_i y_i^{a_i})\), where \(Y\) is constant within the block. Euler differentiation and (B2.21) bound every fixed derivative of \(F_Y\) by
\[
m_A(Y)=\min\{Y^{1/4},(1+Y)^{-A}\}
\]
times fixed seminorms. Fourier integration by parts in all logarithmic variables shows that the common separating density has weighted \(L^1\)-norm bounded by the same scalar. For a row vector linear in this whole profile, write \(F_Y=m_A(Y)\widetilde F_Y\), apply its single common Fourier inversion, and then Minkowski:
\[
\|U(F_Y)\|_{\ell^2(I)}
\le m_A(Y)\int |\widehat{\widetilde F_Y}(\mathbf t)|
\|B(\mathbf t)\|_{\ell^2(I)}\,\frac{d\mathbf t}{(2\pi)^d}.
\tag{B2.22}
\]
Only now may the positive row set be enlarged. The separated formula defines \(B\) on the added rows; no kernel estimate is asserted there. Squaring gives \(m_A(Y)^2\). In particular the small-argument gain for a linear reflected sum is \(Y^{1/2}\) in its energy. Choosing separate Fourier densities for different rows would not justify (B2.22).

For either lattice \(\Lambda=\mathcal O,\lambda^{-4}\mathcal O\), if \(|K(x)|\le C_Ax^{-A}\) for \(x\ge1\), \(A>1\), then
\[
\sum_{\substack{0\ne\mu\in\Lambda\\a q_\mu>U}}|K(aq_\mu)|
\ll_A C_A(1+a^{-1})U^{1-A}\qquad(a>0,\ U\ge1).
\tag{B2.23}
\]
Indeed the shell \(2^jU<aq_\mu\le2^{j+1}U\) has \(O(1+2^jU/a)\) lattice points; sum the two resulting geometric series. This estimate controls the entire discarded dual series, without presupposing a bound on its retained indices.
title: B2.3. Common profiles and whole-series tails

    ∃theta : ℝ, 0 < theta ∧ theta < (1 / 200 : ℝ) / 2 ∧

      ∀eta : Character, ∃C : ℝ, 0 < C ∧ ∀ᶠZ : ℝ in atTop,

          G.ell (fun _ => F.w) (1 / 200) (7 / 8) 2 G.ε G.t G.t G.t

def errorLabelNumerator {K : ℕ} (S : Finset (Ideal O)) (hS : SourceExclusions S)
    (η : Character) (u : FreeRow) (J : Finset (Fin K))
    (T : Fin K→Finset HeckeInverseAmplification.PrimeIdeal)
    (hT : ∀i P,P∈T i→P.val∉S) (W : Fin K→ℝ→ℂ) (Yp : Fin K→ℝ)
    (x z : ℂ) (W1 : ℝ→ℂ) (Y : ℝ) : ℂ :=
  ∑P:(∀i:J,T i.val),(∏i:J,physicalSlotWeight (P i).val (W i.val) (Yp i.val) z)*
    errorNumeratorIntegral S hS η u (Finset.univ.image (fun i:J=>(P i).val))
      (partial_image_supported S hS J T hT P) x z W1 Y

/-- The normalized full-w integral of the actual calibrated prime tuples equals
its error-label numerators times the remaining, unaltered prime sums. -/
title: errorLabelNumerator

statement:
def padState {Z B radial Cfixed : ℝ}
    (s : NaturalPlainState Z B radial Cfixed) (t : ℝ)
    (ht : 0 ≤ t) (hC : Cfixed ≤ Z ^ t) : NaturalPlainState Z B radial 1 where
  character := s.character
  puncture := s.puncture
  radial := s.radial
  rowWidth := s.rowWidth
  characterWidth := s.characterWidth + t
  displayedSupport := s.displayedSupport
  displayed_squarefree := s.displayed_squarefree
  displayed_bound := s.displayed_bound.trans
    (Real.rpow_le_rpow_of_exponent_le s.base_ge_one (by linarith))
  displayed_zeros := s.displayed_zeros
  base_ge_one := s.base_ge_one
  row_nonneg := s.row_nonneg
  character_nonneg := add_nonneg s.character_nonneg ht
  scale_eq := s.scale_eq
  modulus_bound := by
    have hz : 0 < Z := zero_lt_one.trans_le s.base_ge_one
    apply s.modulus_bound.trans
    simpa only [one_mul, mul_one, Real.rpow_add hz, mul_comm] using
      mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_right hC (Real.rpow_nonneg hz.le s.characterWidth)
  puncture_ne_zero := s.puncture_ne_zero
  puncture_bound := s.puncture_bound
  radial_support := s.radial_support
  row_ne_zero := s.row_ne_zero
  row_nonprincipal := s.row_nonprincipal
title: padState

statement:
def SourceBins {e : ℝ} (F : ZetaZeroFree.Analytic.SourceData e) (η : Character)
    (Z τ : ℝ) (n : ℕ) (idx grid : FreeRow→ℕ) : Prop :=
  (∀u,1 ≤ idx u ∧ idx u≤n ∧ grid u≤⌊(49/100:ℝ)/e⌋₊ ∧
    (3*idx u+1:ℕ)*Z^τ+Z^τ/2≤(3*idx u+2:ℕ)*Z^τ) ∧
  (∀u,let a : ℝ := 51/100+e*grid u
    51/100≤a ∧ a≤1 ∧
    a≤detectorMaximum (sourceDetectorFamily F.S F.exclusions.prime η u
      (rayCubeFamily F.modulus ⊤ (by exact le_top) u)) ((3*idx u:ℕ)*Z^τ) ∧
    detectorMaximum (sourceDetectorFamily F.S F.exclusions.prime η u
      (rayCubeFamily F.modulus ⊤ (by exact le_top) u)) ((3*idx u:ℕ)*Z^τ)<a+e ∧
    detectorMaximum (sourceDetectorFamily F.S F.exclusions.prime η u
      (rayCubeFamily F.modulus ⊤ (by exact le_top) u)) ((3*(idx u+1):ℕ)*Z^τ)<a+2*e ∧
    (51/100<a → ∃j s,LFunction (sourceDetectorFamily F.S F.exclusions.prime η u
      (rayCubeFamily F.modulus ⊤ (by exact le_top) u) j) s=0 ∧
      ¬((sourceDetectorFamily F.S F.exclusions.prime η u
        (rayCubeFamily F.modulus ⊤ (by exact le_top) u) j).residue=1 ∧ s=1) ∧
      a≤s.re ∧ s.re<a+e ∧ |s.im|≤(3*idx u:ℕ)*Z^τ))
title: SourceBins

    (base : ∀ i, α i) (A S : ∀ i, α i → ℂ) (N : ∀ i, α i → ℝ)
    (hN : ∀ i e, 0 < N i e) (Lc : ι → ℝ) (kap U xi : ℝ) (n : ℕ)
    (valid : ∀ i, α i → Prop) [∀ i e, Decidable (valid i e)]
    (Q : ℕ → ι → ℂ) (P : ι → ℂ)
    (R q L z delta loss epsilon Ccount Cmoment M : ℝ)
    (hkap : 7/10 ≤ kap) (hM : 0 < M) (hU : 1 ≤ U) (hxi : 0 ≤ xi)
    (hc : 1 ≤ Ccount) (hm : 1 ≤ Cmoment) (hq : 0 ≤ q) (hqdelta : q ≤ delta/2)
    (hcard : (Fintype.card ι : ℝ) ≤ Ccount*U^R)
    (hzero : ∀ i e, ¬valid i e → S i e = 0)
    (hupper : ∀ i e, valid i e → max 1 (Lc i * N i e) ≤ U^((n : ℝ)*xi))
    (hseries : ∀ i, Summable (fun e=>‖A i e*(N i e:ℂ)^(-(1/2:ℂ))*S i e‖))
    (hs : ∀ i, Summable (fun e => ‖A i e‖ * (N i e)^(-(1 / 2 : ℝ)) *
      max 1 (Lc i * N i e)^(delta/4)))
    (hmass : ∀ i, (∑' e, ‖A i e‖ * (N i e)^(-(1 / 2 : ℝ)) *
      max 1 (Lc i * N i e)^(delta/4)) ≤ M)
    (hselected : ∀ j ∈ Finset.range (n+1), ∀ i,
      U^(q*selectedCapacity kap z ((j : ℝ)*xi+xi)-loss) ≤ ‖Q j i‖)
    (hfull : ∀ i, ‖P i‖ ≤ U^(q*L))
    (hselection : ∀ j ∈ Finset.range (n+1), ∀ e : ∀ i, α i,

      ((n+1 : ℕ) : ℝ)*M*Ccount*Cmoment*

statement:
## Reproduction

Run from this snapshot's root on Linux with Python 3, Git, tar, and zstd.
Setup downloads the exact pinned public sources, Lean compiler, and official
Mathlib cache. No private repository or private Git history is required.

```sh
python3 tools/setup_workspace.py --with-dependencies
python3 tools/reproduce_tightened.py --output replay --compare-formalization compressed/formalization
python3 compressed/scripts/build_cached.py QRH QRH.Analytic QRH.Detector.UniformDetectorCount QRH.Hecke.DynamicBatchCount --jobs 16
python3 compressed/scripts/verify_tightening.py --numerator 874957019420098946128604623 --denominator 1000000000000000000000000000
python3 tools/count_lean_tokens.py
```

The first replay reconstructs the compressed proof from the immutable public
baseline, applies the rational tightening, and checks every final source byte.
The recorded replay matches all 210 source/configuration files. Source replay
alone is not proof verification; the subsequent build and target gates are
required. Compiler objects and local build logs are regenerated rather than
shipped. The archived native reports describe the completed author-side run.
The external checker suite remains a separate required step before upgrading
the catalogue status.

`compression-result.json` and `tightening-result.json` describe the final
251,464-token candidate. `tightening/baseline/` retains the historical
251,528-token compression-stage reports.
`publication-transformations.json` identifies neutralized workspace paths in
runtime metadata. Mathematical source bytes and gate outcomes are unchanged.
The repository manifest and public archive checksum authenticate the published
snapshot. Historical source-preparation reports may say that they had not yet
been Lean verified; the final target report records the later completed check.

statement:
### B3.9. Fixed-character rows and rectangle cancellation

Call a child exceptional if it satisfies the complementary fixed-inducing predicate above. Before taking absolute values, a nonzero genuine second allocation is disjoint from every old moving support: those primes are common column zeros. Thus no old character at such a prime can cancel a factor supplied by \(G_cV_{\rm id}\). Let \(v_1\) be the radical length of nonunit-partition primes whose common multiplicity is one, and set \(f=2v_1\). At each such prime the fixed row factor \(G_cV_{\rm id}\) has valuation two. Its primitive inducing character has conductor dividing the fixed modulus and is therefore unramified at these good primes. Exceptionality forces
\(v_p(h')\equiv4\pmod6\). More generally, at every good prime it specifies one residue class modulo six, with residue zero outside the frozen moving supports. Unit and \(S\)-valuations contribute finitely many sectors, while their sixth powers remain in the free sixth-power factor. Therefore
\((h')=h_0v^6\) for a fixed sixth-power-free \(h_0\), and \(q_{h_0}\ge Z^{4v_1}=Z^{2f}\). Ideal counting gives the stronger exponent \((m'_{\rm act}-2f)/6\); we need only
\[
\#\{h'\text{ exceptional}:q_{h'}\ll Z^{m'_{\rm act}}\}
\ll Z^{(m'-f)/6+\delta_2/6+o(1)}.
\tag{B3.73}
\]
Below the forced initial norm the range is empty, apart from a fixed endpoint factor. This counts the full fixed-inducing part, including the principal character, and also rows admitted when a former partition restriction is bounded by one. The corresponding source estimates are `chosen_exceptional_block` in `OAI.NumberTheory.DirichletL.Moments.SecondExceptionalFixedQChosenBlock` and `original_exceptional_energy` in `OAI.NumberTheory.DirichletL.Moments.SecondExceptionalFixedQSource`. No saving from the unit set \(t_2\) is used.

After the full Möbius allocation, take the pointwise absolute product on these rows. Absolute volume on side \(j\), with its raw normalizer and live slots, is
\(O(Z^{(\alpha_j-r_j)/2+e_j})\). Together with both extraction scalars and the divisor count, (B3.67) gives paired volume at most
\(Z^{a_0-b_2+2\theta_N+o(1)}\): indeed
\(t_--r_1-r_2\le\omega_2\), and \(r_1\ge0\). Its nominal excess over the inner allowance (B3.64), including (B3.73), is exactly
\[
\frac{m'-f}{6}+a_0-b_2-(M'+\Delta)
=A-\frac56M-F_1-F_2,
\tag{B3.74}
\]
where
\[
\begin{aligned}
F_1&=c/6+5\{d+(K_0-K)\}/6+w/3+\widetilde q/6+w_o+B_c-5g/6+\ell,\\
F_2&=2b_2-5g_2/6-p_2+t_2+V/6+f/6.
\end{aligned}\tag{B3.75}
\]
These expressions obey
\[
F_1\ge\frac23(c+w)-3\sigma-5\delta_1/6,
\qquad F_2\ge\frac23b_2.
\tag{B3.76}
\]
For the first, initially take \(g=J_+,\ell=0\), and put \(D_0=d+K_0-K\). If \(J\ge0\), substitution gives \(F_1=c+2w+\widetilde q/6+w_o/6+B_c\). If \(J<0\), use
\(B_c+\widetilde q/6\ge(3c-5D_0)_+/6-5\delta_1/6\), since \(\widetilde q\ge R\). Hence
\(F_1\ge[c+5D_0+(3c-5D_0)_+]/6+w/3-5\delta_1/6\ge2(c+w)/3-w/3-5\delta_1/6\).
Restoring \(g\le J_++2\sigma\), \(\ell\ge0\), and \(w\le7\sigma/3\) loses less than \(3\sigma\). For the second, the local contributions in units of \(\log_ZP\) are:

| Common case | \(F_2\) | \(b_2\) |
|---|---:|---:|
| \(i=i,6\nmid i\), unit | \(7i/6\) | \(i\) |
| \(i=i,6\nmid i\), nonunit | \((7i-5)/6+\mathbf1_{i=1}/3\) | \(i\) |
| \(i=i,6\mid i\) | \(7i/6-1\) | \(i\) |
| \(i>j_0,6\mid j_0\), unit | \(i+j_0/6-1\) | \((i+j_0)/2\) |

Each first entry is at least two thirds of the second: the only smallest case is \(i=1\) in the second row, where the \(f/6\) contribution makes equality. This proves (B3.76). Consequently (B3.74) is at most \(3\sigma+O(\xi+\theta_N)\) when \(A\le5M/6\). This completes the current uncentered stage and validates its comparisons from §B3.5.

**Masked lattice cancellation.** For a fixed \(\vartheta\in\Theta\), a squarefree mask \(R_*\) of polynomial norm, a fixed annular \(W_i\), and real \(t\), put
\(L_i(X,t)=\sum_l\vartheta(l)\mathbf1_{(l,R_*)=1}q_l^{it}W_i(q_l/X)\). Then, uniformly for \(X>0\),
\[
L_i(X,t)=c_{\vartheta,R_*}X^{1+it}I_i(t)
 +O(Z^{\epsilon_1}\langle t\rangle^J),\qquad |L_i(X,t)|\ll X,
\tag{B3.77}
\]
where \(c_{\vartheta,R_*}\) is independent of \(X,t\), and \(I_i(t)\) is the fixed lattice measure constant times \(\int_0^\infty W_i(y)y^{it}dy\).

To prove it first omit the mask. The primary ideals outside \(S\), with fixed weight \(\vartheta\), form a finite weighted set of classes in a fixed lattice. Poisson for \(q_z^{it}W_i(q_z/X)=X^{it}f_t(z/\sqrt X)\) gives zero-frequency main term \(c_\vartheta X^{1+it}I_i(t)\). Integration by parts on the fixed annulus gives \(|\widehat f_t(\xi)|\ll_J\langle t\rangle^J(1+|\xi|)^{-J}\). For \(X\ge1\), summing nonzero frequencies bounds the error by \(O(\langle t\rangle^J)\) for fixed sufficiently large \(J\); for \(0<X<1\), both the finite lattice sum and main term are \(O(1)\). Insert the mask with
\(L_i(X,t)=\sum_{d\mid R_*}\mu(d)\vartheta(d)q_d^{it}L_i^0(X/q_d,t)\), omitting already excluded primes. Its main coefficient is
\(c_{\vartheta,R_*}=c_\vartheta\sum_{d\mid R_*}\mu(d)\vartheta(d)/q_d\); the two norm powers of \(d\) cancel. The divisor bound gives the stated error. Finally absolute counting on a nonempty annulus is \(O(X)\); below its first possible ideal it is empty. This proves (B3.77).

For \(U_i=X_i/q_{b_i}\), \(V_i=Y_i/q_{b_i}\) and \(T=U_1U_2=V_1V_2\), the sum of (B3.66) is
\(L_1(U_1,t)L_2(U_2,t)-L_1(V_1,t)L_2(V_2,t)\).
Its two main terms agree. If all four scales are at least \(Z^r\), \(r\ge0\), (B3.77) bounds the centrally normalized difference by
\[
O\bigl(Z^{\epsilon_1}\langle t\rangle^{2J}T^{1/2}Z^{-r}\bigr).
\tag{B3.78}
\]
Each one-error term uses one scale at most \(TZ^{-r}\); the two-error term fits because \(1\le TZ^{-r}\). Without a nonnegative lower length the all-scale volume fallback is \(O(T^{1/2})\). This is an equality-of-main-terms argument for the same row, mask and norm power; it would fail for independently modified rectangles.

Apply (B3.78) to the centered exceptional children. Initially all four plain lengths are at least \(L\). Before the final \(t\)-allocation, the two sides have lower lengths at least \(L-c-w-c_2\), \(L-c-w-d_2\). Let
\(r=(L-c-w-\min(c_2,d_2))_+\), and call the side with this saving side one. Its final allocation removes at most \(r_1\) from either plain. If \(r_1<r\), use (B3.78) with saving \(r-r_1\); otherwise use volume. Keep the raw equal-product scales, with no clipping of a signed rectangle. The divisor dyad and both reductions give exactly
\[
t_--r_1-r_2-(r-r_1)_+
=(t_--r_2)-\max(r,r_1)\le\omega_2-r.
\tag{B3.79}
\]
Thus the paired absolute volume improves to \(Z^{a_0-b_2-r+2\theta_N+o(1)}\), uniformly in the live slots. Their labels were absent from the Fourier density; sum them only now by absolute volume, using the exact normalization (B3.67).

Put \(v=c+w+\min(c_2,d_2)\). From (B3.76), \(F_1+F_2\ge2v/3-3\sigma-5\delta_1/6\). The remaining centered exceptional deficit is bounded by
\[
A-5M/6-2v/3-(L-v)_+\le(A-M)_+,
\qquad L=M/4.
\tag{B3.80}
\]
The left side increases for \(v\le L\), decreases for \(v\ge L\), and equals \(A-M\) at \(v=L\). In the positive-slot range \(A\le M\); in the padded zero-slot core \(A\le M+\delta\). The exceptional terminal cost is therefore at most \(3\sigma+\delta\), with its numerical support and frequency errors already reserved. This finishes the centered stage.
title: B3.9. Fixed-character rows and rectangle cancellation

statement:
### A.3. Local Euler factors

At \(\mathfrak p\notin S\), put

\[
Q=q_{\mathfrak p},\quad j=v_{\mathfrak p}(u)\in\{0,\ldots,5\},\quad
\rho=\chi_{\mathfrak p}(u/\mathfrak p^j),
\]

\[
a_{\mathfrak p}=\overline{\alpha(\mathfrak p)}^3\eta(\mathfrak p)^3,
\quad b_{\mathfrak p}=\overline{\alpha(\mathfrak p)}^2\eta(\mathfrak p)^2
\overline{\chi_{\mathfrak p}(4)},\quad b_{\mathfrak p}^3=a_{\mathfrak p}^2,
\]

\[
V=Q^{-6z},\quad R=a_{\mathfrak p}^2Q^{4-6s-6z},\quad
W^\circ=\rho Q^{-w},\quad
W=\chi_{\mathfrak p}(u)Q^{-w},\quad
D=\eta(\mathfrak p)\overline{\chi_{\mathfrak p}(u)}Q^{-s}.
\tag{A.8}
\]

In particular \(W=D=0\) when \(j>0\), whereas \(W^\circ\) retains its unit phase. The marked and full local series are

\[
P_{\mathfrak p}^*=\frac1{1-R}
\left\{\frac{R(1-Q^{-1})-\eta(\mathfrak p)(Q-1)Q^{-s-w}V^{\mathbf1_{j\le1}}}{1-V}+J_j\right\},
\]

\[
P_{\mathfrak p}=\frac1{1-V}+\mathbf1_{j=0}\frac{W^\circ}{1-W^\circ}+P_{\mathfrak p}^*,
\qquad
H_{\mathfrak p}=P_{\mathfrak p}\frac{(1-V)(1-W)}{1-D},
\quad H_{\eta,u}=\prod_{\mathfrak p\notin S}H_{\mathfrak p},
\tag{A.9}
\]

with

| \(j\) | \(J_j\) |
|---:|:---|
| 0 | \(-\eta(\mathfrak p)\rho^{-1}Q^{-s}+W^\circ R\) |
| 1 | \(\eta(\mathfrak p)Q^{-s-w}\) |
| 2 | \(a_{\mathfrak p}\rho^{-3}Q^{3/2-3s}\) |
| 3 | \(-\eta(\mathfrak p)b_{\mathfrak p}\rho^{-2}Q^{2-3s-w}+b_{\mathfrak p}^2\rho^{-4}Q^{2-4s}\) |
| 4 | \(-\eta(\mathfrak p)a_{\mathfrak p}\rho^{-3}Q^{5/2-4s-w}\) |
| 5 | \(-a_{\mathfrak p}^2Q^{3-6s}\) |

Here \(V^{\mathbf1_{j\le1}}=V\) for \(j=0,1\), and equals one otherwise.

Writing \(a_p,b_p,\rho,R,V,W^\circ\) as in (A.8), the local series is therefore
\[
\begin{aligned}
P_p=\sum_{\substack{e_0=0,1\\l,k,m\ge0}}
&(-1)^{e_0}\gamma_1(p)^{-e_0}\eta(p)^{e_0}
\bigl(a_p\overline{\gamma_3(p)}\bigr)^l
\rho^{k-t}\epsilon_p^{tk-e_0l-l(l-1)/2}\\
&\times C_p(t,k,j+6m)
Q^{-(s+1/2)e_0-(1+3s)l-wk-6zm},\qquad t=e_0+3l.
\end{aligned}
\tag{A.10}
\]

The marked series restricts the restored sum to \(t>0\). Its four families and the allowed frequencies are
\[
\begin{array}{c|cc}
 t&k=0&k=1\\\hline
 6r+6&j'\ge t-1&j'=t\\
 6r+1&j'=t-1&j'\ge t\\
 6r+3&j'=t-1&j'=t\\
 6r+4&j'=t-1&j'=t
\end{array}\qquad r\ge0.
\tag{A.11}
\]
This follows by lifting a residue modulo \(p\): a nonprincipal Gauss sum is supported at valuation exactly \(t-1\), while a principal one has its negative boundary there and its value \(Q^t-Q^{t-1}\) at larger valuations. In (A.7), these conditions apply to exponents \(t\) for \(k=0\) and \(t-1\) for \(k=1\).

Insert \(j'=j+6m\). Increasing \(r\) and the first allowed \(m\) together by one multiplies a term by \(R\); increasing \(m\) further gives \(V\). The two strict-inequality tails are therefore
\[
 \frac{R(1-Q^{-1})}{(1-R)(1-V)},\qquad
 -\frac{\eta(p)(Q-1)Q^{-s-w}V^{\mathbf1_{j\le1}}}{(1-R)(1-V)}.
\]
The second tail begins at \(m=r+1\) for \(j\le1\), and at \(m=r\) otherwise. The equality cases give the six \(J_j\) in (A.9), using (A.1). For example \(j=2\) comes from \((t,k,m)=(3,0,0)\); \(j=3\) comes from \((3,1,0)\) and \((4,0,0)\). In the restored summand the cube phase is \(\overline{\gamma_3(p)}\), not \(\gamma_3(p)\); \(\gamma_3(p)^2=\chi_p(-1)\) keeps the parity factor explicit.

For \(t=0\), the \(k=0\) terms give \((1-V)^{-1}\); the \(k>0\) terms require \(j=m=0\) and give \(W^\circ/(1-W^\circ)\). This proves (A.9) in every valuation, including shared primes. Factoring out \((1-V)^{-1}\), \((1-W)^{-1}\), and \(1-D\) gives
\[
 \mathcal F_{\eta,u}(s,w,z)=
 \frac{\zeta_K^S(6z)L_K^S(w,\psi_u)}{L_K^S(s,\eta\overline{\psi_u})}
 H_{\eta,u}(s,w,z).
\]
Together with §A.2 this proves (2.8). ∎
title: A.3. Local Euler factors

    (e : ℝ) (he : 0<e) (he' : e<1/1000)

statement:
### D.6. Exceptional children

At every prime outside the fixed support, membership of the child inducing character in \(\Theta\) prescribes the valuation of \(h'\) modulo six. Hence its ideal is \(h_0v^6\) for one fixed sixth-power-free \(h_0\). Let \(v_1\) be the radical length of the nonunit primes of common multiplicity exactly one, and put \(f=2v_1\). At such a prime the fixed row factor has valuation two, so exceptionality requires \(v_p(h')\equiv4\pmod6\). The old moving support cannot meet this genuine common support, because its old zero would have killed the allocation. Thus \(q_{h_0}\ge Z^{4v_1}\), and the deliberately weaker sufficient count is

\[
\#\{h'\text{ exceptional}\}\ll Z^{(m'-f)/6+\epsilon}.
\tag{D.23}
\]

This includes all members of \(\Theta\) and rows added by positive enlargement; if the forced \(h_0\) does not fit, the range is empty.

After summing (D.22), absolute volume of the paired normalized residual convolutions is \(\ll Z^{a_0-b_2+\epsilon}\). The exact excess of this volume and (D.23) over (D.21) is

\[
\frac{m'-f}{6}+a_0-b_2-(M'+\Delta_{\rm child})
=A-\frac56M-F_1-F_2,
\tag{D.24}
\]

where

\[
F_1=\frac c6+\frac{5D_0}{6}+\frac{\widetilde q}{6}+B_c-\frac{5g}{6},
\]

\[
F_2=2b_2-\frac56g_2-p_2+t_2+\frac V6+\frac f6.
\tag{D.25}
\]

There are the two local lower bounds

\[
F_1\ge\frac23c-\frac56\sigma-O(\xi),\qquad F_2\ge\frac23b_2.
\tag{D.26}
\]

For \(F_1\), if \(D_0\ge c\), substitute \(g=D_0-c+\sigma\) to obtain
\(c+\widetilde q/6+B_c-5\sigma/6\). Otherwise use
\(\widetilde q+6B_c\ge(3c-5D_0)_+-O(\xi)\), since \(\widetilde q\ge R\). Then
\(c+5D_0+(3c-5D_0)_+\ge4c\).

For \(F_2\), the local contributions, in units of \(\log_ZP\), are:

| Common multiplicities and divided frequency | \(F_2\) | \(b_2\) |
|---|---:|---:|
| \(i=i,\ 6\nmid i\), unit | \(7i/6\) | \(i\) |
| \(i=i,\ 6\nmid i\), nonunit | \((7i-5)/6+\frac13\mathbf1_{i=1}\) | \(i\) |
| \(i=i,\ 6\mid i\) | \(7i/6-1\) | \(i\) |
| \(i>j,\ 6\mid j\), unit | \(i+j/6-1\) | \((i+j)/2\) |

Every entry in the middle column is at least two thirds of the last; the nonunit multiplicity-one case gives equality. These are exactly the local cases from (A.17)–(A.18).

If \(A\le5M/6\), (D.24)–(D.26) already finish the exceptional contribution, up to the small terminal loss \(5\sigma/6+O(\xi)\). This proves the uncentered stage before its use in the comparison.

For the centered stage, the common-character calculation gives, on an exceptional row, a coefficient of the form

\[
\vartheta(l_1)\vartheta(l_2)\mathbf1_{(l_1l_2,R_*)=1}q_{l_1l_2}^{it}\mathcal D_b(l_1,l_2).
\tag{D.27}
\]

The mask includes all redundant natural zeros and is common to the two factors and both rectangles. Before the last divisor extraction, at least one of the paired sides has all four formal plain scales at least

\[
Z^{L-c-\min(c_2,d_2)}.
\]

Put \(r=(L-c-\min(c_2,d_2))_+\). If this side's final extracted total is \(r_1<r\), use (D.2) to save \(Z^{-(r-r_1)}\). If \(r_1\ge r\), use volume. Together with the divisor count, the exact inequality

\[
t_--r_1-r_2-(r-r_1)_+\le-r
\tag{D.28}
\]

shows that the paired normalized products, after all these divisor allocations, are bounded by
\(Z^{a_0-b_2-r+\epsilon}\). Taking triangle before the full divisor sum would lose this saving.

With \(v=c+\min(c_2,d_2)\) and \(b_2\ge\min(c_2,d_2)\), the remaining deficit is at most

\[
A-\frac56M-\frac23v-(L-v)_++\frac56\sigma+O(\xi)
\le A-M+\frac56\sigma+O(\xi).
\tag{D.29}
\]

The maximum of the left-hand piece in \(v\ge0\) is at \(v=L=M/4\). The padded core has \(A\le M+2\xi\), so only a small terminal loss remains. This completes the centered stage.
title: D.6. Exceptional children

theorem finite_actual_pair_le_energy {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    (rows : Finset FreeRow) (η : Character) (Q : Ideal O)
    (Φ : 𝓢(ℝ,ℂ)) (U bΦ δ : ℝ) (hU : 1 ≤ U) (hδ : 0 ≤ δ)
    (hs : Function.support (Φ:ℝ→ℂ) ⊆ Set.Iic bΦ) (hp : ∀x, 0 ≤ (Φ x).re)
    (hη : (η.modulus.absNorm:ℝ) ≤ U^δ)
    (hrows : ∀u∈rows, rowNorm u ≤ U)
    (hkeep : ∀u∈rows, weighted_initialKeep η Q u.val)
    (hone : ∀x∈Set.Icc (0:ℝ) 1, Φ x = 1)
    (W₁ W₂ : ℝ → ℂ) (b₁ b₂ X₁ X₂ : ℝ)
    (hs₁ : Function.support W₁ ⊆ Set.Iic b₁) (hs₂ : Function.support W₂ ⊆ Set.Iic b₂)
    (hX₁ : 0 < X₁) (hX₂ : 0 < X₂)
    (slots : ι → Finset (Ideal O)) (β : ι → Ideal O → ℂ) (P : ι → ℝ)
    (hP : ∀i, 0 < P i) :
    (∑u∈rows, ‖polynomial ((momentData η).character (momentElement u)) false W₁ X₁ 0 0 *
      polynomial ((momentData η).character (momentElement u)) false W₂ X₂ 0 0 *
        ∏i, normalizedSlot η rowMaskElement 1 u.val (slots i) (β i) 0 (P i)‖^2)
      ≤ energy η (fixedBadMask*ConcretePrimeRowBridge.idealGenerator 1) 1 0 W₁ W₂
        slots β P X₁ X₂ (weighted_initialKeep η Q) Φ U
title: finite_actual_pair_le_energy

theorem selected_integral_normalized_epsilon
    (W0 W1 : ℝ→ℂ) (a0 b0 a1 b1 B : ℝ)
    (ha0 : 0<a0) (ha1 : 0<a1) (hab1 : a1<b1) (hB : 0≤B)
    (hW0 : Function.support W0⊆Set.Icc a0 b0)
    (hW1 : Function.support W1⊆Set.Icc a1 b1)
    (hW0s : ContDiff ℝ ∞ W0) (hW1s : ContDiff ℝ ∞ W1)
    (hWB : ∀x,‖W1 x‖≤B)
    (aCut bCut : ℝ) (haCut : 0<aCut) (hbCut : 0<bCut)
    (η : HeckeFamily.Character) (S : Finset Id) (hS : ∀P∈S,P.IsMaximal)
    (hbad : fixedBadPrimes⊆S) (K : ℕ) (ε : ℝ) (hε : 0<ε) :
    ∃ degree : ℕ, ∃ C Z₀ : ℝ, 0<C ∧ 1<Z₀ ∧
    ∀ (Z shift : ℝ), Z₀≤Z → |shift|≤min (1/2) (ε/1000) →
    ∀ (T : Fin K→Finset PrimeIdeal), (∀i P,P∈T i→Supported P.val) →
      (∀i P,P∈T i→P.val∉S) → Pairwise (fun i j=>Disjoint (T i) (T j)) →
    ∀ (J : Finset (Fin K)) (H : SelectedSlot J→ℝ),
      (∀i,1≤H i) → (∀i P,P∈T i.val→(Ideal.absNorm P.val:ℝ)≤H i) →
      (∏i,H i)≤Z^z →
    ∀ (W : Fin K→ℝ→ℂ), (∀i x,‖W i x‖≤1) → ∀ (P : Fin K→ℝ) (t : ℝ),
      (Real.sqrt (lowPhysicalScale (calibrationForSet S hS) (Z^(13/33:ℝ)) (Z^(15/33:ℝ))))⁻¹/(2*Real.pi)*
      ‖∫v : ℝ,lowSeparatedIntegrand (calibrationForSet S hS) W0 W1
        (lowOuterCutoff aCut bCut) (Z^(13/33:ℝ)) (Z^(15/33:ℝ))
        (lowSelectedInverseRow Finset.univ
          (lowSelectedWeight η (fun i=>canonicalSlotSupport (T i)) J W P t)
          η S hS (lowSelectedIdeal (fun i=>canonicalSlotSupport (T i)) J)
          (Z^(Nstar+shift)) t) v‖ ≤
      C*(1+‖t‖)^degree*Z^(20/99+ε:ℝ)

statement:
theorem plain_capacity_comparison {δ x Δ t r m γ : ℝ}
    (hδ : 0≤δ) (hδ' : δ≤5/6) (hx : 0≤x) (hx' : x≤1/2)

theorem actual_nonfloor_cube_arithmetic (N n : ℕ) (e eps c b A R dmin dmax rmin τ ε κ cost mesh margin loss : ℝ)
    (he : 0 < e) (he1 : e<1/1000) (heps : 0 < eps) (hc : 0 < c) (hcb : c≤b) (hA : 0≤A)
    (hR : 0≤R) (hdmin : 0 < dmin) (hdmax : 0≤dmax) (hdRange : dmin≤dmax) (hrmin : 0 < rmin)
    (hτ : 0<τ) (hε : 0<ε) (hκ : 0<κ) (hcost : 0≤cost) (hmesh : 0 < mesh)
    (hbudget : 8*e*R+κ≤ε) (hgap : ε < rmin*mesh) (hmargin : 0 < margin)
    (hheight : 2*τ < dmin*cost) (hloss : τ*(2+4*eps) < loss)
    (S : Finset (Ideal O)) (hS : SourceExclusions S) (hfirst : FirstTail (4*e) S)
    (hmax : ∀P∈S,P.IsMaximal)
    (ell : Fin N→ℝ) (hell : Function.Injective ell)
    (hello : ∀j,dmax*rmin≤ell j) (hellhi : ∀j,ell j≤dmin*R)
    (W : Fin N→ℝ→ℂ)
    (hWs : ∀j,Function.support (W j)⊆Ioo c b) (hW : ∀j,ContDiff ℝ ∞ (W j)) (hWB : ∀j t,‖W j t‖≤A)
    (hellsum : ∑j,ell j=Cycle25.ell)
    (hdtop : dmax≤37/42) (hε1 : ε≤1/1000) (hκ1 : κ≤1)
    (hτzero : τ < dmin/2) (hτheight : 4*τ < dmin*cost)
    (hwbudget : 12*e*((22:ℝ)+2)+8*κ+2*cost≤ε/2)
    (φ : ℝ→ℝ) (hφ : ContDiff ℝ ∞ φ) (hφc : HasCompactSupport φ)
    (hφp : tsupport φ⊆Ioi 0) (hφ0 : ∀y,0≤φ y) (hφne : φ≠0)
    (a₀ b₀ B₀ : ℝ) (ha₀ : 0 < a₀) (hab₀ : a₀≤b₀) (hB₀ : 0 < B₀)
    (hφs : Function.support φ⊆Ioo a₀ b₀) (hφB : ∀y,φ y≤B₀)
    (εm ν logCost heightCost momentCost : ℝ)
    (hεm : 0<εm) (hν : 0<ν)
    (hlog : 0 < logCost) (hMomentHeight : τ < heightCost)
    (μ : ℝ)
    (hfinal : (159*ε+εm+R+7*ν)+(12*e+eps*(N+8))+
      (logCost+heightCost+momentCost+loss+mesh*Cycle25.ell+(16-6*Cycle25.ly)*e)+μ≤1/4000) (counts : CountParameters M H εm) :
    ∃C : ℝ,0 < C ∧
    ∀η : Character,∀ᶠZ : ℝ in atTop,
      ∀d : ℝ,dmin≤d → d≤dmax → ∀(v a C0 : ℝ),0≤v → v≤d → d-v≤μ →
      51/100 < a → a≤7/8 → Cycle25.Transport.OriginalBranch d a → 0≤C0 → ∀rows : Finset FreeRow,
      (∀u∈rows,u.val≠1 ∧ Z^(1/100:ℝ)≤rowNorm u ∧
        (calibrationForSet S hmax).residueMonoid u.val≠0 ∧ rowNorm u≤Z^(d-margin)) →
      (∀u∈rows,Z^v≤rowNorm u ∧ rowNorm u≤2*Z^v) →
      ∀i : ℕ,i≤n →
      (∀u∈rows,detectorMaximum (sourceDetectorFamily S hS.prime η u (rayCubeFamily M H hH u))
        (3*(i+1:ℕ)*Z^τ) < a+2*e) →
      (∀u∈rows,a≤detectorMaximum (sourceDetectorFamily S hS.prime η u (rayCubeFamily M H hH u))
        ((3*i:ℕ)*Z^τ)) →
      let Y : Fin N→ℝ

    ∃C : ℝ,0≤C ∧ ∀(η : Character) (u : FreeRow),u.val≠1 →
      ∀(P : Fin K→PrimeIdeal),Function.Injective P → ∀hPS : ∀j,(P j).val∉S,
      ∀ψ : ι→Character,∀Z : ℝ,1≤Z →
      ((Ideal.span {u.val}:Ideal O).absNorm:ℝ)≤Z^(QRH.h+ζ) →
      ∀length : Fin K→ℝ,(∑j,length j)=QRH.ell →
      (∀j,((P j).val.absNorm:ℝ)≤b*Z^(length j)) →
      ∀a B H : ℝ,∀i : ℕ,(51/100:ℝ)≤a → a≤1 → 2<B → Z^τ≤H → H≤(3*i+2:ℕ)*B →

        centralCubeIntegral S hS hmax P hPS η u W0 W1 (Z^QRH.lx) (Z^QRH.ly) Z a e H‖≤

statement:
theorem exists_optimized_nonfloor_cube_bound_with_parameters (gap:ℝ) (hgap:0<gap)
    (hgap1:gap≤(1-QRH.kappa0)/2)
    (hκbeta:2*HeckeZeroSupremum.beta-1≤QRH.kappa0+2*gap)
    (hbeta:(51/100:ℝ)≤HeckeZeroSupremum.beta):
    ∃D:Parameters.HighData gap,∃S:SourceData D,∃τ:ℝ,0<τ ∧
    τ<(1/200:ℝ)/2 ∧ 4*τ<(1/200:ℝ)*D.cost ∧
    D.t<gap/100 ∧ 2000*D.ε≤D.t ∧ 2000*D.e≤D.t ∧
    ((D.N:ℝ)+8)*D.eps≤D.t ∧
    (∀j,QRHParameters.optimizedLengths D j≤D.t/200) ∧ τ*(2+4*D.eps)<D.t ∧
    ∀n:ℕ,∀η:Character,∃C:ℝ,0<C ∧ ∀ᶠZ:ℝ in atTop,1<Z ∧
    ∀d:ℝ,(1/200:ℝ)≤d→d≤7/8→∀(v a:ℝ)(i:ℕ),i≤n→
      0≤v→v≤QRH.h+D.t→d-v≤2*D.t→51/100<a→a≤1→

statement:
\begin{lemma}[Fourth moment with short prime factors]\label{lem:plain}
Let \(13/18\le\kappa\le1\).  Let \(n_1,n_2\ge0\), and let
\(Q=\prod_{i\in\mathcal I}Q_{\psi_k,i}\), where
\[
 Q_{\psi_k,i}=P_i^{-1/2}\sum_{p\ {\rm prime}}
       \psi_k(p)\nu_i(p)W_i^{\rm slot}(q_p/P_i),\qquad P_i=Z^{z_i},
\]
be a finite product of prime polynomials of lengths
\(z_i\ge0\) and total length \(z=\sum_{i\in\mathcal I}z_i\).
Their underlying prime supports are pairwise disjoint before common
masks and row zero extensions are imposed.  Their coefficients are
fixed finite linear combinations of finite-ray characters.  For every
positive-length slot the expansion has the form
\[
 \nu_i(n)=\sum_{j=1}^{J_i}c_{ij}\vartheta_{ij}(n),
 \qquad \vartheta_{ij}\in\Theta,
\]
where the finite list and its coefficients are fixed independently of
\(Z\) and of the row.  The row and mask hypotheses are those just stated.

For every \(\epsilon>0\), there is a slot mesh \(\eta>0\) such that,
if \(z_i\le\eta\) for every \(i\), then
\begin{equation}
 \sum_{k\in\mathcal R_z}
 \left|S_{\psi_k}(n_1;W_1)S_{\psi_k}(n_2;W_2)Q\right|^2
 \ll Z^{M+\epsilon}
 \label{old-eq:2.1}
\end{equation}
in either of the following cases:
\begin{enumerate}
\item \(z=0\).  There is no restriction on the bounded nonnegative
      lengths \(n_1,n_2\), and no lower bound on the conductor.
\item \(z>0\) and
\begin{equation}
 n_1+n_2+6\kappa z=A+(6\kappa-1)z\le M.
 \label{old-eq:3.9}
\end{equation}
      If \(\kappa<1\), assume in addition that
      \(\beta_*\le(1+\kappa)/2\).  If \(\kappa=1\), no zero-free
      hypothesis is required.
\end{enumerate}
For an empty slot list, \(Q=1\).  If \(z=0\) and the list contains
zero-length slots, their scales are bounded and absolute counting
absorbs them into the constant; the zero-slot assertion therefore
has the same strength.  All real length parameters range over prescribed bounded
sets.  The mesh depends only on those sets and \(\epsilon\), uniformly
for \(\kappa\in[13/18,1]\).  For each fixed \(Z\)-independent arithmetic
datum \(\mathcal A\) and fixed slot count, the bound uses finitely many
smooth seminorms and a fixed polynomial in the separated norm-twist
heights.  Their orders, and the bound itself, are uniform over all
moving moduli, admissible masks, and frozen outer labels in the stated
ranges.
\end{lemma}
title: lem:plain

statement:
theorem large_physical_dyad_bound (K : ℕ) (δ a b B r : ℝ)
    (hδ : 0<δ) (hδ' : δ≤1) (hr : (17/50:ℝ)≤r)
    (ha : 0 < a) (hb : 0 < b) (hB : 0≤B)
    (S : Finset (Ideal O)) (hS : SourceExclusions S) (hmax : ∀P∈S,P.IsMaximal)
    (hfirst : FirstTail (1/4) S)
    (W0 W1 : SchwartzMap ℝ ℂ) (a0 b0 a1 b1 : ℝ) (ha0 : 0 < a0) (ha1 : 0 < a1)
    (hW0 : Function.support W0⊆Icc a0 b0) (hW1 : Function.support W1⊆Icc a1 b1) :
    ∃C : ℝ,0 < C ∧ ∀(η : Character) (Z U : ℝ),1≤Z → 1≤U →
      ∀R : Finset FreeRow,
      (∀u∈R,u.val≠1 ∧ U≤((Ideal.span {u.val}:Ideal O).absNorm:ℝ) ∧
        ((Ideal.span {u.val}:Ideal O).absNorm:ℝ)≤2*U) →
      ∀(T : Fin K→Finset ProbePhysical.PrimeIdeal) (hT : ∀i P,P∈T i→P.val∉S),
      (∀P:(∀i,T i),Function.Injective (fun i=>(P i).val)) →
      ∀length : Fin K→ℝ,(∀i,0≤length i) → (∑i,length i)=(Cycle25.ell:ℝ) →
      ∀W : Fin K→ℝ→ℂ,(∀i,Function.support (W i)⊆Icc a b) → (∀i y,‖W i y‖≤B) →
      absolutePhysicalDyadIntegral S hS hmax η R T hT W (fun i=>Z^(length i)) W0 W1
        (Z^(Cycle25.lx:ℝ)) (Z^(Cycle25.ly:ℝ)) Z 2 2 r
      ≤C*(η.modulus.absNorm:ℝ)^δ*Z^((1+Cycle25.lx/2+Cycle25.ly)+(Cycle25.h:ℝ)*r)*U^(8/5+δ-r)
title: large_physical_dyad_bound

statement:
### Section 10: Nonprincipal comparison

The contour path remains in the stated Euler region, first with global reciprocal control and then inside the buffered rectangle.

Amplitude subdivisions are made only after the original fixed-bin expression has been continued. The proof does not analytically continue row sets defined by pointwise inequalities.

The exponent
\[
E(d;\delta,q,R)
\]
matches the outside powers, row count, reflected numerator, and central slot normalizations.

The small-row argument includes nonidentity unit rows. The statement that only \(u=1\) has a principal numerator is supported by the Kummer-character argument, not by ignoring units.

The large-row estimate is an actual summable infinite tail. The very large fixed value of \(z_\infty\) changes constants and required smooth orders, but not the logical order of choices.
title: Section 10: Nonprincipal comparison

def FullWCellsAt {Δ : ℝ} (D : WeightedQRH.HighParameters.HighData Δ)
    (F : WeightedSourceData D.toMomentData) (η : Character)
    (Z τ : ℝ) (n : ℕ) (weightedC C0 : ℝ) : Prop :=
  letI : NeZero (∏P∈F.S,P) := ⟨fixedPrimeProduct_ne_zero F.S F.exclusions.prime⟩
  ∀idx grid : FreeRow→ℕ,
    let rows := supportedNonfloorRows F.S F.maximal
      (rowBand (Z^(1/100:ℝ)) (Z^((1587/2000:ℝ)+D.t))) grid
    (∀u∈rows,idx u ≤ n ∧ grid u ≤ ⌊(49/100:ℝ)/D.e⌋₊ ∧
      (51/100:ℝ)+D.e*grid u ≤ 7/8) →
    (∀u∈rows,detectorMaximum
      (sourceDetectorFamily F.S F.exclusions.prime η u (rayCubeFamily F.modulus ⊤ le_top u))
      (3*(idx u+1:ℕ)*Z^τ) < 51/100+D.e*grid u+2*D.e) →
    (∀u∈rows,(51/100:ℝ)+D.e*grid u ≤ detectorMaximum
      (sourceDetectorFamily F.S F.exclusions.prime η u (rayCubeFamily F.modulus ⊤ le_top u))
      ((3*idx u:ℕ)*Z^τ)) →
    ∀k∈smallDyadicIndices (Z^(1587/2000+D.t)),
    ∀i∈Finset.range (n+1),∀j∈Finset.range (⌊(49/100:ℝ)/D.e⌋₊+1),
      let rows' := cubeBinRows (rows∩dyadicRows 1 k) idx grid i j
      let Y : Fin D.N→ℝ := fun j=>Z^(D.ell j)
      let T := fun j=>pool (RayQuotient.identityClass F.modulus ⊤) F.S 1 2 (Y j)
      let hT := nonfloorPoolOutside F.modulus ⊤ F.S D.N 1 2 Y
      let normer := sourceResidueConstant F.W F.W (∏P∈F.S,P)*
        (Probe.principalScalar Finset.univ Z (167/1000)
          (slotMass T (residueWeights (fun _=>F.w) Y)) : ℂ)
      rows'.Nonempty → (1/2:ℝ) < sourceDyadConductor Z D.t k →
      (1/3:ℝ) < 2*(51/100+D.e*j)-1 →
      sourceDyadConductor Z D.t k ≤ WeightedQRH.h+WeightedQRH.rowExtension →
      ‖WeightedQRH.FullWContour.finiteCentralFullWRows F.S F.exclusions F.maximal η rows' T hT
          (fun _ y=>(F.w y:ℂ)) Y F.W F.W (Z^(747/2000:ℝ)) (Z^(919/2000:ℝ)) Z D.e
          (fun _=>51/100+D.e*j) (fun _=>(3*i+1:ℕ)*Z^τ)/normer‖ ≤
        weightedC*C0*(η.modulus.absNorm:ℝ)^(2*D.eps)*
          Z^(WeightedQRH.signal WeightedQRH.theta-1/40000+D.t/8)

end SevenEighths.WeightedHighFinalAssembly
end
end OAI
title: FullWCellsAt

statement:
structure SlotBounds (S : Finset κ) (T : κ → Finset ι) (w Q : κ → ι → ℝ)
    (A η : κ → ι → ℂ) (P : ℝ) : Prop where
  lower : 480 ≤ P
  small : 1440 * P ^ (-(87/100 : ℝ)) ≤ 1
  weight_nonneg : ∀ j ∈ S, ∀ p ∈ T j, 0 ≤ w j p
  norm_lower : ∀ j ∈ S, ∀ p ∈ T j, P ≤ Q j p
  phase_bound : ∀ j ∈ S, ∀ p ∈ T j, ‖A j p‖ ≤ 1
  target_unit : ∀ j ∈ S, ∀ p ∈ T j, ‖η j p‖ = 1
  mass_pos : ∀ j ∈ S, 0 < slotMass T w j

section
variable (S : Finset κ) (T : κ → Finset ι) (w Q : κ → ι → ℝ) (A η : κ → ι → ℂ) {P : ℝ} (h : SlotBounds S T w Q A η P)
include S T w Q A η P h



section
variable {s : ℂ} (hs : 87/100 ≤ s.re)
include s hs
title: SlotBounds

statement:
theorem low_completed_fiber_energy_optimized (Q : Ideal Eis) (hQ : Q≠0)
    (F : Ideal Eis) (hF : Squarefree F) (m : Eis) (hm : m≠0)
    (hmLam : ConcretePrimeRowBridge.goodLambda∣m) (hm2 : (2:Eis)∣m)
    (hperiod : Q*Ideal.span {(72:Eis)}∣Ideal.span {m})
    (hbad : ∀ P∈fixedBadPrimes,P∣Ideal.span {m}*F)
    (lo hi : ℝ) (hlo : 0<lo)
    (W : ℝ→ℂ) (hWs : Function.support W⊆Set.Icc lo hi) (hW : ContDiff ℝ ∞ W)
    (Ck η : ℝ) (hCk : 0<Ck) (hη : 0<η) (hη1 : η≤1) (rmax : ℕ) :
    ∃ (degree : ℕ) (C Z₀ : ℝ),0<C ∧ 1<Z₀ ∧
    ∀ {σ : Type v} [Fintype σ] [DecidableEq σ],∀ (J : Ideal Eis) (_hJ : J≠0)
      (Z d ell0 shift : ℝ), Z₀≤Z → 0≤d → d≤QRH.ell → 0≤ell0 → ell0≤QRH.ell-d+η → |shift|≤η →
      (Ideal.absNorm J:ℝ)≤Ck*Z^(QRH.M-2*d) →
    ∀ (parents : Finset (Ideal Eis)),(∀ I∈parents,I≠0 ∧ (Ideal.absNorm I:ℝ)≤Ck*Z^(QRH.M-2*d)) →
      Fintype.card σ≤rmax → ∀ (lists : σ→Finset (Ideal Eis)) (H : σ→ℝ),
      Pairwise (fun i j => Disjoint (lists i) (lists j)) →
      (∀ i,∀ P∈lists i,P.IsMaximal) →
      (∀ i,∀ P∈lists i,ConcretePrimeRowBridge.goodLambda∉P) →
      (∀ i,∀ P∈lists i,Prime P) →
      (∀ i,∀ P∈lists i,ringChar (Eis⧸P)≠2) →
      (∀ i,∀ P∈lists i,IsCoprime (Q*Ideal.span {(72:Eis)}) P) →
      (∀ i,1≤H i) → (∀ i,∀ P∈lists i,(Ideal.absNorm P:ℝ)≤H i) → (∏ i,H i)≤Z^ell0 →
    ∀ (Ψ : Eis→*ℂ),(∀ n,‖Ψ n‖≤1) → CanonicalCoefficientClass.FactorsModulo Q Ψ →
    ∀ (u : Eisˣ) (θ : ℝ) (w : ∀ i,lists i→ℂ),(∀ i P,‖w i P‖≤1) →
      (∑ I∈representativeRowFiber parents J (Ideal.span {m}*F),
        ‖∑ p : ∀ i,lists i,(∏ i,w i (p i))*markedCompletedT
          (rowTwist Ψ m (ConcretePrimeRowBridge.idealGenerator F)
            (u.val*ConcretePrimeRowBridge.idealGenerator I)) (CompletedHeight.normTwistedSource W θ)
          (Z^(1+ell0+shift)) (fun A => ∏ i,if (p i).val∣A then (1:ℂ) else 0)‖^2)≤
      C*(1+‖θ‖)^degree*Z^((QRH.M-2*d)+QRH.lowPenalty d+506*η)*(Ideal.absNorm (rowPowerfulPart J):ℝ)^(-(1/2:ℝ))
title: low_completed_fiber_energy_optimized

statement:
### D.2. The family closed under both transforms

Moving twists and a common exclusion ideal are needed for closure under the transforms; no selected primes or zero-free hypothesis are used.

Fix bounded nonnegative real ranges for \(m,q,n_1,n_2,B\). A fixed twist within a row sum has the form

\[
\tau(n)=\nu(n)\prod_{p\mid A}\chi_n(p)^{e_p},\qquad \nu\in\Theta,\quad q_{\operatorname{rad}A}\le Z^q,
\]

with every displayed zero retained, even if an exponent is zero modulo six. Reciprocity puts other local residue products in this form. Count all displayed moving support in \(q\). A squarefree puncture \(R\), \(q_R\le Z^B\), is a common exclusion fixed across the row sum and all plain factors. Define

\[
\psi_k(n)=\tau(n)\chi_n(k)\mathbf1_{(n,R)=1},\qquad
S_k(N;W)=N^{-1/2}\sum_n\psi_k(n)W(q_n/N).
\]

**Theorem D.1 (mixed plain moment).** For every fixed \(\epsilon>0\),

\[
\sum_{\substack{0<q_k\le Z^m\\\psi_k^*\ne1}}
 |S_k(Z^{n_1};W_1)S_k(Z^{n_2};W_2)|^2
\ll Z^{m+q+\epsilon}.
\tag{D.3}
\]

There is no lower conductor bound or restriction on \(n_1+n_2\). The bound has factor \(\|W_1\|_{C^J}^2\|W_2\|_{C^J}^2\), with orders uniform in moving supports, punctures and bounded lengths. Real powers and norm-twist heights have the convention of §1.2; a fixed list of Euler or profile derivatives is handled by increasing \(J\). In particular, taking no moving twist and two copies of one polynomial yields

\[
\sum_{\substack{0<q_k\le H\\(\nu\chi_\bullet(k))^*\ne1}}
 |S_k(N;W)|^4\ll H^{1+\epsilon}
\tag{D.4}
\]

for bounded polynomial ranges of \(N\) relative to \(H\).

We descend in the **effective width** \(M=m+q\). Fixed-conductor twists alone would not be closed under the first transform.
title: D.2. The family closed under both transforms

statement:
## Background sources used in B0–B4

The formal development uses [OpenAI/math](https://github.com/openai/math/tree/fd4aeeb2ee4fc729c18d98444fed42fd0529eeeb) at revision `fd4aeeb2ee4fc729c18d98444fed42fd0529eeeb`, and Akash Levy’s [weighted-numerator development](https://github.com/akashlevy/QuasiRiemannTracker/tree/2fd60c0926b66ea18d7436f5ed55250fd006ab5d) at revision `2fd60c0926b66ea18d7436f5ed55250fd006ab5d`. Both upstream attributions and Apache-2.0 notices are retained. The public endpoint module is `Cycle25.Assembly.Final.Endpoint`; the coefficient, reflection, moment and source adapters named above identify the analytic dependencies. The following literature supplies the background and normalization conventions:

* [DR] Alexander Dunn and Maksym Radziwiłł, *Bias in cubic Gauss sums: Patterson's conjecture*, Annals of Mathematics 200 (2024), 967–1057, [arXiv:2109.07463v3](https://arxiv.org/html/2109.07463v3). Only the unconditional theta/cusp material of §5 and Appendix A is used. Its conditional prime asymptotic is not used.
* [GL] Leo Goldmakher and Benoît Louvel, *A quadratic large sieve inequality over number fields*, Math. Proc. Cambridge Philos. Soc. 154 (2013), 193–212, [arXiv:1112.1642v2](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1112.1642v2), Definition 1 and Theorem 1.1. B2 checks the quadratic family and masks; the corresponding sharp canonical sieve is also located in the pinned Lean source.
* [HB] D. R. Heath-Brown, *Kummer's conjecture for cubic Gauss sums*, Israel J. Math. 120 (2000), 97–124, [Theorem 2](https://doi.org/10.1007/s11856-000-1273-y). The squarefree cubic sieve is also stated in DR, Theorem 9.1, and proved in the pinned `CubicSieve/Sharp.lean`.
* [GZ] Peng Gao and Liangyi Zhao, *Moments of quadratic Hecke L-functions of imaginary quadratic number fields*, J. Number Theory 209 (2020), 359–377, [arXiv:1707.00091v3](https://arxiv.org/html/1707.00091v3), equation (1.1), for the ordinary primitive trivial-infinite-type functional equation. The formal proof uses the pinned Hecke primitive reflection declarations.
* [TZ] Jesse Thorner and Asif Zaman, *A unified and improved Chebotarev density theorem*, Algebra & Number Theory 13 (2019), 1039–1068, [arXiv:1803.02823v3](https://arxiv.org/html/1803.02823v3), Theorem 1.1 for the fixed identity extension. Only a fixed-field annular prime-ideal count is needed; no uniformity over growing extensions is invoked.
title: Background sources used in B0–B4

Poonen’s Theorem 5.22 supplies the required continuation and functional equation. The submission specializes the complex-place gamma factor consistently to

\]
The principal regularization is separately handled rather than incorrectly treating the principal \(L\)-function as entire. ([math.mit.edu](https://math.mit.edu/~poonen/786/notes.pdf))

statement:
### Quotient-free selected correction

This is a significant strength of the treatment.

The proof does **not** continue the raw quotient \(P_p^*/P_p\) through possible zeros of \(P_p\). Instead, it defines \(G_p\) and the full selected-tuple correction by expressions without that denominator.

The tuple formula is holomorphic in the required Euler regions. The later factorization into individual slot quotients is used only in the dynamic region where \(H_p\) has separately been shown to be bounded away from zero.

I found no illicit division at an unknown zero in this part.

---

theorem weighted_amplitude_bin {ι : Type*} (s : Finset ι) (S Q P : ι → ℂ)
    (U R total selected epsilon Ccount Cmoment : ℝ)
    (hU : 0 < U) (hc : 1 ≤ Ccount) (hm : 1 ≤ Cmoment)
    (hcard : (s.card : ℝ) ≤ Ccount * U^R)
    (hselected : ∀ i ∈ s, U^selected ≤ ‖Q i‖)
    (hfull : ∀ i ∈ s, ‖P i‖ ≤ U^total)
    (henergy : (∑ i ∈ s, ‖S i‖^4 * ‖Q i‖^2) ≤ Cmoment * U^(1+epsilon)) :
    (∑ i ∈ s, ‖S i * P i‖) ≤
      Ccount * Cmoment * U^(total-selected/2+(3*R+1+epsilon)/4)

statement:
### Section 6: Principal correction and comparison

The extension below \(7/8\) is proved directly from the rational local expressions. The numerical contraction estimate is supported by the ideal-count tail bound.

The argument gives both:

- a holomorphic, nonvanishing \(H_\eta\);
- a nonzero eventual normalizer \(A_T(Z)\) with only logarithmic reciprocal growth.

The prime asymptotic is applied to a fixed ray extension. Deleting the target-dependent finite set changes the starting threshold, not the limiting density.

The contour moves cross only the stated poles at \(w=1\) and \(z=1/6\). The reciprocal target is initially kept to the right of \(B\). The principal target is regularized correctly, and polynomial height bounds are dominated by the three independent decay coordinates.

The resulting three principal error exponents agree with the displayed Mellin powers.

    ∃ J : ℕ, ∃ C : ℝ, 0 < C ∧ ∀ᶠ Z : ℝ in atTop, 1 < Z ∧

      ∀ η : Character, (η.modulus.absNorm : ℝ) ≤ Cfixed * Z ^ q →
      ∀ R : Ideal O, R ≠ 0 → (R.absNorm : ℝ) ≤ Z ^ B →
      ∀ rows : Finset O, (∀ z ∈ rows, z ≠ 0) →
        (∀ z ∈ rows, (naturalPlainCharacter η z).residue ≠ 1) →
        (∀ z ∈ rows, ((Ideal.span {z}).absNorm : ℝ) ≤ Z ^ m) →

statement:
### 2.7 Prior-improvement discussion

Liu’s version 1 was submitted on **October 8, 2026**, and Theorem 21.1 states the all-Hecke/all-Dirichlet bound
\[
\frac{1507-2\sqrt{921}}{1653}.
\]
The manuscript’s comparison with that stated constant is accurate, and its exact checker verifies the claimed rational interval for the difference. No theorem from Liu is needed in the present proof. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.12234v1))

The cited heuristic exploration does label its smaller extrapolated values as heuristic and uses a changed long-row slope. The submission correctly refuses to import that slope change without a new moment estimate. ([github.com](https://github.com/tomoto0/quasi-riemann-hypothesis-7-8-verification/blob/main/reports/improvement_exploration.md))

I did not use any claimed formal-verification result or earlier critic approval to validate an analytic step.

---

    (B C U δ x Δ t r m ε ν γ : ℝ)
    (hC : 0 ≤ C) (hU : 1 ≤ U) (hδ : 0 ≤ δ) (hδ' : δ ≤ 5 / 6)

    (ht : 1 ≤ t) (ht' : t ≤ 3 / 2) (hν : 0 ≤ ν) (hγ : 0 ≤ γ)
    (hleft : t - r - γ ≤ m) (hright : r ≤ t + γ)
    (hI0 : B ≤ C * U ^ (max 1 ((1 + 5 * r) / 6) - δ * r + ε))
    (hP0 : B ≤ C * U ^ (1 - 2 * δ * m + ε))

      (HeckeDetectorRowCount.longExponent δ t) + Δ / 4 + ε + 6 * ν + 5 * γ)

statement:
### 3.1. The two moments and a starting half-plane

For a fixed finite-ray character \(\nu\), let \(\varphi_u=\nu\psi_u^{\pm1}\), with its original zeros, and define
\[
 M_u(D;W)=D^{-1/2}\sum_n\mu(n)\varphi_u(n)W(q_n/D),\qquad
 S_u(N;W)=N^{-1/2}\sum_n\varphi_u(n)W(q_n/N).
\tag{3.1}
\]
We need the following two coefficient-specific estimates:
\[
 \sum_{0<q_u\le H}|M_u(D;W)|^2\ll H(HD)^\varepsilon\|W\|_{C^J}^2,
 \qquad H\ge D^{1+\vartheta},\quad \vartheta>0;
\tag{3.2}
\]
\[
 \sum_{\substack{q_u\asymp U\text{ sixth-power-free}\\\varphi_u^*\ne1}}
 |S_u(U^m;W)|^4\ll U^{1+\varepsilon}\|W\|_{C^J}^4.
\tag{3.3}
\]
Here \(m\ge0\) is bounded and \(\varphi_u^*\) denotes the primitive inducing character. Appendix C proves (3.2), including sixth-power rows; Appendix D proves (3.3) through a mixed moment closed under its transforms. Both have the common-profile uniformity of §1.2, and neither assumes a zero-free boundary.

Sixth-power amplification extends (3.2) to longer inverse polynomials. The exact reconstruction identity is
\[
 M_u(D;W)=\sum_{d\mid\operatorname{rad}(a)}
 \mu(d)\varphi_u(d)q_d^{-1/2}M_{ua^6}(D/q_d;W).
\tag{3.4}
\]
It follows by separating the squarefree column's primes dividing \(a\); it remains valid at shared primes of \(u,a\), because both sides retain their zeros. Its coefficient mass is \(\ll q_a^\varepsilon\). Differentiation in log scale replaces \(W\) by \(-W/2-yW'\). Sobolev and (3.2) therefore give
\[
 \sum_{0<q_v\ll H}\sup_{0<E\le D}|M_v(E;W)|^2\ll H(HD)^\varepsilon,
 \qquad H\ge D^{1+\vartheta}.
\tag{3.5}
\]
There are only \(O(\log(2+D))\) relevant log intervals; subunit scales contain boundedly many columns and eventually none.

For sixth-power-free \(q_u\asymp U\), take \(H=\max(2U,D^{1+\vartheta})\) and average (3.4) over primary \(q_a\le(H/U)^{1/6}\), prime to \(S\). There are \(\gg_S(H/U)^{1/6}\) such ideals. The map \((u,a)\mapsto ua^6\) is injective: valuations modulo six recover \(u\), and the primary generator recovers its unit. Equation (3.5) gives \(\sum^{(6)}|M_u(D)|^2\ll U^{1/6}H^{5/6}(UD)^\varepsilon\). For bounded \(r\), take \(D=U^r\) and then \(\vartheta\) small to obtain
\[
 \sum_{q_u\asymp U}^{(6)}|M_u(U^r;W)|^2
 \ll U^{e(r)+\varepsilon},\qquad e(r)=\max\{1,(1+5r)/6\}.
\tag{3.6}
\]
The same argument at the single row \(u=1\) gives
\[
 \left|\sum_n\mu(n)\nu(n)W(q_n/D)\right|\ll D^{11/12+\varepsilon}.
\tag{3.7}
\]
Its Mellin transform equals \(\widehat W(s)/L_K^S(s,\nu)\) for \(\Re s>1\), and converges holomorphically for \(\Re s>11/12\). A zero \(s_0\) there is impossible: take \(W(y)=y^{-s_0}\phi(y)\) with nonzero nonnegative smooth \(\phi\) on \((1,2)\), so \(\widehat W(s_0)>0\). Consequently
\[
 \tfrac12\le\beta_*\le\tfrac{11}{12}.
\tag{3.8}
\]
Classical nonvanishing on \(\Re s=1\) and absolute Euler convergence cover the remaining right half-plane. No zero or character is assumed to attain \(\beta_*\).
title: 3.1. The two moments and a starting half-plane

statement:
\begin{proposition}\label{central-joint}
Put $z_0=17/50$ and $\delta=2a-1$. Consider central nonprincipal
rows in one retained box of Section~8 of \cite{q30}, at real parts
\[
                  x_r=a+16e,\quad w_r=1-a-6e,\quad z_r=z_0.
\]
Fix an error-slot set $I$ and an amplitude row set at a retained
point. Suppose the row count is at most $C_\eta U^{R+\eps_{\rm cnt}}$
after \eqref{count-loss-budget}--\eqref{count-height-ceiling}, and the mean
main-slot amplitude exponent is $q$, assigning exponent zero to
error slots. The corresponding piece of the full correction satisfies
\begin{equation}\label{joint-bound}
\begin{aligned}
 \sum_u\bigl|L_F^S(w,\chi_\bullet(u))
                    H^{(I)}_{\eta,u,Z}(s,w,z)\bigr|
 \ll_\eta{}&U^{R+\delta/2+\eps_{\rm cnt}+\eps_c}\\
 &\times Z^{\ell(z_0-1/2)+q\ell+\eps_c}
                      (1+T_1)^{A_\eta}.
\end{aligned}
\end{equation}
The central analytic loss $\eps_c$ excludes $\eps_{\rm cnt}$ and
can be made arbitrarily small after the slot system is fixed.
The finite height order $A_\eta$ here includes only the remaining
analytic factors; the count height has already been absorbed into
$\eps_{\rm cnt}$. It does not change with the external tail order. In particular the amplitude term in the general exponent
is $g=q\ell$.
\end{proposition}
title: central-joint

statement:
def SourceBins {e : ℝ} (F : ZetaZeroFree.Analytic.SourceData e) (η : Character)
    (Z τ : ℝ) (n : ℕ) (idx grid : FreeRow→ℕ) : Prop :=
  (∀u,1 ≤ idx u ∧ idx u≤n ∧ grid u≤⌊(49/100:ℝ)/e⌋₊ ∧
    (3*idx u+1:ℕ)*Z^τ+Z^τ/2≤(3*idx u+2:ℕ)*Z^τ) ∧
  (∀u,let a : ℝ := 51/100+e*grid u
    51/100≤a ∧ a≤1 ∧
    a≤detectorMaximum (sourceDetectorFamily F.S F.exclusions.prime η u
      (rayCubeFamily F.modulus ⊤ (by exact le_top) u)) ((3*idx u:ℕ)*Z^τ) ∧
    detectorMaximum (sourceDetectorFamily F.S F.exclusions.prime η u
      (rayCubeFamily F.modulus ⊤ (by exact le_top) u)) ((3*idx u:ℕ)*Z^τ)<a+e ∧
    detectorMaximum (sourceDetectorFamily F.S F.exclusions.prime η u
      (rayCubeFamily F.modulus ⊤ (by exact le_top) u)) ((3*(idx u+1):ℕ)*Z^τ)<a+2*e ∧
    (51/100<a → ∃j s,LFunction (sourceDetectorFamily F.S F.exclusions.prime η u
      (rayCubeFamily F.modulus ⊤ (by exact le_top) u) j) s=0 ∧
      ¬((sourceDetectorFamily F.S F.exclusions.prime η u
        (rayCubeFamily F.modulus ⊤ (by exact le_top) u) j).residue=1 ∧ s=1) ∧
      a≤s.re ∧ s.re<a+e ∧ |s.im|≤(3*idx u:ℕ)*Z^τ))
title: SourceBins

statement:
### 2.1 Goldmakher–Louvel

The cited Definition 1 requires a family of primitive, trivial-infinite-type Hecke characters, a finite reciprocity-class structure, and the primitive-conductor property for products of coprime indices in the same class. Theorem 1.1 then supplies the stated squarefree quadratic large sieve. The manuscript does not merely assume that its symbols fit this framework: its unit adjustment at \(\lambda_3\), conductor calculation, and common-class argument address these hypotheses. statement:
### B3.7. Enlarging a Gauss-row norm

Let \(w\) be a column length extracted from (B3.54), and \(w_o\le w\) the additional moving-radical length, whose squared scalar coefficient is \(Z^{-w_o}\). Put \(a_0=A-c-w\). The allowance (B3.55) for the unweighted remaining norm is
\[
\Lambda_c=a_0+\widetilde q+w_o+w+B_c-s_0+\epsilon_G.
\tag{B3.57}
\]
Define \(J=d-c+(K_0-K)-2w+w_o\), \(J_+=\max(J,0)\). With zero slots take \(w=w_o=0\), \(\ell=0\), and enlarge the row norm to a smooth ball of length \(K+g\), \(g=J_++\sigma\).

With positive slots, put \(\ell_* =\sigma/3\), choose the mesh below \(\sigma/6\), and use the fixed pool
\(\mathcal P=\{p:Z^{\ell_*}/2<q_p\le Z^{\ell_*},\ p\notin S\}\).
The fixed-field prime ideal theorem [TZ, Theorem 1.1, specialized to the identity extension of \(\mathbb K\)] gives \(|\mathcal P|=Z^{\ell_*+o(1)}\). The pool is disjoint from every live slot window once \(Z\) is large. For each \(h\ne0\), omit primes dividing \(h,s\) or frozen supports; only \(O(\log Z)\) are omitted.

For \(p\nmid uh\), the prime-power Gauss identities (B1.13) and CRT give
\[
\mathcal G(p^iu,h)=R(p,u)^i\chi_p(u)^{2i}\mathcal G(p^i,h)\mathcal G(u,h),
\qquad\mathcal G(u,hp^6)=\mathcal G(u,h).
\tag{B3.58}
\]
Replacing \(h\) by \(hp^6\) changes only column valuations \(i=1,6,7\). Allocate their powers to the two plain variables, since the pool is disjoint from the slots, and puncture the residual product at \(p\). The same allocation updates both rectangles. Jensen in the eligible primes and this finite allocation list bounds the original squared value by the average of the amplified squared value and these extracted squared errors. A fixed output \(hp^6\) has boundedly many representations, since all pool primes have norm \(\asymp Z^{\ell_*}\) and the output norm has bounded logarithmic length. Thus the amplified norm gets one density factor \(Z^{-\ell_*+o(1)}\). For it take \(\ell=\ell_*\), \(g=J_++2\sigma\), which contains the new rows because \(6\ell_*=2\sigma\).

The extracted alternatives are exactly:

| Column valuation \(i\) | Squared extraction coefficient | \(w\) | \(w_o\) |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | \(q_p^{-1}\) | \(\ell_p\) | \(\ell_p\) |
| 6 | \((1-q_p^{-1})^2\) | \(6\ell_p\) | 0 |
| 7 | \(q_p^{-1}\) | \(7\ell_p\) | \(\ell_p\) |

Here \(\ell_p=\log_Zq_p\in[\sigma/6,\sigma/3]\). At valuation six the exact zero power \(\chi_p(u)^{12}\) is its already common puncture; retain the fixed phase \(R(p,u)^6\). At valuations one and seven the local character remains displayed and its prime is counted in \(w_o\). Freeze \(p\) for each error, set \(\ell=0,g=J_++\sigma\), and apply the second transform directly, with no further amplification. The normalized average \(|\mathcal P|^{-1}\sum_p\) costs no second prime count. Always
\[
0\le w_o\le w\le7\sigma/3.
\tag{B3.59}
\]
The coefficient remains (B3.51) times \(\mathcal G(u,h)\), including its whole difference, common puncture and \(s\)-divisibility.

Add row zero only when passing to the final smooth ball. Formula (B1.13) gives \(\mathcal G(u,0)=0\) unless \(u\) is a sixth power and \(|\mathcal G(u,0)|\le\sqrt{q_u}\). If \(Y=e^{H_N}Z^{a_0}\) is a nonempty column upper bound and \(s\mid u\), then \(q_s^6\le Y\). Counting \(O(Y^{1/6})\) sixth powers bounds the normalized squared zero row by
\(Z^{-a_0}Y^{4/3+o(1)}\le Z^{a_0-s_0+2\theta_N+o(1)}\), within (B3.57). Zero is never amplified.
title: B3.7. Enlarging a Gauss-row norm

statement:
\begin{lemma}[Logarithmic control]\label{lem:logarithmic-control}
Let $\psi$ be a primitive nonprincipal finite-order Hecke character of
conductor norm $Q$, and put $\mathcal L(s)=L(s,\psi)$.  For the principal
character put $Q=1$ and
$\mathcal L(s)=(s-1)\zeta_F(s)/(s+1)$, with its removable value at one.
Fix $a\in[1/2,1]$ and $0<e<10^{-3}$.  Suppose $\mathcal L$ has no zero in
the open disk of radius $2-a-2e$ centered at $2+it$.  Uniformly on the
closed concentric disk of radius $2-a-6e$,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:disk-control}
 |\mathcal L(s)|+|\mathcal L(s)^{-1}|
 \ll_{e,\epsilon}\{2Q(3+|t|)^2\}^{\epsilon}.
\end{equation}
On the disk of radius $2-a-8e$ one also has
\[
 |\mathcal L'(s)/\mathcal L(s)|\ll_e\log\{2Q(3+|t|)^2\}.
\]
In particular, for every fixed $b\ge\beta_*$ and $v>0$, these bounds hold
on $\Re s\ge b+v$, with constants depending on $v,\epsilon$ (and with the
height of $s$ in place of $t$).  In the principal case the reciprocal bound
passes to $1/\zeta_F$; the upper and logarithmic-derivative bounds are for
the regularized function $\mathcal L$.
\end{lemma}
title: lem:logarithmic-control

statement:
#### B2.4.1. Imported sieves and their domains

For squarefree primary good ideals, the quadratic sieve used here is
\[
\sum_{\substack{a\ {\rm sf}\\q_a\le U}}
\left|\sum_{\substack{b\ {\rm sf}\\q_b\le V}}c_b\chi_a(b)^3\right|^2
\ll_\epsilon(UV)^\epsilon(U+V)\sum_b|c_b|^2.
\tag{B2.24}
\]
Here is the family check needed to apply [GL]. The quadratic symbol at the primary generator of an ideal \((x)\), initially on \(\lambda\)-units, is
\[
\vartheta_a((x))=\epsilon_\lambda(x)^{e(a)}(x/a)_2,\qquad
e(a)=(q_a-1)/2\bmod2,
\]
where \(\epsilon_\lambda\) is the nontrivial character modulo \(\lambda\). The powers of \(\omega\) used to make a generator primary are squares; its sign contributes exactly the displayed \(\lambda\)-character. CRT gives primitive conductor \(a\lambda^{e(a)}\) and trivial infinite type. When \(e(a)=0\), take the primitive inducing character with the \(\lambda\)-factor absent. In a fixed primary square class modulo \(4\), two indices have the same \(e(a)\); for coprime such indices the primitive product character has conductor exactly their product. The established reciprocity factor is a bicharacter of a fixed ray group. These are the three conditions of [GL, Definition 1]; its theorem and transpose duality give (B2.24).

Heath-Brown’s cubic sieve gives
\[
\sum_{\substack{a\ {\rm sf},\,a\equiv1(3)\\q_a\le U}}
\left|\sum_{\substack{b\ {\rm sf},\,b\equiv1(3)\\q_b\le V}}
c_b(b/a)_3\right|^2
\ll_\epsilon(UV)^\epsilon
\{U+V+(UV)^{2/3}\}\sum_b|c_b|^2.
\tag{B2.25}
\]
Squarefreeness is in \(\mathcal O\); squarefree rational norms and an exclusion of rational prime factors are not hypotheses. Conjugation and cubic reciprocity permit the opposite orientation. In either sieve, fixed row restrictions decrease the positive outer sum, and fixed column restrictions are implemented by zero coefficients. A row–column collision mask must first be resolved.
title: B2.4.1. Imported sieves and their domains
