statement:
### B0.4. Exact Euler replacement and principal signal

Write \(\mathscr M(z)=\int_0^\infty\widetilde W_0(r)r^{z-1}dr\) for the radial Fourier Mellin transform. Poisson in the physical row and \(s=t+1-z\) give
\[
I_\eta=\frac1{(2\pi i)^3}\int_{(2)}\int_{(3)}\int_{(3)}
X^{1/2-z}Z^{s+z-1}Y^{w-1}e^{(s+z-1)^2}\mathscr M(z)\widehat W_1(w)
\sum_u^{(6)}q_u^{-z}\overline{\xi(u)}
\frac{\zeta_{\mathbb K}^S(6z)L_{\mathbb K}^S(w,\psi_u)}{L_{\mathbb K}^S(s,\eta\overline\psi_u)}H_{\eta,u}\,dz\,dw\,ds.
\tag{B0.28}
\]
The fixed primitive factor excludes zero frequency. Writing a nonzero frequency as \(ua^6\) gives \(\zeta_{\mathbb K}^S(6z)\); no unit row is discarded.

The complete local table is as follows. For \(p\notin S\), set
\[
Q=q_p,\ j=v_p(u),\ \rho=\chi_p(u/p^j),\
\mathfrak a=\overline{\alpha(p)}^3\eta(p)^3,\
\mathfrak b=\overline{\alpha(p)}^2\eta(p)^2\overline{\chi_p(4)},\quad\mathfrak b^3=\mathfrak a^2,
\]
\[
V=Q^{-6z},\quad R=\mathfrak a^2Q^{4-6s-6z},\quad W^\circ=\rho Q^{-w},
\quad W=\chi_p(u)Q^{-w},\quad D=\eta(p)\overline{\chi_p(u)}Q^{-s}.
\]
In particular \(W=D=0\) if \(j>0\). Then
\[
P_p^*=\frac1{1-R}\left\{\frac{R(1-Q^{-1})-\eta(p)(Q-1)Q^{-s-w}V^{\mathbf1_{j\le1}}}{1-V}+J_j\right\},
\]
\[
P_p=(1-V)^{-1}+\mathbf1_{j=0}W^\circ/(1-W^\circ)+P_p^*,\qquad
H_p=P_p(1-V)(1-W)/(1-D),\quad H_{\eta,u}=\prod_{p\notin S}H_p.
\tag{B0.29}
\]

| \(j\) | \(J_j\) |
|---:|---|
| 0 | \(-\eta(p)\rho^{-1}Q^{-s}+W^\circ R\) |
| 1 | \(\eta(p)Q^{-s-w}\) |
| 2 | \(\mathfrak a\rho^{-3}Q^{3/2-3s}\) |
| 3 | \(-\eta(p)\mathfrak b\rho^{-2}Q^{2-3s-w}+\mathfrak b^2\rho^{-4}Q^{2-4s}\) |
| 4 | \(-\eta(p)\mathfrak a\rho^{-3}Q^{5/2-4s-w}\) |
| 5 | \(-\mathfrak a^2Q^{3-6s}\) |

The exponent \(V^{\mathbf1_{j\le1}}\) is \(V\) at \(j=0,1\), and one otherwise. Appendix B4 derives this table by full-modulus Poisson summation and CRT. For reference, its finite local sum is
\[
C_p(t,k,j')=\sum_{\substack{d\bmod p^k\\p^{j'}\equiv p^td\pmod{p^k}}}
\chi_p(d)^k g_{\chi_p^t}\!\left(p^t,\frac{p^{j'}-p^td}{p^k}\right),\qquad t=e+3l,
\tag{B0.30}
\]
with \(e=0,1\). The appendix evaluates every case, restores the unit phases, and sums the resulting geometric series. The local table therefore includes all shared primes and imprimitive rows.

Set \(c_p=\overline{\eta(p)}Q^s\), \(h_p=Q^{-w}\), and define, without division by \(P_p\) or \(H_p\),
\[
G_p=\frac{(c_p-h_p)(1-V)(1-W)P_p^*-h_p(1-VW)}{1-D}.
\tag{B0.31}
\]
Then
\(\overline{\eta(p)}Q^{s+z-1}P_p^*-Q^{z-w-1}P_p
=Q^{z-1}(1-D)G_p/((1-V)(1-W))\).
Thus compensation replaces \(H_{\eta,u}\) in (B0.28) by
\[
\mathcal H_{\eta,u,Z}=\sum_{(p_i)}\prod_iw_i(Q_i/P_i)Q_i^{z-1}G_{p_i}
\prod_{p\notin S\cup\{p_i\}}H_p.
\tag{B0.32}
\]
For \(p\nmid u\), put \(v=\chi_p(u)\), \(E_p=P_p^*+D\). The phase identity \(c_pD=v^{-1}\) gives
\[
G_p+v^{-1}H_p=\frac{(1-V)(1-W)}{1-D}
\left[(v^{-1}-h_p)\left(\frac V{1-V}-D\right)
+(c_p+v^{-1}-h_p)E_p\right].
\tag{B0.33}
\]
Define \(\Delta_p=G_p+\overline{\psi_u(p)}H_p\) also at row primes. Expanding \(G_p=-\overline{\psi_u(p)}H_p+\Delta_p\) factors every main slot into
\(-\sum_pw_i(Q/P_i)Q^{z-1}\overline{\psi_u(p)}\), while error slots replace the corresponding \(H_p\) by \(\Delta_p\). This exact expansion keeps row collisions and never assumes local nonvanishing.

The local products converge normally and satisfy \(H_{\eta,u}\ll q_u^\epsilon\) on
\[
\Re s\ge.51,\quad\Re z\ge.34,\quad\Re w\ge-.01,\quad\Re(s+w)\ge1+\epsilon_1.
\tag{B0.34}
\]
For the principal row they also converge on \(\Re s\ge.87,\Re w\ge3/4,\Re z\ge1/8\). The entire correction has a fixed raw polynomial bound on every contour box. On \((\beta_*+e,1/2,.34)\) and \((2,2,v)\), respectively, it is \(\ll q_u^\epsilon Z^{.34\ell}\) and \(\ll q_u^\epsilon Z^{v\ell}\).

Only \(u=1\) has principal numerator. A nonunit sixth-power-free row coprime to \(S\) has nontrivial tame inertia. For a unit \(u\ne1\), choose a primary \(n\equiv-2-3\omega\pmod{36\mathcal O}\), coprime to the remaining fixed primes by CRT. Then \(q_n\equiv7\pmod{36}\), so \(\chi_n(u)=u\ne1\); this proves that its numerator character is also nonprincipal. At \(w=1,z=1/6\), write \(t=Q^{-1}\), \(D=\eta(p)Q^{-s}\), \(R=\overline{\alpha(p)}^6\eta(p)^6Q^{3-6s}\). Then
\[
H_{\eta,p}(s)=\frac{1-t^2}{1-R}\left(1+\frac{t(D-R)}{1-D}\right).
\tag{B0.35}
\]
Enlarging the fixed cutoff gives \(|H_\eta(s)-1|\le1/2\) for \(\Re s\ge.87\). At this residue, \(G_p/H_p=-1+O(Q^{-.87})\). With \(r_{\rm slot}\) fixed prime slots, define
\[
c_S=\frac{(\operatorname{Res}_{s=1}\zeta_{\mathbb K}^S(s))^2}{6}\widehat W_1(1)\mathscr M(1/6)>0,
\quad A(Z)=(-1)^{r_{\rm slot}}Z^{-\ell/6}\prod_i\sum_pw_i(Q/P_i)Q^{-5/6}.
\]
Writing the radial Riesz kernel as a positive integral of Gaussians and Fourier-transforming gives, with \(\kappa_{\rm rad}=2\pi/\sqrt3\),
\[
\mathscr M(\sigma)=\kappa_{\rm rad}^{\,1-2\sigma}
\frac{\Gamma(\sigma)}{\Gamma(1-\sigma)}
\int_0^\infty W_0(r)r^{-\sigma}\,dr>0,\qquad 0<\sigma<1.
\]
In particular, \(\mathscr M(1/6)>0\). The prime ideal theorem gives \(|A(Z)|\asymp(\log Z)^{-r_{\rm slot}}\), and
\(\mathcal H_{\eta,1,Z}(s,1,1/6)=H_\eta(s)Z^{\ell/6}A(Z)(1+O(Z^{-\mu_P}))\)
for any \(0<\mu_P<.87\min\ell_i\). Put
\[
h=1+\ell-x,\quad k=5/6-x/3-\ell/6,\quad J_\eta=I_\eta^{\rm comp}/(c_SA(Z)),
\]
\[
f_\eta(Z)=\frac1{2\pi i}\int_{(2)}Z^{s-k}e^{(s-5/6)^2}\frac{H_\eta(s)}{L_{\mathbb K}^S(s,\eta)}\,ds.
\tag{B0.36}
\]
The main term of the double residue is \(f_\eta\), with the prime-product approximation error estimated in §B0.7; the power \(Z^{\ell/6}\), rather than the logarithmic normalizer, is the compensator's quantitative gain.

statement:
\begin{theorem}\label{thm:main}
For every integer \(q\ge1\) and every Dirichlet character \(\chi\)
modulo \(q\), \(L(s,\chi)\) has no zero in the strict half-plane
\(\Rea s>\theta\), with \(\theta\) exactly as in \eqref{eq:theta}.
The assertion includes \(\zeta\), all real zeros, all heights,
principal characters, and imprimitive characters.  A principal
pole at \(1\) is allowed.  Moreover, every finite-order Hecke
\(L\)-function over \(F=\mathbb Q(\sqrt{-3})\) is zero-free in
this same half-plane, with its principal pole allowed.
\end{theorem}

statement:
### B4.1. Full-modulus Poisson summation

For \(A=cn^3\), define the finite convolution
\[
\mathcal F(a,A,H)=\sum_{\substack{d\bmod a\\H\equiv b_*Ad\pmod a}}
\chi_a(d)g_{\xi\chi_A}\!\left(b_*A,\frac{H-b_*Ad}{a}\right).
\tag{B4.1}
\]
Expanding the \(a\)-Gauss sum and writing \(m=r+b_*A l\) gives
\[
\sum_{m\bmod ab_*A}\xi(m)\chi_A(m)q_a^{-1/2}g_{\chi_a}(a,-m)e(Hm/(ab_*A))
=q_a^{1/2}\mathcal F(a,A,H).
\tag{B4.2}
\]
The \(l\)-sum imposes the congruence in (B4.1); the \(r\)-sum is its remaining Gauss sum. This calculation uses the full modulus and requires no coprimality between \(a\) and \(A\).

The planar dilation contributes \(X/q_A\); with the physical square root it leaves \(X^{1/2}/(\sqrt{q_{b_*}}q_A)\). Its Fourier argument is \(Xq_H/q_A\). At each prime of \(S\), the local factor of \(\xi\) is primitive and its Gauss frequency is a unit multiple of \(H\). Thus all frequencies meeting \(S\), including zero, vanish. Write the remaining frequency uniquely as \(H=u r^6\), with \(r\) primary and \(u\) sixth-power-free retaining the unit of \(H\). No factor six is introduced. Mellin inversion, followed by \(s=t+1-z\), gives (B0.28). On the initial lines \((\Re s,\Re w,\Re z)=(3,3,2)\), the trivial finite-sum bound gives the summable majorant
\[
C_S\sum_{u,c,n,a,r}q_u^{-2}q_c^{-5/2}q_n^{-7}q_a^{-2}q_r^{-12}.
\tag{B4.3}
\]
Together with the Gaussian and Mellin decay, this justifies the initial interchanges.

We record the phase cancellation because it determines every local numerator. CRT gives
\[
g_{\xi\chi_A}(b_*A,K)=\xi(A)\chi_A(b_*)g_\xi(b_*,K)g_{\chi_A}(A,K).
\]
At \(S\), \(K\equiv H/a\); its factor is \(\sqrt{q_{b_*}}\tau\xi(A)\overline{\xi(u)}\xi(a)\). The normalizing factors in the probe leave precisely \(\overline{\xi(u)}\). The remaining \(b_*\)-symbols cancel with \(\chi_a(b_*)\Xi(A)^{-1}\).

For a good prime put \(t_p=v_p(A)\), \(k_p=v_p(a)\), \(H_p=H/p^{v_p(H)}\), \(a_p'=a/p^{k_p}\), \(A_p'=A/p^{t_p}\). Before cancellation, its CRT-unit factor is
\[
\chi_p(H_p)^{k_p-t_p}\chi_p(a_p')^{t_p}\chi_p(A_p')^{t_p-k_p}\chi_p(b_*)^{t_p-k_p}.
\]
Reciprocity (B1.5) gives the exact identity
\[
R(A,a)\prod_p\chi_p(a_p')^{t_p}\chi_p(A_p')^{-k_p}
=\prod_pR(p,p)^{t_pk_p}.
\tag{B4.4}
\]
Write \(t_p=e_p+3l_p\), \(e_p\in\{0,1\}\). After dividing by the cross-prime factors in \(\gamma_1(c)\), the remaining pair factor for \(p<r\) is \(R(p,r)^{e_pl_r+e_rl_p+l_pl_r}\). By the quadratic-refinement identity (B1.4), their product is
\[
R(c,n)G(n^3)\prod_p\overline{G(p^3)}^{\,l_p}
R(p,p)^{-e_pl_p-l_p(l_p-1)/2}.
\tag{B4.5}
\]
The first two factors, together with \(G(c)\), cancel the inserted \(\overline{G(cn^3)}\). Also \(\alpha(c)\overline{\alpha(cn^3)}=\overline{\alpha(n)}^{\,3}\). These identities allow \(c\) and \(n\) to share primes.
title: B4.1. Full-modulus Poisson summation

finite-order Eisenstein Hecke nonvanishing statements hold above it.
The independently stated rational corollaries use the upper bound
874957019420098946128603850561452983/1000000000000000000000000000000000000. Seven checked statements include unique root existence, so
the exact root hypotheses are not vacuous.

Native Lean verification passed at 2026-10-09T19:22:58.033625+00:00.

independent Comparator/Lean/NanoDa/con-ron acceptance, if obtained later,
belongs in a separate dossier bound to this source manifest and public commit.
This snapshot alone does not claim external checker acceptance or a signed receipt.

3132 locally built and 4101
official cache modules. The original seven protected files remain unchanged.
The native audit also checks all previous literal N24 targets by monotonicity.
Allowed axioms are only propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound.

This continues the sequence: compression, rational certificate refinement,
then removal of approximation slack at the cubic endpoint. It does not
establish a new moment estimate or a threshold below the method's cubic barrier.
Nielstron is the human contributor; research and formalization were AI-assisted.
The work builds on Tim Gehrunger / ProofCouncil and OpenAI/math.

The exact pinned LeanLeanBench metric counts 259073 QRH tokens,
versus 251464 at the previous N24 result and 294019 in the immutable original.
Per-file counts, source hashes, and the separate unchanged OAI support scope
are in compressed/audit/token-counts.json. This is not an official benchmark
entry. Verification wrappers are separate audit artifacts outside that package.

statement:
### 5.2. Principal, small and large rows

For \(u=1\), move first to \((\Re s,\Re w,\Re z)=(\beta_*+e,1+e,1/6+e)\). Move \(w\) to \(3/4\), crossing its numerator pole, and in that residue move \(z\) to \(1/8\), crossing the pole of \(\zeta_K^S(6z)\). The paths lie in \(\mathcal B_1\), and \(\mathscr M\) has no positive-strip pole. Equations (2.18), (2.22) and (2.23) identify the double residue. The two remaining contours save \(y/4\) and \(h/24\), while the prime approximation saves \(\mu_P\).

For \(q_u\le Z^{d_{\min}}\), excluding \(u=1\), use \((\beta_*+e,1/2,z_0)\). The functional equation and convexity bound the numerator by \(U^{3/5+\varepsilon}(1+T)^A\). Equation (2.17), ideal counting, and \(q_u^{-z_0}\) give relative exponent
\[
 h(z_0-1/6)-y/2+\frac{63}{50}d_{\min}
 =-\frac{88763}{990000}<-\frac1{20}.
\tag{5.4}
\]
This includes the five nonprincipal unit rows. No numerator pole is crossed.

For \(q_u>Z^{h+\zeta_0}\), take \((\Re s,\Re w,\Re z)=(2,2,v)\). Absolute Euler convergence and (2.17) give a total
\[
 \ll Z^{x/2+1+y+(h+\zeta_0)(1+\varepsilon)-\zeta_0v+\varepsilon},
\tag{5.5}
\]
which is arbitrarily power-small after fixing \(v>2\) sufficiently large.

For all these moves the independent height coordinates are \(\Im(s+z),\Im z,\Im w\). The Gaussian and two Mellin transforms have arbitrary decay in these coordinates. On fixed real boxes the unseparated arithmetic factor has a fixed polynomial conductor-height bound, so omitted segments and horizontal joins contribute \(O_N(Z^BT^{-N})\). Reciprocal segments outside a buffered rectangle are never moved off the global line. On a horizontal face inside it, the buffered reciprocal estimate and a global polynomial numerator estimate suffice. The exponent \(B\) is fixed before the external tail order \(N\).

Choose the real buffers and internal moment losses first, preserving a common positive fraction of
\(\min(\mu,y/4,h/24,\mu_P,1/20)\). For each fixed target and its already chosen smooth orders, take \(T=3Z^\tau\), with \(\tau>0\) small enough to absorb every polynomial height cost and to make the witness tails valid uniformly for \(d\ge d_{\min}\). Choose \(N\) last. The height exponent and thresholds may depend on the target; the retained real margin need not. We obtain some common \(\Delta>0\) with
\[
 J_\eta(Z)-f_\eta(Z)\ll_\eta Z^{\beta_*-k-\Delta}.
\tag{5.6}
\]

theorem calibrated_physical_tuple_sum_first87
    (K : ℕ) (e delta a b r B : ℝ)
    (he : 0 < e) (he1 : e < 1 / 1000)

    (ha : 0 < a) (hb : 0 < b) (hr : (17 / 50 : ℝ) ≤ r)
    (hB : 0 ≤ B)
    (S : Finset (Ideal O)) (hS : SourceExclusions S)
    (hmax : ∀P∈S, P.IsMaximal) (hfirst : FirstTail (4 * e) S) :
    ∃C : ℝ, 0 < C ∧ ∀(eta : Character) (u : FreeRow), u.val ≠ 1 →
      ∀(T : Fin K → Finset PrimeIdeal) (hTout : ∀i P, P ∈ T i → P.val ∉ S),
      (∀P : (∀i, T i), Function.Injective (fun i => (P i).val)) →
      ∀(Y : Fin K → ℝ), (∀i, 1 ≤ Y i) →
      ∀(W : Fin K → ℝ → ℂ),
      (∀i, Function.support (W i) ⊆ Icc a b) →

      ∀(x w z : ℂ), (87 / 100 : ℝ) ≤ x.re →
      HeckeZeroSupremum.beta + 8 * e ≤ x.re →

      (∑P : (∀i, T i), ‖calibratedTupleValue S hS hmax eta u
        (fun i => (P i).val) (fun i => hTout i (P i).val (P i).property)
        W Y x w z‖) ≤
      C * (eta.modulus.absNorm : ℝ) ^ delta *
        ((Ideal.span {u.val} : Ideal O).absNorm : ℝ) ^ (3 / 5 + delta) *
        (∏i, (Y i) ^ r) * (3 + |x.im|) ^ 2 * (3 + |w.im|) ^ 2

statement:
## T1. Dependency order, conventions and exact endpoint

Read B1 for finite arithmetic; B2 for completed reflection, local branches and its energy bound; B3 for inverse and plain moments; B4 for physical Euler factors and coefficient mass. B0 assembles these results using the detector, signed Gram bound, full numerator inversion and a uniform improvement of the zero supremum. The forward references are acyclic.

The normalizations are fixed throughout: ideal columns use one primary generator, element rows keep all six units, \(q_a=|a|^2\), the additive character is \(e(z)=\exp(2\pi i\operatorname{Tr}(z/\lambda))\), and the measure is \(2\,dx\,dy/\sqrt3\). Symbols at nonunits are zero even for exponent zero or six. The Hecke ideal-series normalization is ordinary \(L\), not completed \(L\); upstream `Hecke/IdealBridge.lean` divides its lattice continuation by six. No extra factor six is introduced into the unique frequency factorization \(H=ur^6\).

The following elementary facts complete the exact numerical part of B0.6. The formal counterpart is `Cycle25.Arithmetic.Endpoint`, using exact rational and polynomial identities.

**T1.1 (root).** Exact substitution gives \(p(\inf I)<0<p(\sup I)\). On \([1/6,1/5]\),
\[
p'(x)=3708x^3-9405x^2+4866x+275
\ge-9405/25+4866/6+275=3549/5>0.
\]
The intermediate value theorem and strict monotonicity prove existence and uniqueness of the chosen root. Other roots of the quartic are irrelevant.

**T1.2 (geometry without numerical optimization).** In B0.45–B0.49 use
\[
\begin{split}
\kappa_0&=(5-3\ell_0)/6,\\
\delta_0&=\frac{25-60\ell_0+27\ell_0^2}{6(5+4\ell_0-3\ell_0^2)},\\
C_0&=\frac{6\kappa_0-1}{15\kappa_0-2},\quad V_0=5/6-\delta_0,\\
R'_0&=-1+\frac{C_0(V_0^2-\delta_0^2C_0)}{2(V_0+\delta_0C_0)^2},\\
h_0&=-\frac{(1+\ell_0)/2+\ell_0/(6\kappa_0)}{3R'_0/4-1/(24\kappa_0)},\quad
x_0=1+\ell_0-h_0,\quad y_0=h_0-2\ell_0.
\end{split}
\]
Every denominator is separated from zero by the same rational interval calculation. Reducing polynomials modulo \(p\) verifies both binding equations B0.48 and the full two-variable identity B0.49. The latter identity, with its strictly positive coefficient minorants, proves the bound on the entire parameter rectangle; a floating-point grid would not suffice. In particular, \(36-174\delta+347\delta^2>0\) follows by completing the square, since \(36-174^2/(4\cdot347)>0\). The nonnegative terms in B0.49 prove \(F^{(4)}_{\kappa_0}\le b_0\), with equality only at its binding point.

**T1.3 (uniform perturbation).** On \(0\le p\le1/2\), \(\kappa\ge7/10\), the counting coefficient of §B0.5 has derivative
\[
\partial_\kappa C_\kappa(p)
=\frac{6p(1-p)^2}{[3\kappa(3-p)-2p]^2}
\le\frac{8/9}{[(15/2)(7/10)-1]^2}<1/18.
\]
For \(V=5/6-\delta\ge0\), \(\partial_C R=\delta V^2/[2(V+\delta C)^2]\le5/12\). The exact intervals give \(h_0<4/5\) and \(0<h_0-4\ell_0<13/100\). Differentiating B0.47 now gives
\[
\partial_\kappa F^{(4)}
\le\frac34\frac45\frac5{12}\frac1{18}
 +\frac5{12}\frac{13/100}{12(7/10)^2}<1/10.
\]
As \(\kappa-\kappa_0=2(\beta_*-b_0)\),
\[
F^{(4)}_\kappa-\beta_*\le-\frac45(\beta_*-b_0).
\]
The other dyad endpoint, floor bin and small rows have respectively margins exceeding \(.06,.01,.05\), all checked with rational intervals. The same exact interval identities check the supply and geometry inequalities. Thus the strict losses can be chosen uniformly before a target character is fixed.

**T1.4 (minimal generalized damping interface).** For \(\kappa\ge7/10\), \(t,z,\delta,q\ge0\), \(q\le\delta/2\), let \(z_\kappa(t)=\max(0,z-t/(3\kappa))\). Since \(0\le z-z_\kappa(t)\le t/(3\kappa)\),
\[
-\delta t/4-qz_\kappa(t)/2
\le-qz/2-\delta t\bigl(1/4-1/(12\kappa)\bigr)\le-qz/2.
\]
This is the variable-\(\kappa\) form of the weaker damping used by the weighted-numerator Lean route. B0.5 proves its own stronger \(\delta/2\)-weighted coefficient statement. The physical coefficient dictionary and combined-conductor mass bound are proved in `Cycle25.Numerator.Imported.NumeratorLocalCoefficients`, `Cycle25.Numerator.Imported.NumeratorPhysicalPacketMass`, `Cycle25.Numerator.ReflectionMass`, and `Cycle25.Numerator.ActualBin`; these supply the scalar-to-source transfer.

**T1.5 (rational target).** The root interval implies
\[
b_0<\theta=683505193/781250000,
\quad 0<\theta-b_0<4\cdot10^{-14}.
\]
Exact cross-multiplication proves
\[
\theta<10499/12000
<874957019420098946128604623/10^{27}<7/8.
\]
The second intermediate value is the pinned public catalogue threshold. No finite decimal approximation to \(b_0\) is treated as its definition. Proving T0 implies the rational target by transitivity of the strict inequalities.

# Single compensating prime: independent 29/33 analytic route

This is a non-record formalization and reusable-estimate contribution.
The precise source is under `formalization/`; the supplied paper is under
`manuscript/`. Start with `Verification.md` for the mathematical coverage.

The key endpoints are:

- `ZetaZeroFree.Analytic.beta_le_twenty_nine_thirty_thirds`;
- `ZetaZeroFree.Analytic.dirichletL_ne_zero_of_twenty_nine_thirty_thirds_lt_re`;
- `ZetaZeroFree.Analytic.riemannZeta_ne_zero_of_twenty_nine_thirty_thirds_lt_re`;
- `ZetaZeroFree.Analytic.heckeL_ne_zero_of_twenty_nine_thirty_thirds_lt_re`;
- `ZetaZeroFree.Analytic.Moments.D3.mixed_plain_moment_radical`.

The contributor's completed ordinary Lean 4.34.1 checks establish the stated
theorems using standard axioms only, independently of the previous terminal
7/8 theorem. The four main proof closures also passed local Comparator, Lean,
NanoDa and con-ron checks on 2026-10-10. The evidence is included for maintainer
review; no registry admission or signed receipt is claimed. See `NOTICE.md`
for provenance and publication rights.

From `formalization/`, with Python 3.9+, Git and elan installed:

```sh
python3 bootstrap_dependencies.py --check-bundle
elan toolchain install leanprover/lean4:v4.34.1
python3 bootstrap_dependencies.py --prepare
elan run leanprover/lean4:v4.34.1 lake exe cache get
python3 verify_analytic.py
```

The cache command is optional; the verifier builds explicit required targets.
Keep `lake-manifest.json` unchanged; do not run a floating dependency update.
The full OpenAI repository and local caches are unnecessary: its required
source closure is vendored as ordinary files. No GPU or FrankenLean is needed.

`evidence/analytic-verification-report.json` is a path-sanitized copy of the
completed source build, all-declaration dependency audit and fresh kernel
replay. `publication-transformations.json` records the original hashes.
`evidence/final-audit.lean` preserves the generated audit source. Negative
controls and their logs are in `evidence/negative-controls/`.

Historical earlier attempts mentioned in `Verification.md` are provenance,
not required inputs; this snapshot intentionally includes the final proof and
its current evidence. It excludes tracker state, old terminal-conclusion
wrappers, experimental proof loaders, caches and compiled `.olean` files.

statement:
### C.3. Two Poisson transformations and the local projector

For an independent target \(\Sigma\), assume
\(1\le H,L,F,\Sigma\le Z^{C_0}\), \(\max(H,LF)\le\Sigma\). We will prove the transfer
\[
E(H,L,F;\xi,W)
\ll Z^\varepsilon\Sigma\|W\|_{C^{4m+12}}^2
\left(1+\sup\frac{E(H',X',F';\xi',U)}{\Sigma'}\right),
\tag{C.8}
\]
where \(\Sigma'=X'F'\), \(H',X',F'\ge1\), \(\|U\|_{C^m}\le1\) on a fixed enlargement of the support, and
\[
H'\le\frac{HL}{\Sigma F},\qquad
\frac{H'}{\Sigma'}\le\frac H\Sigma,\qquad \Sigma'\le L.
\tag{C.9}
\]

Choose a nonnegative radial Schwartz majorant \(\Phi\ge1\) on \([0,1]\), with \(\widehat\Phi\) supported in \([0,C_\Phi]\), by squaring a suitably rescaled real Schwartz function of compact Fourier support. If \(\operatorname{supp}W\subset[u,v]\), fix \(c_I\ge\max(1,4C_\Phi v^2)\) and an enlarged support \([u/2,2v]\).

First apply (C.3) to the squared column sum. Write \(n_i=Cu_i\), \(C=(n_1,n_2)\). The primitive row character has conductor \(u_1u_2\) and residual mask \(C\); let \(d\mid C\) be its mask divisor. The zero frequency costs \(O(H\|W\|_\infty^2)\). Use \(a_\xi(n)\gamma_1(n)=\mu(n)G(n)\xi(n)\), expand its fixed ray factor, and remove \((u_1,u_2)=1\) by \(u_i=tx_i\) and complete Möbius inversion. The resulting inverse polynomial for a fixed ray character is
\[
P_{C,d,t}(y;U)=\sum_n^{*}\mu(n)\xi_1(n)1_{(n,t)=1}
\overline{\chi_n(y)}\chi_n(C)^4\chi_n(d)U(q_n/\ell),
\qquad \ell=\frac L{q_Cq_t}.
\tag{C.10}
\]
Here \(C,t\) are coprime squarefree, \(d\mid C\), and \(q_Cq_t\le2vL\). Combine the original frequency and label as \(y=hf^2\); the old zeros include \((f,Ct)=(h,t)=1\). This map has divisor-bounded fibres. Enlarge its nonzero image to \(q_y\le Y_{C,d}\), where
\[
w_{C,d}=\frac{Hq_C}{q_dL^2F},\qquad
Y_{C,d}=\frac{c_I\Sigma LFq_d}{Hq_C^2}.
\]
Because \(\Sigma\ge LF\), the first Cauchy–Schwarz and smooth separation permit the positive form
\[
Q_{\xi_1}(U)=
\sum_{\substack{C,t\ \mathrm{sf}\\(C,t)=1\\q_Cq_t\le2vL}}
\sum_{d\mid C}w_{C,d}\sum_y\Phi(q_y/Y_{C,d})|P_{C,d,t}(y;U)|^2.
\tag{C.11}
\]
After this positive enlargement, if \(Q_{\xi_1}(U)\le M\|U\|_{C^j}^2\) for every common \(U\), then
\(E(H,L,F;\xi,W)\ll Z^\varepsilon(\Sigma+M)\|W\|_{C^{2j+4}}^2\).
The separated kernels are products of annular weights, inverse square roots and \(\widehat\Phi(A/(x_1x_2))\) in a bounded supported range, so their required derivatives are uniform.

Apply (C.3) again, now to the \(y\)-sum. Write the two columns as \(gz_i\), take \(e\mid g\) for the mask divisor, and remove \((z_1,z_2)=1\) by \(z_i=wn_i\). The nonzero terms satisfy
\[
(g,Ct)=(w,gCth)=1,\qquad e\mid g,\qquad h\ne0,
\]
and have sign \(\mu(e)\mu(w)\). The inverse-character conversion in (A.1) restores cubic coefficients. The paired ray phase is \(\xi_1(z_1z_2^{-1})G(z_2z_1^{-1})\). Expanding the fixed function
\(\xi_1(z)G(z^{-1})=\sum_{\xi'}c_{\xi'}\xi'(z)\)
therefore supplies coefficients \(a_{\xi'}(n)\) independent of every reconstruction choice.

Reconstruct the puncture, label and row by
\[
r=tg/e,\qquad f'=Cew,\qquad k'=deh,
\qquad a^\sharp(n)=a_{\xi'}(n)1_{(n,r)=1}\chi_n(k')\chi_n(f')^4.
\tag{C.12}
\]
The ideals \(r,f'\) are coprime and squarefree. The local character calculation includes the conjugation
\[
\chi_n(dh)\overline{\chi_n(e)}\chi_n(C)^4
=\chi_n(deh)\chi_n(Ce)^4;
\tag{C.13}
\]
Both sides have exponent five at \(e\) on units and vanish otherwise. The \(w\)-factor is the multiplicative correction in (A.1).

Let \(U_0(x)=x^{-1/2}U(x)\). Direct substitution gives the column scale, full scalar, and kernel:
\[
X'_0=\frac\ell{q_gq_w}=\frac L{q_rq_{f'}},
\qquad w_{C,d}\frac{Y_{C,d}q_g}{q_e\ell}=\frac{c_I\Sigma q_r}{L^2},
\]
\[
K_{r,f',k'}(x_1,x_2)=U_0(x_1)\overline{U_0(x_2)}
\widehat\Phi\!\left(\frac{c_I\Sigma Fq_{k'}q_r^2}{HLx_1x_2}\right).
\tag{C.14}
\]
The kernel and scalar depend only on the reconstructed triple. Their support imposes
\(q_rq_{f'}\le2vL\), \(0<q_{k'}\le HL/(\Sigma Fq_r^2)\).

At fixed \((r,f',k')\), all preimages are
\[
t\mid r,\quad f'=Cew,\quad e\mid k',\quad(w,k')=1,
\quad d\mid(C,k'),\quad g=e(r/t),\quad h=k'/(de),
\]
with the factorization \(f'=Cew\) disjoint. At a prime \(\mathfrak p\mid f'\), put \(I_{\mathfrak p}=1_{\mathfrak p\mid k'}\). Allocating it to \(C,e,w\) gives, respectively,
\[
\underbrace{(1+I_{\mathfrak p})}_{\mathfrak p\mid C}
+\underbrace{(-I_{\mathfrak p})}_{\mathfrak p\mid e}
+\underbrace{(-(1-I_{\mathfrak p}))}_{\mathfrak p\mid w}
=I_{\mathfrak p}.
\tag{C.15}
\]
The two \(C\)-terms correspond to \(\mathfrak p\nmid d\) and \(\mathfrak p\mid d\). Thus the signed fibre sum forces \(f'\mid k'\); choices \(t\mid r\) contribute \(\tau(r)\). The shared kernel, scalar and character make this an exact cancellation before absolute values.

Writing \(Z_Q\) for the second zero frequency, we have
\[
Q_{\xi_1}(U)-Z_Q=
\frac{c_I\Sigma}{L^2}\sum_{\xi'}c_{\xi'}
\sum_{\substack{r,f'\ \mathrm{sf}\\(r,f')=1}}q_r\tau(r)
\sum_{\substack{k'\ne0\\f'\mid k'}}\sum_{n_1,n_2}^{*}
a^\sharp(n_1)\overline{a^\sharp(n_2)}
K_{r,f',k'}(q_{n_1}/X'_0,q_{n_2}/X'_0).
\tag{C.16}
\]
The principal calculation in (C.3) gives
\(|Z_Q|\ll Z^\varepsilon\Sigma\|U\|_\infty^2\): its absolute divisor sum is bounded by
\(\Sigma\sum_C\tau(C)q_C^{-2}\sum_{q_t\ll L}q_t^{-1}\).

On dyads \(q_r\asymp R,q_{f'}\asymp F'\), set
\[
X'=\frac L{RF'},\qquad \Sigma'=\frac LR,
\qquad H'=\frac{HL}{\Sigma FR^2}.
\tag{C.17}
\]
Retain only nonempty supports. The projector implies \(F'\le q_{k'}\le HL/(\Sigma Fq_r^2)\), hence \(H'\ge1\). For every \(j\mid r\),
\[
\frac{X'}{q_j}\ge\frac{\Sigma Fq_r^2}{HRq_j}
\ge\frac{\Sigma F}{H}\ge1.
\tag{C.18}
\]
Thus puncture removal gives admissible scales and preserves \(\Sigma'\). Also \(1\le X'/X'_0<4\), so rescaled kernels lie in a fixed enlargement and have uniform \(C^{2m+4}\) norm controlled by \(\|U\|_{C^{2m+4}}^2\).

Let \(S_m\) be the supremum in (C.8). For each retained \(r\), puncture removal and positive enlargement of the \((f',k')\) ranges bound the common-test column sum by \(Z^\varepsilon(\Sigma')^2S_m\|V\|_{C^m}^2\). Apply (1.4), then count \(O(R)\) ideals \(r\). The complete scalar is
\[
\frac{\Sigma R}{L^2}\,R(\Sigma')^2=\Sigma.
\]
Divisor factors and dyadic counts cost \(Z^\varepsilon\). This proves (C.8); (C.17) gives
\(H'/\Sigma'=H/(\Sigma FR)\le H/\Sigma\), \(H'\le HL/(\Sigma F)\), and \(\Sigma'\le L\).

    (hW1 : Function.support W1⊆Set.Icc a1 b1)
    (hW0s : ContDiff ℝ ∞ W0) (hW1s : ContDiff ℝ ∞ W1)
    (hWB : ∀x,‖W1 x‖≤B)
    (aCut bCut : ℝ) (haCut : 0<aCut) (hbCut : 0<bCut)
    (η : HeckeFamily.Character) (S : Finset Id) (hS : ∀P∈S,P.IsMaximal)
    (hbad : fixedBadPrimes⊆S) (a ε : ℝ) (ha : 0<a) (hε : 0<ε) (hε1 : ε≤1) :

      elementNorm (calibrationForSet S hS).generator≤Z^(2/33:ℝ) →
      1≤Z^(15/33:ℝ)/L →
      1≤(Z^(15/33:ℝ)/L)^2/
        lowPhysicalScale (calibrationForSet S hS) (Z^(13/33:ℝ)/L) (Z^(15/33:ℝ)/L) →
    ∀ t : ℝ,

        (lowMarkedInverseRow η S hS 1 (Z^(1+σ)) t) v‖ ≤

    (η : HeckeFamily.Character) (S : Finset Id) (hS : ∀P∈S,P.IsMaximal)
    (hbad : fixedBadPrimes⊆S) (a b τ : ℝ) (ha : 0<a) (hτ : 0<τ) (hτ1 : τ≤1/2)
    (W0 W1 : ℝ→ℂ) (a0 b0 a1 b1 B : ℝ)

    (hW0 : Function.support W0⊆Set.Icc a0 b0)
    (hW1 : Function.support W1⊆Set.Icc a1 b1)
    (hW0s : ContDiff ℝ ∞ W0) (hW1s : ContDiff ℝ ∞ W1) (hWB : ∀x,‖W1 x‖≤B) :
    ∃ degree : ℕ, ∃ C : ℝ, 0<C ∧ ∀ᶠ Z : ℝ in Filter.atTop, 1<Z ∧
    ∀ (T : Fin 1→Finset PrimeIdeal), (∀i P,P∈T i→Supported P.val) →
      (∀i P,P∈T i→P.val∉S) →
      (∀i P,P∈T i→a*Z^z≤(Ideal.absNorm P.val:ℝ) ∧ (Ideal.absNorm P.val:ℝ)≤b*Z^z) →
    ∀ (J : Finset (Fin 1)) (σ : ℝ), |σ|≤τ/4 →
    ∀ (W : Fin 1→ℝ→ℂ), (∀i x,‖W i x‖≤1) → ∀ t : ℝ,
      ‖∑p : (∀i,canonicalSlotSupport (T i)),
        compensationSubsetWeight η W (fun _=>Z^z) (fun i=>(p i).val) J*
        compensationRowTest η (calibrationForSet S hS) W0 W1 (fun i=>(p i).val)
          J (Z^(13/33:ℝ)) (Z^(15/33:ℝ))
          (Z^(1+lowSelectedLength (fun _ : Fin 1=>z) J+σ)) t*
        selectedSlotFactor W (fun _=>Z^z) (fun i=>(p i).val) J t‖ ≤
      C*(1+‖t‖)^degree*Z^(20/99+1000*τ:ℝ)

def AllNaturalMixedAt (a b radial B Bfixed L Mcap ε Z : ℝ)
    (J : ℕ) (S : Finset (ℕ × ℕ)) (C : ℝ) : Prop :=
  ∀ s : NaturalPlainState Z B radial 1, s.width ≤ Mcap →
    (s.puncture.absNorm : ℝ) ≤ Z ^ B →
    (∀ z, s.radial.keep z →
      ((excluded (naturalPlainCharacter s.character z) s.puncture).modulus.radical.absNorm : ℝ) ≤ Z ^ Bfixed) →
    ∀ W₁ W₂ : 𝓢(ℝ, ℂ), Function.support (W₁ : ℝ → ℂ) ⊆ Set.Icc a b →
      Function.support (W₂ : ℝ → ℂ) ⊆ Set.Icc a b →
    ∀ X₁ X₂ t₁ t₂ : ℝ, 0 < X₁ → 0 < X₂ → X₁ ≤ Z ^ L → X₂ ≤ Z ^ L →
    s.energy W₁ W₂ X₁ X₂ t₁ t₂ ≤

        ((S.sup (schwartzSeminormFamily ℝ ℝ ℂ) W₁) *
         (S.sup (schwartzSeminormFamily ℝ ℝ ℂ) W₂)) ^ 2 *
        (1 + ‖t₁‖) ^ J * (1 + ‖t₂‖) ^ J * Z ^ (s.width + ε)

statement:
## Compression before tightening

The unchanged pinned LeanLeanBench tokenizer counts the QRH package as follows:

| Stage | Lean source tokens |
| --- | ---: |
| Immutable original | 294,019 |
| Compressed, original bound | 251,528 |
| Final compressed and tighter result | 251,464 |

The final reduction is 42,555 tokens (14.4736%). It includes shorter proofs,
shared binders, removal of unused helper declarations, readable public
corollaries, and the stronger result. These are source tokens, not LLM tokens.
Comments, imports, `lakefile.lean`, and `.lake` are excluded by the benchmark.
The unchanged selected OAI supporting source contributes 5,809,761 tokens:
QRH plus that fixed support decreases from 6,103,780 to 6,061,225 tokens,
about 0.6972%. Mathlib, Lean, and other fixed dependencies are outside both
reported source scopes. Per-file counts and hashes are in
`compressed/audit/token-counts.json`.
title: Compression before tightening

statement:
def FullWCellsAt {Δ : ℝ} (D : Cycle25.HighParameters.HighData Δ)
    (F : WeightedSourceData D.toMomentData) (η : Character)
    (Z τ : ℝ) (n : ℕ) (weightedC C0 : ℝ) : Prop :=
  letI : NeZero (∏P∈F.S,P) := ⟨fixedPrimeProduct_ne_zero F.S F.exclusions.prime⟩
  ∀idx grid : FreeRow→ℕ,
    let rows := supportedNonfloorRows F.S F.maximal
      (rowBand (Z^(1/100:ℝ)) (Z^(Cycle25.h+D.t))) grid
    (∀u∈rows,idx u ≤ n ∧ grid u ≤ ⌊(49/100:ℝ)/D.e⌋₊ ∧
      (51/100:ℝ)+D.e*grid u ≤ 7/8) →
    (∀u∈rows,detectorMaximum
      (sourceDetectorFamily F.S F.exclusions.prime η u (rayCubeFamily F.modulus ⊤ le_top u))
      (3*(idx u+1:ℕ)*Z^τ) < 51/100+D.e*grid u+2*D.e) →
    (∀u∈rows,(51/100:ℝ)+D.e*grid u ≤ detectorMaximum
      (sourceDetectorFamily F.S F.exclusions.prime η u (rayCubeFamily F.modulus ⊤ le_top u))
      ((3*idx u:ℕ)*Z^τ)) →
    ∀k∈smallDyadicIndices (Z^(Cycle25.h+D.t)),
    ∀i∈Finset.range (n+1),∀j∈Finset.range (⌊(49/100:ℝ)/D.e⌋₊+1),
      let rows' := cubeBinRows (rows∩dyadicRows 1 k) idx grid i j
      let Y : Fin D.N→ℝ := fun j=>Z^(D.ell j)
      let T := fun j=>pool (RayQuotient.identityClass F.modulus ⊤) F.S 1 2 (Y j)
      let hT := nonfloorPoolOutside F.modulus ⊤ F.S D.N 1 2 Y
      let normer := sourceResidueConstant F.W F.W (∏P∈F.S,P)*
        (Probe.principalScalar Finset.univ Z Cycle25.ell
          (slotMass T (residueWeights (fun _=>F.w) Y)) : ℂ)
      rows'.Nonempty → (1/2:ℝ) < sourceDyadConductor Z D.t k →
      (1/3:ℝ) < 2*(51/100+D.e*j)-1 →

    (hφs : Function.support φ⊆Ioo a₀ b₀) (hφB : ∀ y,φ y≤B₀)
    (εm : ℝ) (hεm : 0<εm) :
    ∃ c κ K₀ : ℝ,0<c ∧ c≤1 ∧ 0<κ ∧ 0≤K₀ ∧ ∀ᶠ U : ℝ in atTop,
      ∀ (a ε T allowance Δ C height q : ℝ) (i : ℕ),

### Child coefficient class

statement:
\begin{proposition}[Dynamic local errors and conductor allocation]
\label{prop:probe-errors}
Let $51/100\le a\le1$, $0<e\le10^{-3}$, and take
\[
 x_r=a+16e,\qquad w_r=1-a-6e,\qquad z_r=17/50.
\]
Choose $P_0$ sufficiently large in terms of $e$ and the fixed data.
For $U,T_1\ge1$ and a sixth-power-free row $u$ with $(u,S)=1$
and $q_u\asymp U$, let $\psi_u^*$
be the primitive character inducing $\chi_\bullet(u)$.  Let
$\mathcal W_u$ be any subset of
$\{w:\Re w=w_r,\ |\Im w|\le T_1\}$.  Suppose $\psi_u^*$ is
nonprincipal and, uniformly for $w\in\mathcal W_u$,
\[
 |L(1-w,\overline{\psi_u^*})|\ll U^\epsilon
\]
with any prescribed small power.
For this row on the displayed dynamic region, define \(\mathcal B_i\) by
its preceding slot sum, interpreting each \(\mathcal B_p\) as \(G_p/H_p\),
with \(G_p\) from Equation~\eqref{old-eq:5.13c}.  The stated choice of
\(P_0\) makes \(H_p\ne0\) there for every slot prime, as proved at the start
of the proof.  This statement asserts individual continuation only on this
dynamic region.
Define the main and error parts of a slot by
\[
 \mathcal Q_i(u;z)=
       -\sum_{p\in\mathcal P_i(Z)}W_i(q_p/P_i)q_p^{z-1}\overline{\chi_p(u)},
 \qquad
 \mathcal D_i(u)=\mathcal B_i(u;x,w,z)-\mathcal Q_i(u;z).
\]
Then, for every subset $I$ of the slots and the same points $w\in\mathcal W_u$,
\begin{equation}\label{old-eq:5.13e}
 \left|L^S(w,\chi_\bullet(u))\prod_{i\in I}\mathcal D_i(u)\right|
 \ll U^{a-1/2+12e+\epsilon}(3+T_1)^C
       \prod_{i\in I}P_i^{z_r-1/2}.
\end{equation}
The main parts retain the physical row, all zero masks, and the
fixed identity-ray restriction.  In particular, their central
normalization is
\[
 \mathcal Q_i(u;z)=-P_i^{z-1/2}
       \left(P_i^{-1/2}\sum_{p\in\mathcal P_i(Z)}
          \overline{\chi_p(u)}W_i(q_p/P_i)(q_p/P_i)^{z-1}\right).
\]
At the same points $w\in\mathcal W_u$, and on this dynamic region only, the
full correction has the finite decomposition
\begin{equation}\label{eq:dynamic-compensated-decomposition}
 \mathfrak H_{\eta,u,Z}
 =\mathcal H_{\eta,u}\prod_{i=1}^K(\mathcal Q_i+\mathcal D_i)
 =\mathcal H_{\eta,u}
   \sum_{I\subseteq\{1,\ldots,K\}}
       \prod_{i\in I}\mathcal D_i\prod_{i\notin I}\mathcal Q_i.
\end{equation}
\end{proposition}
title: prop:probe-errors

statement:
### B0.2. Finite reconstruction and common zero witnesses

The original zero extensions give

\[
\varphi_{ua^6}(n)=\varphi_u(n)\mathbf1_{(n,a)=1}.
\]

Separating the primes of a squarefree column which divide \(a\) gives the exact finite identity

\[
M_u(D;W)=\sum_{d\mid\operatorname{rad}(a)}
\mu(d)\varphi_u(d)q_d^{-1/2}M_{ua^6}(D/q_d;W).
\tag{B0.7}
\]

There is no requirement \((u,a)=1\). The character zeros make (B0.7) valid also at shared primes. The coefficient mass is at most \(d(a)\ll q_a^\varepsilon\), where \(d(a)\) counts the ideal divisors of \(a\).

Differentiating in log scale replaces \(W\) by \(-W/2-yW'\). Sobolev on unit log intervals, followed by UM for these common profiles, therefore gives

\[
\sum_{0<q_v\ll H}\sup_{0<E\le D}|M_v(E;W)|^2
\ll H(HD)^\varepsilon,
\qquad H\ge D^{1+\vartheta}.
\tag{B0.8}
\]

The range of subunit scales contains only boundedly many columns and is empty below a fixed positive scale. The \(O(\log(2+D))\) intervals cost only a small power. This argument never assigns a moving arithmetic coefficient to a common-profile moment.

For sixth-power-free \(q_u\asymp U\), choose

\[
H=\max(2U,D^{1+\vartheta}),\qquad P=(H/U)^{1/6}.
\]

There are \(\gg_S P\) primary ideals \(a\), prime to \(S\), with \(q_a\le P\). The map \((u,a)\mapsto ua^6\) is injective: valuations modulo six recover \(u\), the quotients recover \(a\), and its primary generator fixes the unit of \(u\). Averaging (B0.7), summing the rows, and applying (B0.8) gives

\[
\sum_{q_u\asymp U}^{(6)}|M_u(D;W)|^2
\ll U^{1/6}H^{5/6}(UD)^\varepsilon.
\tag{B0.9}
\]

For bounded \(r\) and \(D=U^r\), choose \(\vartheta\) sufficiently small in terms of the requested final loss. Thus the exponent in the sixth-power-free inverse moment is \(e(r)=\max\{1,(1+5r)/6\}\). Sobolev in the real power and height variables gives the same bound for separate rowwise parameters in a fixed real range and a height interval of length \(T\), at a fixed polynomial cost \((1+T)^A\). Only the smooth tests vary in that argument.
title: B0.2. Finite reconstruction and common zero witnesses

def IntegratedWeightedCellsAt {Δ : ℝ} (D : WeightedQRH.HighParameters.HighData Δ)
    (F : WeightedSourceData D.toMomentData) (η : Character)
    (Z τ : ℝ) (n : ℕ) (Cw C0 : ℝ) : Prop :=
  ∀idx grid : FreeRow→ℕ,
    let rows := supportedNonfloorRows F.S F.maximal
      (rowBand (Z^(1/100:ℝ)) (Z^((1587/2000:ℝ)+D.t))) grid
    (∀u∈rows,idx u ≤ n ∧ grid u ≤ ⌊(49/100:ℝ)/D.e⌋₊ ∧
      (51/100:ℝ)+D.e*grid u ≤ 7/8) →
    (∀u∈rows,detectorMaximum
      (sourceDetectorFamily F.S F.exclusions.prime η u (rayCubeFamily F.modulus ⊤ le_top u))
      (3*(idx u+1:ℕ)*Z^τ) < 51/100+D.e*grid u+2*D.e) →
    (∀u∈rows,(51/100:ℝ)+D.e*grid u ≤ detectorMaximum
      (sourceDetectorFamily F.S F.exclusions.prime η u (rayCubeFamily F.modulus ⊤ le_top u))
      ((3*idx u:ℕ)*Z^τ)) →
    ∀k∈smallDyadicIndices (Z^(1587/2000+D.t)),
    ∀i∈Finset.range (n+1),∀j∈Finset.range (⌊(49/100:ℝ)/D.e⌋₊+1),
      let rows' := cubeBinRows (rows∩dyadicRows 1 k) idx grid i j
      let Yp : Fin D.N→ℝ := fun j=>Z^(D.ell j)
      let T := WeightedQRH.Numerator.sourcePrimePool F Z
      let hT := nonfloorPoolOutside F.modulus ⊤ F.S D.N 1 2 Yp
      rows'.Nonempty → (1/2:ℝ) < sourceDyadConductor Z D.t k →
      (1/3:ℝ) < 2*(51/100+D.e*j)-1 →
      sourceDyadConductor Z D.t k ≤ WeightedQRH.h+WeightedQRH.rowExtension →
      ∀q∈WeightedQRH.FullWContour.szRectangle ((3*i+1:ℕ)*Z^τ),
        ‖WeightedQRH.FullWContour.integratedDyadValue F.S F.exclusions F.maximal η rows' T hT
          (fun _ y=>(F.w y:ℂ)) Yp F.W (Z^WeightedQRH.ly)
          ((((51/100+D.e*j)+16*D.e:ℝ):ℂ)+q.1*I) ((17/50:ℂ)+q.2*I)‖ ≤
          Cw*C0*(η.modulus.absNorm:ℝ)^(2*D.eps)*
            Z^(WeightedQRH.signal WeightedQRH.theta-1/40000-
              weightedSourceSZExponent (51/100+D.e*j) D.e)

/-- The literal integrated estimate closes the exact FullWCellsAt interface.
The constant is independent of the moment constant C0 and is linear in Cw. -/

statement:
#### Buffered zero bins

Fix a finite conjugation-stable group \(\Theta\) of characters supported on \(S\), containing the numerator, denominator, and fixed phase presentations needed for the chosen target. For a sixth-power-free row having a prime factor outside \(S\), define

\[
\mathcal X(u)=\{\nu\psi_u^{\pm1}:\nu\in\Theta\}.
\]

Every member is nonprincipal: a good prime of valuation \(1,\ldots,5\) in \(u\) has nontrivial tame inertia. Its primitive conductor norm is \(O_S(q_u)\).

Let \(a_*=51/100\), take a small buffer \(e>0\), and put \(I=\lceil1/e\rceil+2\). For a height \(T\), let \(B_j(u)\) be the maximum of \(a_*\) and the real parts of zeros of members of \(\mathcal X(u)\) at height at most \(3^jT\). Some \(i<I\) satisfies \(B_{i+1}-B_i\le e\). Round \(B_i\) down to the \(e\)-grid, obtaining \(a\), so that

\[
a\le B_i<a+e,\qquad B_{i+1}<a+2e.
\tag{B0.13}
\]

There are only finitely many labels, independently of \(U\). A nonfloor bin supplies an actual zero \(\rho=\sigma+i\gamma\), with \(a\le\sigma<a+e\), \(|\gamma|\le3^iT\). Put \(\delta=2a-1\). The floor bin is counted trivially.

Here is the analytic estimate used in these bins. The functional equation and Euler convergence give a polynomial conductor-height bound for \(L_{\mathbb K}\) on a fixed strip. In a zero-free disk about \(2+it\), continue its Euler logarithm. Borel–Carathéodory bounds the logarithm by \(O_e(\log(Q(3+|t|)^2))\) on a slightly smaller disk; it is bounded on the concentric radius \(49/100\) by Euler convergence. Three circles gives a bound of the form \(O_e((\log(Q(3+|t|)^2))^{\theta_e})\), with \(\theta_e<1\), on a disk smaller by another fixed buffer. Exponentiating either sign yields

\[
|L_{\mathbb K}(s,\varphi)|+|L_{\mathbb K}(s,\varphi)^{-1}|
\ll_{e,\varepsilon}\{2Q(3+|t|)^2\}^{\varepsilon}
\tag{B0.14}
\]

on the retained zero-free region. Cauchy's formula gives the corresponding bounds for finitely many derivatives of \(\log L_{\mathbb K}\). A principal pole is handled by applying the logarithm argument to \((s-1)\zeta_{\mathbb K}(s)/(s+1)\).

Deleting primes of radical norm \(O_S(U)\) costs \(U^\varepsilon\) on a fixed positive half-plane. On \(\Re s\ge-v\), the direct deleted product costs \(U^{v+\varepsilon}\). These follow primewise from \(\log|1-z|^{\pm1}=O(|z|)\), treating a fixed finite set separately.

Mellin inversion, (B0.14), and the primitive functional equation give, for the required bounded real powers and retained heights,

\[
|M_u(U^r)|^2\ll U^{\delta r+\varepsilon_0},\qquad
|S_u(U^m)|^2\ll U^{\delta\min(m,1-m)+\varepsilon_0}.
\tag{B0.15}
\]

For the inverse polynomial, move the retained Mellin segment only to \(\Re s=a+6e\). For the plain polynomial, use either that line or \(1-a-6e\); reflection supplies \(U^{a-1/2+O(e)}\) on the second line. This gives exactly the two exponents in (B0.15). The original character zeros are restored as deleted Euler factors, not removed from the polynomials.

For a centrally normalized smooth prime polynomial of length \(P\), the same logarithm estimate and the Dirichlet series of \(-L'/L\) give

\[
\left|P^{-1/2}\sum_{\mathfrak p}\overline{\psi_u(\mathfrak p)}
w(q_{\mathfrak p}/P)(q_{\mathfrak p}/P)^{it}\right|
\ll P^{\delta/2+O(e)+\varepsilon}U^\varepsilon(1+T)^A.
\tag{B0.16}
\]

Insert the factor \(1/\log q_{\mathfrak p}\) into the smooth test after using \(-L'/L\). Prime powers contribute \(O(P^{1/2+\varepsilon})\) before central normalization and are harmless. Primes in the fixed exclusion are removed; the row's nonunit zeros remain. Formula (B0.16) needs only the numerator presentation and its conjugate, both included in \(\mathcal X(u)\).

For precision about heights, first fix the real losses and smooth orders. On a retained segment allocate a fixed fraction of \(T\) to each of the finitely many independent height coordinates. Outside it, leave reciprocal contours on an absolute or globally zero-free line. The discarded tails are \(O(U^BT^{-N})\), with \(B\) fixed before \(N\). Taking \(U^{\tau_-}\le T\le U^{\tau_+}\), with fixed sufficiently small positive exponents, makes the retained bounds and discarded tails compatible. The final choices in §B0.7 impose these requirements simultaneously.
title: Buffered zero bins

def CommonProbeConstructionGoalAt (b0 : ℝ) : Prop :=
  b0 < HeckeZeroSupremum.beta → ∃omega saving : ℝ,
    0 < omega ∧ omega < HeckeZeroSupremum.beta-b0 ∧ 0 < saving ∧
    ∀η : Character, FiniteFourier.IsPrimitiveOnIdeals η.residue →
      ∃χ : Character, ∃correction : ℂ → ℂ, ∃probe : ℝ → ℂ,
        (∀I,idealCoeff χ I = if IsCoprime I χ.modulus then idealCoeff η I else 0) ∧
        AnalyticOnNhd ℂ correction {s : ℂ | b0 < s.re} ∧
        (∀s : ℂ,b0 < s.re → ‖correction s-1‖ ≤ 1/2) ∧
        probe =O[atTop] (fun Z : ℝ => Z ^ (b0-11/16+omega)) ∧
        (fun Z => probe Z-HeckeSignal.signal χ correction (-11/16) Z) =O[atTop]
          (fun Z : ℝ => Z ^ (HeckeZeroSupremum.beta-11/16-saving))

end
end OAI.SevenEighths.HighFrontierTargets

statement:
### A.4. Finite Fourier correlations

For arbitrary primary moduli, distinguish the normalized Gauss sum from the ray phase:

\[
\mathfrak g(a,h)=q_a^{-1/2}\sum_{x\bmod a}\chi_a(x)e(hx/a),\qquad \mathfrak g(1,h)=1.
\]

For a good prime \(p\), \(P=q_p\), and \(j\ge1\), the direct lift \(x=x_0+py\) gives

\[
|\mathfrak g(p^j,h)|=P^{(j-1)/2}\mathbf1_{v_p(h)=j-1}\quad(6\nmid j),
\]

\[
\mathfrak g(p^j,h)=P^{j/2}\mathbf1_{p^j\mid h}
 -P^{j/2-1}\mathbf1_{p^{j-1}\mid h}\quad(6\mid j).
\tag{A.12}
\]

Here \(v_p(0)=\infty\); a sixth-power character retains its coprimality mask.

Define the full correlation

\[
F(u,v;j)=\sum_{\substack{x\bmod u,\ y\bmod v\\vx-uy\equiv j\pmod{uv}}}
 \chi_u(x)\overline{\chi_v(y)}.
\tag{A.13}
\]

Additive orthogonality, with the minus sign in the Fourier factor, gives the exact identity

\[
F(u,v;j)=\frac1{\sqrt{q_uq_v}}
 \sum_{h\bmod uv}\mathfrak g(u,h)\overline{\mathfrak g(v,h)}e(-jh/(uv)).
\tag{A.14}
\]

At \(j=0\), a nonzero summand has both residues units. The congruence then forces \(u\mid v\) and \(v\mid u\). Hence

\[
F(u,v;0)=\mathbf1_{u=v}\phi(u).
\tag{A.15}
\]

For complete common-support extraction, let

\[
u=Da,\quad v=Eb,\quad (a,b)=1,\quad (ab,DE)=1,
\]

where every prime of \(D\) also divides \(E\), and conversely. Then

\[
F(Da,Eb;j)=F(D,E;j)R(a,E)R(b,D)R(a,b)
 \chi_a(j)\overline{\chi_b(-j)}.
\tag{A.16}
\]

To verify the phases, reduction at primes of \(a,b\) gives
\(\chi_a(j)\overline{\chi_a(Eb)}\) and
\(\overline{\chi_b(-j)}\chi_b(Da)\). At the common primes, put
\(x'=bx\), \(y'=ay\). The remaining scalar is
\(\overline{\chi_D(b)}\chi_E(a)\). The three unit quotients combine to the displayed three factors of \(R\). Every inversion here is at a unit. If \(j\) is a nonunit, the displayed zero symbols are retained; the congruence calculation gives the same zero.

The exact common-prime correlations needed for estimates follow from (A.13). At a prime of common multiplicities \(i,j\), the correlation vanishes unless \(p^{\min(i,j)}\mid h\). Write the divided frequency as \(k\). For \(i=j\), its local value is

\[
P^{i-1}\begin{cases}
P-1,&p\mid k,\\
-1,&p\nmid k,\ 6\nmid i,\\
P-2,&p\nmid k,\ 6\mid i.
\end{cases}
\tag{A.17}
\]

For \(i>j\), it vanishes unless \(6\mid j\) and \(p\nmid k\), in which case it is

\[
P^{j-1}(P-1)\chi_p(k)^{i-j}.
\tag{A.18}
\]

The case \(j>i\) follows by conjugating and changing the sign of the frequency. These are finite-field sums: after division by the common power, one variable is fixed if the multiplicities differ; for equal multiplicities one obtains a multiplicative-character sum over \(\mathbb F_P^\times\setminus\{1\}\).

**Artificial extension rule.** Formula (A.16) is not an identity on newly noncoprime residual pairs. When separating such pairs, define its right side on all individually allowed \(a,b\), and first insert the complete finite Möbius identity

\[
\sum_{(a,b)=1}c(a,b)F(Da,Eb;j)
=\sum_t\mu(t)\sum_{t\mid a,b}c(a,b)\widetilde F_{D,E}(a,b;j).
\tag{A.19}
\]

The complete divisor sum kills the artificial pairs before factorwise estimates. Its extra primes are not part of the genuine common support and inherit none of its valuation restrictions.
title: A.4. Finite Fourier correlations

    (hδ : 0<δ) (hδ' : δ≤1) (hr : (17/50:ℝ)≤r) (hr' : 8/5+δ < r) (hζ : 0<ζ)
    (ha : 0 < a) (hb : 0 < b) (hB : 0≤B)
    (S : Finset (Ideal O)) (hS : SourceExclusions S) (hmax : ∀P∈S,P.IsMaximal)
    (hfirst : FirstTail (1/4) S)
    (W0 W1 : SchwartzMap ℝ ℂ) (a0 b0 a1 b1 : ℝ) (ha0 : 0 < a0) (ha1 : 0 < a1)
    (hW0 : Function.support W0⊆Icc a0 b0) (hW1 : Function.support W1⊆Icc a1 b1) :
    ∃C : ℝ,0 < C ∧ ∀(η : Character) (Z : ℝ),1≤Z → ∀R : ℕ→Finset FreeRow,
      (∀n u,u∈R n → u.val≠1 ∧ Z^((Cycle25.h:ℝ)+ζ)*(2:ℝ)^n≤((Ideal.span {u.val}:Ideal O).absNorm:ℝ) ∧
        ((Ideal.span {u.val}:Ideal O).absNorm:ℝ)≤2*(Z^((Cycle25.h:ℝ)+ζ)*(2:ℝ)^n)) →
      ∀(T : Fin K→Finset ProbePhysical.PrimeIdeal) (hT : ∀i P,P∈T i→P.val∉S),
      (∀P:(∀i,T i),Function.Injective (fun i=>(P i).val)) →
      ∀length : Fin K→ℝ,(∀i,0≤length i) → (∑i,length i)=(Cycle25.ell:ℝ) →
      ∀W : Fin K→ℝ→ℂ,(∀i,Function.support (W i)⊆Icc a b) → (∀i y,‖W i y‖≤B) →
      Summable (fun n=>absolutePhysicalDyadIntegral S hS hmax η (R n) T hT W (fun i=>Z^(length i)) W0 W1
        (Z^(Cycle25.lx:ℝ)) (Z^(Cycle25.ly:ℝ)) Z 2 2 r) ∧
      (∑'n,absolutePhysicalDyadIntegral S hS hmax η (R n) T hT W (fun i=>Z^(length i)) W0 W1
        (Z^(Cycle25.lx:ℝ)) (Z^(Cycle25.ly:ℝ)) Z 2 2 r)
      ≤C*(η.modulus.absNorm:ℝ)^δ*Z^((1+Cycle25.lx/2+Cycle25.ly)+((Cycle25.h:ℝ)+ζ)*(8/5+δ)-ζ*r)

theorem fixed_induced_mixed (a b ε B Q : ℝ) (ha : 0 < a) (hε : 0 < ε)
    (hB : 0 ≤ B) (hQ : 0 < Q) :
    ∃ S : Finset (ℕ × ℕ), ∃ C : ℝ, 0 < C ∧
      ∀ (W₁ W₂ : 𝓢(ℝ, ℂ)), Function.support (W₁ : ℝ → ℂ) ⊆ Set.Icc a b →
        Function.support (W₂ : ℝ → ℂ) ⊆ Set.Icc a b →
      ∀ (χ ψ : O → Character) (r : Radial) (R : Ideal O) (Z m X₁ X₂ : ℝ),
        R ≠ 0 → 1 ≤ Z → 0 ≤ m → r.scale = Z ^ m → 0 < X₁ → 0 < X₂ →
        (∀ z, r.keep z → CenteredExceptionalProfile.InducedBy (χ z) (ψ z)) →
        (∀ z, r.keep z → (ψ z).residue ≠ 1) →
        (∀ z, r.keep z → ((ψ z).modulus.absNorm : ℝ) ≤ Q) →
        (∀ z, r.keep z → (((χ z).modulus * R).radical.absNorm : ℝ) ≤ Z ^ B) →
        radialEnergy (fun z => polynomial (excluded (χ z) R) false W₁ X₁ 0 0 *
          polynomial (excluded (χ z) R) false W₂ X₂ 0 0) r.keep r.profile r.scale ≤
          C * diagonalControl r.profile *
            ((S.sup (schwartzSeminormFamily ℝ ℝ ℂ) W₁) *
             (S.sup (schwartzSeminormFamily ℝ ℝ ℂ) W₂)) ^ 2 * Z ^ (m + ε)

    (0 < along ∧ reflected+short+z ≤ 5*M/6 ∧
      reflected+short+6*kappa*z ≤ M)

      polynomial (excluded (χ z) R) false
        (normPowerProfile W₂ a b ha hs₂ (W₂.smooth ⊤) t₂) X₂ 0 0) r.keep r.profile r.scale =
    radialEnergy (fun z => polynomial (excluded (χ z) R) false W₁ X₁ 0 t₁ *
      polynomial (excluded (χ z) R) false W₂ X₂ 0 t₂) r.keep r.profile r.scale

    (e : ℝ) (he : 0 < e) (he' : e<1/1000)
    (S : Finset (Ideal O)) (hS : SourceExclusions S) (hmax : ∀P∈S,P.IsMaximal)

    (W0 W1 : SchwartzMap ℝ ℂ) (a0 b0 a1 b1 : ℝ) (ha0 : 0 < a0) (ha1 : 0 < a1)
    (hW0 : Function.support W0⊆Icc a0 b0) (hW1 : Function.support W1⊆Icc a1 b1) :
    ∃C : ℝ,0≤C ∧ ∀(η : Character) (Z : ℝ),1≤Z → ∀R : Finset FreeRow,
      (∀u∈R,u.val≠1 ∧ ((Ideal.span {u.val}:Ideal O).absNorm:ℝ)≤Z^((Cycle25.h:ℝ)+ζ)) →
      ∀(T : Fin K→Finset ProbePhysical.PrimeIdeal) (hT : ∀i P,P∈T i → P.val∉S),
      (∀P:(∀i,T i),Function.Injective (fun i=>(P i).val)) →
      ∀length : Fin K→ℝ,(∑j,length j)=(Cycle25.ell:ℝ) →
      (∀j P,P∈T j → (P.val.absNorm:ℝ)≤b*Z^(length j)) →
      ∀W : Fin K→ℝ→ℂ,(∀j y,‖W j y‖≤A) →
      ∀(a B H : FreeRow→ℝ) (idx : FreeRow→ℕ) (ψ : FreeRow→ι→Character),

        detectorMaximum (sourceDetectorFamily S hS.prime η u (ψ u)) (3*(idx u+1:ℕ)*B u) < a u+2*e) →
      ‖finitePhysicalRows S hmax η R T W (fun j=>Z^(length j)) W0 W1 (Z^(Cycle25.lx:ℝ)) (Z^(Cycle25.ly:ℝ)) Z-
        finiteCentralCubeRows S hS hmax η R T hT W (fun j=>Z^(length j)) W0 W1
          (Z^(Cycle25.lx:ℝ)) (Z^(Cycle25.ly:ℝ)) Z e a H‖≤C*(η.modulus.absNorm:ℝ)^2*Z^(-saving)

statement:
#### The principal term

(B0.27), the normalization in (B0.36), and (B0.45) give

\[
J_\eta(Z)\ll Z^{b_0-k+\varepsilon}.
\tag{B0.50}
\]

We will prove, for some fixed \(\Delta>0\) independent of \(\eta\),

\[
J_\eta(Z)-f_\eta(Z)\ll_\eta Z^{\beta_*-k-\Delta}.
\tag{B0.51}
\]

Consider first \(u=1\) in the compensated version of (B0.28). Move to
\((\Re s,\Re w,\Re z)=(\beta_*+e,1+e,1/6+e)\). The global line for \(s\) is zero-free by definition and (B0.14). Move \(w\) to \(3/4\), crossing only the simple numerator pole at one. In its residue, move \(z\) to \(1/8\), crossing only the simple pole at \(1/6\). The local product and replacement are holomorphic on the full principal box following (B0.34). The Mellin transform \(\mathscr M\) has no pole in these positive strips.

Equations (B0.35)–(B0.36) identify the double residue, including both residue scalars. Substitute the prime-product approximation following (B0.35) on the global \(s\)-line before replacing its main integral by the line \(\Re s=2\). The latter move crosses no singularity. Its main term is exactly \(f_\eta\). The two contour remainders and the error in the residue approximation are respectively

\[
O_\eta\!\left(
 Z^{\beta_*-k-y/4+O(e)+\varepsilon}
+Z^{\beta_*-k-h/24+O(e)+\varepsilon}
+Z^{\beta_*-k-\mu_P+O(e)+\varepsilon}
\right).
\tag{B0.52}
\]

For the first two bounds use the quotient-free correction on the principal box, with size \(O(Z^{\ell\Re z+\varepsilon})\); the remaining geometric exponents are \(y(\Re w-1)\) and \(h(\Re z-1/6)\). The third bound uses the prime-product approximation following (B0.35) only on its stated residue locus. In particular a \(Q^{-7/8}\) approximation has not been used below its permissible line.
title: The principal term

statement:
def AllNaturalMixedAt (a b radial B Bfixed L Mcap ε Z : ℝ)
    (J : ℕ) (S : Finset (ℕ × ℕ)) (C : ℝ) : Prop :=
  ∀ s : NaturalPlainState Z B radial 1, s.width ≤ Mcap →
    (s.puncture.absNorm : ℝ) ≤ Z ^ B →
    (∀ z, s.radial.keep z →
      ((excluded (naturalPlainCharacter s.character z) s.puncture).modulus.radical.absNorm : ℝ) ≤ Z ^ Bfixed) →
    ∀ W₁ W₂ : 𝓢(ℝ, ℂ), Function.support (W₁ : ℝ → ℂ) ⊆ Set.Icc a b →
      Function.support (W₂ : ℝ → ℂ) ⊆ Set.Icc a b →
    ∀ X₁ X₂ t₁ t₂ : ℝ, 0 < X₁ → 0 < X₂ → X₁ ≤ Z ^ L → X₂ ≤ Z ^ L →
    s.energy W₁ W₂ X₁ X₂ t₁ t₂ ≤
      C * diagonalControl s.radial.profile *
        ((S.sup (schwartzSeminormFamily ℝ ℝ ℂ) W₁) *
         (S.sup (schwartzSeminormFamily ℝ ℝ ℂ) W₂)) ^ 2 *
        (1 + ‖t₁‖) ^ J * (1 + ‖t₂‖) ^ J * Z ^ (s.width + ε)
title: AllNaturalMixedAt

theorem adaptive_source_count_from_raw_moments_wide
    (M : Ideal O) [NeZero M] (H : Subgroup (O ⧸ M)ˣ)
    (hH : RayOrthogonality.globalUnits M ≤ H) (S : Finset (Ideal O))
    (φ : ℝ → ℝ) (hφ : ContDiff ℝ ∞ φ) (hφc : HasCompactSupport φ)

statement:
### B.1. Cubic reflection

For arbitrary element rows, write \(k=u_0k_Sk_{\rm good}\). The unit, the valuations at \(S\) modulo six, and the good row's finite ray class leave only finitely many characters
\(\nu(A)\chi_A(u_0k_S)R(A,k_{\rm good})\).
The local good-prime exponents carry all remaining dependence. Thus the fixed modulus in the following reflection is selected before any good row prime varies; no moving prime enters it.

Let \(\nu_0\) belong to a fixed finite collection of ray characters, with their prescribed zero extensions. At finitely many good primes choose \(j_{\mathfrak p}\in\{0,\ldots,5\}\), and put \(\Psi(A)=\nu_0(A)\prod_{\mathfrak p}\chi_{\mathfrak p}(A)^{j_{\mathfrak p}}\). Define
\[
\mathcal C_V(X;\Psi)=
\sum_{n\ \mathrm{sf},b}
\frac{\gamma_2(n)\overline{\alpha(nb^3)}\Psi(nb^3)}{\sqrt{q_n}\,q_b}
V(q_nq_b^3/X).
\tag{B.1}
\]
**Proposition B.1 (cubic reflection).** For annular \(V\), or the Gaussian used in the probe, this sum is a divisor-bounded finite sum of branches
\[
\zeta\sum_{\mu\ne0}\frac{d(\mu)\alpha(\mu)\vartheta(\lambda^4\mu)}{\sqrt{q_\mu}}
\prod_{\mathfrak p\in A}B_{\mathfrak p,j_{\mathfrak p}}(\lambda^4\mu)
V^\sharp\!\left(\frac{q_\mu X}{q_{c_F}^{2}q_r^{2}}\right),
\quad r=\prod_{\mathfrak p\in A}\mathfrak p,
\tag{B.2}
\]
where \(c_F\) has finitely many fixed possibilities and the local factors are
\[
B_{\mathfrak p,j}(x)=
\begin{cases}
\chi_{\mathfrak p}(x)^{-j-2},&j\notin\{0,4\},\\
q_{\mathfrak p}^{-1/2}(-1+q_{\mathfrak p}1_{\mathfrak p\mid x}),&j=4,\\
q_{\mathfrak p}^{-1/2}\chi_{\mathfrak p}(x)^{-2},&j=0\text{ active}.
\end{cases}
\tag{B.3}
\]
Every nonzero exponent is active. An exponent-zero prime also has an inactive branch with scalar \(1-q_{\mathfrak p}^{-1}\), in which it is absent from \(r\).

The branch scalar, needed when the prime varies, is
\[
\zeta=-\frac{i}{81}\overline{\alpha(c)}^{\,2}\widehat\phi(h_0)
\overline{\kappa_F}
\prod_{\mathfrak p\in I}(1-q_{\mathfrak p}^{-1})
\prod_{\mathfrak p\in A}\chi_{\mathfrak p}(\sigma_{\mathfrak p})^{-2}
\omega_{\mathfrak p,j_{\mathfrak p}},\qquad c=c_Fr,
\tag{B.4}
\]
where \(I\) is the inactive set, \(\widehat\phi\) is the normalized fixed-modulus Fourier coefficient used below, and
\[
\begin{gathered}
\sigma_{\mathfrak p}=\lambda^2c/\mathfrak p,\qquad
\epsilon_{\mathfrak p}=-\bigl((\lambda^3c/\mathfrak p)\sigma_{\mathfrak p}\bigr)^{-1}
\pmod{\mathfrak p},\\
\omega_{\mathfrak p,j}=
\begin{cases}
\chi_{\mathfrak p}(-1)^j\gamma_j(\mathfrak p)\gamma_{j+2}(\mathfrak p)
\chi_{\mathfrak p}(\epsilon_{\mathfrak p})^{-j-2},&j\notin\{0,4\},\\
\gamma_4(\mathfrak p),&j=4,\\
-\gamma_2(\mathfrak p)\chi_{\mathfrak p}(\epsilon_{\mathfrak p})^{-2},&j=0.
\end{cases}
\end{gathered}
\]
The inverse is taken in the residue field; its argument is a unit. Each \(\omega_{\mathfrak p,j}\) has modulus one, so \(|\zeta|\le1/81\).
The three fixed cusp sequences are supported on
\[
\mu=u\lambda^mnb^3,\qquad m\ge-4,
\qquad |d(u\lambda^mnb^3)|\le27\,3^{m/6}\sqrt{q_b}.
\tag{B.5}
\]
Here the dual ideals \(n,b\) are primary and prime to \(\lambda\), \(n\) is squarefree, and they may share primes and meet \(S\). They do not carry the primal \(S\)-exclusion. After the active radical is fixed modulo one fixed ray modulus, \(d\), \(\vartheta\), and \(c_F\) are independent of its moving primes. Only a bounded scalar and the displayed local characters vary with that radical.

With \(\widehat V(t)=\int_0^\infty V(x)x^t\,dx/x\), the exact transform is
\[
V^\sharp(y)=\frac1{2\pi i}\int_{(0)}\widehat V(-t)
\prod_{\pm}\frac{\Gamma(1+t\pm1/6)}{\Gamma(1-t\pm1/6)}
\left(\frac{(2\pi)^4y}{27}\right)^{-t}\,dt.
\tag{B.6}
\]
For \(V(y)=y^{1/2}W(y)\), with annular \(W\), every fixed \(A,j\) has a finite \(J\) such that
\[
|(y\partial_y)^jV^\sharp(y)|
\ll_{A,j}\|W\|_{C^J}\min(y^{1/4},y^{-A}).
\tag{B.7}
\]
The same bound holds for \(V_G\), with a fixed constant in place of the annular seminorm.

**Proof.** We derive the reflection from the classical cubic-theta automorphy and cusp expansions [DR, §5 and Appendix A]. Write \(\check e(z)=e(\lambda z)\) and \(L(t)=\left(\begin{smallmatrix}1&0\\t&1\end{smallmatrix}\right)\). Here \(\Gamma_1(3)=\{g\in\operatorname{SL}_2(\mathcal O):g\equiv I\pmod3\}\). Its theta multiplier is \(\kappa(\left(\begin{smallmatrix}a&b\\c&d\end{smallmatrix}\right))=(c/a)_3\) for \(c\ne0\), and one otherwise; it extends to \(\operatorname{SL}_2(\mathbf Z)\Gamma_1(3)\) by taking value one on \(\operatorname{SL}_2(\mathbf Z)\). The conjugate theta expansion has coefficient \(3^{5/2}|b|\chi_n(\lambda)^{-2}\gamma_2(n)\) at \(\lambda^{-3}nb^3\), and constant term \(3^{5/2}v^{2/3}/2\). At \(I,L(\lambda),L(-\lambda)\), the conjugate expansions are
\[
\sigma_Hv^{2/3}+\sum_{\mu\ne0}d_H(\mu)vK_{1/3}(4\pi|\mu|v)\check e(\mu z).
\tag{B.8}
\]
These three published cusp expansions give (B.5). We derive their twisted reflection here; no prime-sum asymptotic is used.

Choose a fixed modulus \(L\) containing the primary condition, supplementary conditions and fixed conductors. Call the periodic function \(\chi_x(\lambda)^2\nu_0(x)\), with its prescribed primary and nonunit zeros, \(\phi(x)\), and set \(\widehat\phi(h_0)=q_L^{-1}\sum_{x\bmod L}\phi(x)e(-h_0x/L)\). Expand it additively modulo \(L\). At a moving prime, the Fourier coefficient is
\[
q^{-1}\sum_{x\bmod\mathfrak p}\chi_{\mathfrak p}(x)^j e(-hx/\mathfrak p)
=\begin{cases}
q^{-1/2}\tau^-_{\mathfrak p,j}\chi_{\mathfrak p}(h)^{-j},&j\ne0, h\ne0,\\
0,&j\ne0, h=0,\\
-q^{-1},&j=0, h\ne0,\\
1-q^{-1},&j=0, h=0,
\end{cases}
\tag{B.9}
\]
with \(|\tau^-_{\mathfrak p,j}|=1\). An active branch therefore translates by
\(z_h=\lambda^2(h_0/L+\sum_{\mathfrak p\mid r}h_{\mathfrak p}/\mathfrak p)\), with all \(h_{\mathfrak p}\ne0\).

Reduce \(\lambda^2h_0/L=a_F/c_F\). Normalize by a unit so that \(a_F\equiv1\pmod3\) when \(\lambda\mid c_F\), and \(c_F\equiv1\pmod3\) otherwise. Then
\[
c=c_Fr,\qquad a=a_Fr+\lambda^2c_F\sum_{\mathfrak p\mid r}(r/\mathfrak p)h_{\mathfrak p},
\qquad z_h=a/c.
\]
Fix \(r\) modulo \(M^2\), where \(M=\lambda^{12}L^4\), and choose the lifts \(h_{\mathfrak p}\) to be zero modulo \(M^2\). Complete \((a,c)\) to \(g=\left(\begin{smallmatrix}a&b_0\\c&\delta\end{smallmatrix}\right)\), choosing \(\delta\equiv a^{-1}\) to the required depth at primes of \(c_F\), \(\delta\equiv0\) at primes of \(M\) not dividing \(c_F\), and \(\delta\equiv a^{-1}\pmod{\mathfrak p}\) for \(\mathfrak p\mid r\). Choose
\[
H=\begin{cases}
I,&3\mid c,\\
L(u_0),\quad u_0\in\{\lambda,-\lambda\},\ u_0\equiv c\pmod3,
&v_\lambda(c)=1,\\
EL(-u_0),\quad u_0\equiv a\pmod3,&(c,\lambda)=1,
\end{cases}
\qquad E=\begin{pmatrix}0&-1\\1&0\end{pmatrix}.
\]
In the last case \(u_0\) is chosen from a fixed set of representatives of \(\mathcal O/3\mathcal O\), not just \(\{\pm\lambda\}\). The congruences above give \(gH^{-1}\equiv I\pmod3\). The trivial multipliers on \(\operatorname{SL}_2(\mathbf Z)\) and translations by \(\mathbf Z+3\mathcal O\) reduce the last case to the same three cusp expansions.

Reciprocity in the multiplier gives
\(\kappa(gH^{-1})=\kappa_F\prod_{\mathfrak p\mid r}\chi_{\mathfrak p}(a)^2\), with \(\kappa_F\) fixed in this sector. The fixed-prime expressions in the three cases are \((c_F/a)_3\), \((-u_0/(a-u_0b_0))_3((c_F/u_0)/a)_3\), and \((a/c_F)_3\), respectively. They contain no residual column.

The coordinate formula
\[
g^{-1}(a/c+z,v)=
\left(-\frac\delta c-\frac{\bar z}{c^2(|z|^2+v^2)},
\frac v{q_c(|z|^2+v^2)}\right)
\tag{B.10}
\]
shows that differentiation by \(\partial_{\bar z}\) at zero kills the constant term and contributes exactly \(-(cv)^{-2}\partial_{z'}\). Put \(x=\lambda^4\mu\) and \(f=\lambda^3c_F\). Additive CRT expresses the translated phase as
\[
\check e(-\delta\mu/c)=\vartheta(x)
\prod_{\mathfrak p\mid r}e(\epsilon_{\mathfrak p}h_{\mathfrak p}^{-1}x/\mathfrak p),
\quad \vartheta(x)=e(-\delta_Fr^{-1}x/f),
\quad\epsilon_{\mathfrak p}\equiv-(\lambda^5c_F^2(r/\mathfrak p)^2)^{-1}\pmod{\mathfrak p}.
\]
Conjugating the theta multiplier contributes \(\chi_{\mathfrak p}(h_{\mathfrak p})^{-2}\). After \(y=h_{\mathfrak p}^{-1}\), the exponent is \(j+2\); the resulting Gauss or Ramanujan sum is exactly (B.3), including its zeros. The normalized Gauss sums in this calculation give exactly the factors \(\omega_{\mathfrak p,j}\) and the scalar (B.4). This records their dependence on the entire active conductor; it is not an arbitrary row-dependent coefficient.

To check the archimedean normalization, define
\[
\mathcal D_\Psi(s)=\sum_{n\ {\rm sf},b}\gamma_2(n)\overline{\alpha(nb^3)}\Psi(nb^3)q_n^{-s}q_b^{1/2-3s}.
\]
Let \(\Theta_\Psi\) be the conjugate theta series with its \(\mu\)-coefficient multiplied by \(\phi(\lambda^3\mu)\prod_{\mathfrak p}\chi_{\mathfrak p}(\lambda^3\mu)^{j_{\mathfrak p}}\). Differentiation supplies \(2\pi i\overline\mu\), and
\[
\int_0^\infty v^{2s}K_{1/3}(4\pi|\mu|v)\,dv
=\frac{2^{2s-1}\Gamma(s+1/3)\Gamma(s+2/3)}{(4\pi|\mu|)^{2s+1}}.
\]
Consequently, initially for \(\Re s>1\),
\[
\int_0^\infty\partial_{\bar z}\Theta_\Psi(0,v)v^{2s-1}\,dv
=\frac{3^{5/2}}4\left(\frac{27}{(2\pi)^2}\right)^s
\Gamma(s+1/3)\Gamma(s+2/3)\mathcal D_\Psi(s).
\]
Apply (B.10) to this integral. Changing height to \(1/(q_cv)\) contributes \(-c^{-2}q_c^{1-2t}\); its factor \(c^{-2}q_c\) has modulus one. Dividing by the direct Mellin factor and replacing \(t\) by \(-t\) yields (B.6) and the scalar \(1/81\). The differentiated cusp expansions decay at both height endpoints. Their Mellin integrals are entire; the direct and reflected absolute-convergence half-planes, Stirling and Phragmén–Lindelöf give polynomial bounds on intervening vertical strips. Rapid test decay therefore justifies the contour shifts; moving to \(\Re t=-1/4\) crosses no gamma pole and gives the small-\(y\) bound, while any positive line gives rapid decay at infinity. This proves the reflection, its scalar, and (B.2)–(B.7) with finite seminorm control. ∎

statement:
### D.7. Closing the finite descent

Choose a small width floor \(\rho>0\), a step \(\sigma>0\), and then padding \(\xi>0\). At \(M\le\rho\), reflection reduces to (D.8), and absolute counting gives an excess at most \(\rho+2\xi\). Above the floor, the descent (D.19) decreases width by \(\sigma\) before the fixed small frequency enclosure. Taking \(\xi\ll\sigma\) makes the actual decrease at least \(\sigma/2\). On bounded initial widths there are at most \(D=2+\lceil2M_{\max}/\sigma\rceil\) stages along any branch.

Within each width band, prove the uncentered range first, then the centered core, then use reflection for arbitrary lengths, and finally use (D.5) for extra punctures. The comparison uses the earlier uncentered range at the same width with a positive margin; all nonexceptional children call a strictly smaller completed band. There is no same-band cycle.

Choose \(\rho,\sigma\) so that the largest terminal loss, among the width-floor, diagonal, and exceptional estimates, is below \(\epsilon/4\). Choose \(\xi\) and every local divisor/Schwartz power loss below a sufficiently small multiple of \(\epsilon/D\). Triangle inequalities take a maximum of child exponents after the stated counting mass, and Cauchy averages the two child exponents. A branch therefore incurs only one terminal loss, plus the small edge losses; terminal losses are not added at every ancestor.

For uniformity, measure extracted powers before dyadic rounding. At each stage keep joint log-norm boxes, selecting whole frequency dyads from the supremum of the nominal scale over the outer box, with padding \(Z^{\xi/2}\). Selection is independent of live columns. On discarded dyads the genuine Poisson argument is at least \(Z^{\xi/4}\). The bounds \(|\mathfrak g(a,h)|\le\sqrt{q_a}\), \(|F(u,v;j)|\le q_uq_v\), and polynomial raw counts make their total arbitrarily small by Schwartz decay, before Fourier separation.

On retained boxes, the kernel \(\widehat\Phi(R\exp L(x))\) has uniformly bounded Euler derivatives for every \(R>0\). Its common Fourier measure has finite weighted \(L^1\) norm; heights are integrated against it. Remove central powers before separating inverse roots. Fixed support enlargements over finite depth cause only \(O(1/\log Z)\) shifts. Rescale subunit annuli only inside nonnegative child norms; never clip formal centered scales. The character and common-mask closure follows from (D.10), (A.16), and (D.22), with polynomial mask norms over finite depth. Choose seminorm and height orders backwards through the descent, then thresholds and external tail orders. This proves (D.3). ∎

Taking no moving twist, a fixed finite-order character, and two copies of the same profile proves (3.3). Restricting the nonnegative row sum to sixth-power-free rows only decreases it. The inverse orientation follows by conjugating the entire polynomial.

statement:
### Continuation criterion

The criterion is valid.

The important points are all present:

1. The two comparison estimates give a common exponent \(C(b_*)\) with
   \[
   \theta<b_*<B.
   \]
2. Moving the defining contour right gives arbitrary power decay as \(Z\downarrow0\).
3. These endpoint estimates give a holomorphic Mellin transform on \(\Re s>b_*\).
4. Fourier inversion identifies that transform on the original line.
5. Meromorphic continuation yields the identity with \(L_F^S\).
6. The nonvanishing right side excludes zeros throughout the enlarged half-plane.

No supremum is assumed to be attained. A principal pole does not obstruct the argument: it corresponds to a zero of the reciprocal.

The quantifiers are also correct. Target-dependent constants and starting scales are allowed; the positive saving and resulting boundary must be common, and the closure section supplies those.
title: Continuation criterion

statement:
### Correlations and Gram estimate

The finite correlation identities include prime powers and zero-extended principal powers.

The artificial extension off the genuine residual-coprime locus is explicitly defined as artificial. The full Möbius indicator is inserted before it is used in a factorized estimate.

The Gram argument separates mean-free frequencies from sixth-power-type frequencies. Its final three terms
\[
1,\qquad P_a^{1/6},\qquad P_a^2/Y'
\]
have distinct justifications. The physical geometry supplies the inequality needed to absorb the third into the second.

---

statement:
### 1.2. Smooth weights and uniformity

An annular weight is smooth with compact support in \((0,\infty)\); its Mellin transform is \(\widehat W(s)=\int_0^\infty W(y)y^s\,dy/y\). Implied constants may depend on fixed characters, supports and positive losses, but not on moving arithmetic labels. Real exponents range over fixed bounded sets. Every estimate has finite smooth-seminorm control; multiplying a test by \(y^{b+it}\), with bounded \(b\), costs a fixed power of \(1+|t|\).

We use common smooth profiles, not row-dependent arithmetic coefficients. A compactly supported joint profile in logarithmic norm coordinates has a Fourier expansion with finite weighted \(L^1\) norm, by integration by parts. Minkowski and Cauchy then reduce its row norm to norms with separated unit-modulus norm powers. In particular, if \(C_j(W)=\sum_nc_{j,n}W(x_{j,n})\) satisfies \(\sum_j|C_j(W)|^2\le M\|W\|_{C^m(I')}^2\) for every common test supported in \(I'\), then, for kernels supported in a fixed \(I^2\Subset(I')^2\),
\[
\left|\sum_jb_j\sum_{n_1,n_2}c_{j,n_1}\overline{c_{j,n_2}}
 K_j(x_{j,n_1},x_{j,n_2})\right|
 \ll M\sup_j\|K_j\|_{C^{2m+4}},\qquad |b_j|\le1.
\tag{1.4}
\]
Indeed Fourier expansion gives decay \((1+|t_1|)^{-m-2}(1+|t_2|)^{-m-2}\); the two common-test bounds leave integrable powers \(-2\). Sobolev on unit intervals in log scale, real power and height likewise permits rowwise choices of these smooth parameters, after summing the common-profile bounds. All internal smooth orders are chosen before the final external height cutoff.

statement:
### A.1. Gauss phases

For squarefree \(n\), and coprime squarefree \(a,b\), the conventions of §1.1 give

\[
\begin{gathered}
\chi_b(a)=R(a,b)\chi_a(b),\qquad R(a,b)=R(b,a)\in\{\pm1\},\quad (a,b)=1,\\
\gamma_2(n)^3=\mu(n)\alpha(n),\qquad
\gamma_1(n)\gamma_2(n)=\mu(n)\alpha(n)G(n),\\
\mu(n)\gamma_{-1}(n)=\chi_n(-1)G(n)^{-1}\overline{\alpha(n)}\gamma_2(n),\\
a_\nu(ab)=a_\nu(a)a_\nu(b)\chi_b(a)^4,
\qquad a_\nu(n)=\overline{\alpha(n)}\gamma_2(n)\nu(n),\quad (a,b)=1.
\end{gathered}
\tag{A.1}
\]

**Proof.** At a prime \(p\), write \(J(A,B)=\sum_xA(x)B(1-x)\), with zero extensions. The substitution \(u=2x-1\) gives
\(\chi_p(4)J(\chi_p,\chi_p)=J(\chi_p,\chi_p^3)\).
The Gauss–Jacobi identity and \(\gamma_2(p)\gamma_4(p)=1\) consequently give
\[
\gamma_1(p)\gamma_2(p)
=\overline{\chi_p(4)}\gamma_3(p)\gamma_2(p)^3.
\]
To evaluate the last cube, \(J(\chi_p^2,\chi_p^2)\) has norm \(q_p\) and is divisible by \(p\): expand \(x^{(q_p-1)/3}(1-x)^{(q_p-1)/3}\) modulo \(p\), and sum its powers over the residue field. Its unit is fixed by reduction modulo three. Indeed \(\prod_{x\ne0,1}x(1-x)=1\); writing the cubic character values as \(\omega^{j_x}\) gives \(\sum j_x\equiv0\pmod3\), hence the Jacobi sum is \(-1\pmod3\). Since \(p\equiv1\pmod3\), the sum is \(-p\). Thus \(\gamma_2(p)^3=-\alpha(p)\).

For odd \(c\), Gaussian-regularized Poisson summation gives
\[
|c|^{-1}\sum_{x\bmod c}e(x^2/c)
=\tfrac12\sum_{y\bmod2\mathcal O}e(-cy^2/4)=\Gamma_{\rm q}(c).
\]
One can take the regulator \(e^{-\pi\eta|z|^2}\): its transformed factor has
\(r_\eta=1+3q_c\eta^2/16\), and replacing \(r_\eta\) by one has error \(O_c(1)\). Division by the Gaussian mass \(\asymp\eta^{-1}\), followed by \(\eta\downarrow0\), proves the formula. The four square classes represented by \(1,-1,\lambda,-\lambda\) have values \(1,1,i,-i\). Their quotient is the symmetric bicharacter
\[
R((-1)^e\lambda^f,(-1)^g\lambda^h)=(-1)^{eh+fg+fh}.
\]
Grouping by \(y=x^2\) gives \(\Gamma_{\rm q}(p)=\gamma_3(p)\). Chinese remaindering and cubic reciprocity then give sextic reciprocity with this \(R\). Also \(\chi_c(4)=(-2/c)_3=(c/(-2))_3\), a fixed character modulo two. Therefore \(G(c)=\overline{\chi_c(4)}\Gamma_{\rm q}(c)\) is a fixed ray phase, and
\[
\begin{gathered}
G(ab)=G(a)G(b)R(a,b),\qquad R(a,a)=\chi_a(-1),\\
G(ba^{-1})=\chi_a(-1)\overline{G(a)}G(b)R(a,b).
\end{gathered}
\tag{A.2}
\]
Chinese remaindering extends the prime Gauss identities to squarefree indices. In particular
\(\gamma_2(ab)=\gamma_2(a)\gamma_2(b)\chi_a(b)^2\chi_b(a)^2\), which gives the multiplicative identity for \(a_\nu\). Finally \(\gamma_1(n)\gamma_{-1}(n)=\chi_n(-1)\) gives the inverse-character conversion in (A.1). Every equality preserves its nonunit zeros. ∎
title: A.1. Gauss phases

    (W0 W1 : SchwartzMap ℝ ℂ) (η : Character) (Z : ℝ) : ℂ :=
  let Yp := fun j=>Z^(ell j)
  let T := fun j=>pool (RayQuotient.identityClass M H) S a b (Yp j)
  compensatedPhysicalProbe η (calibrationForSet S hmax) W0 W1
    (fun j=>canonicalSlotSupport (T j)) (fun j y=>(W j y:ℂ)) Yp
    (Z^(747/2000:ℝ)) (Z^(919/2000:ℝ)) Z /
    (sourceResidueConstant W0 W1 (∏P∈S,P)*
      (Probe.principalScalar Finset.univ Z (167/1000) (slotMass T (residueWeights W Yp)) : ℂ))

statement:
def actualRamifiedErrorCoefficients (η : Character) (u : FreeRow) (P : PrimeIdeal)
    (hs : Supported P.val) (x z : ℂ) : CubicCoefficients :=
  let p := primaryGenerator P.val
  let hp := supported_primeGenerator_prime P hs
  letI : (Ideal.span {p} : Ideal O).IsMaximal := PrincipalIdealRing.isMaximal_of_irreducible hp.irreducible
  let hsp : Supported (Ideal.span {p}) := (span_primaryGenerator_of_supported P.val hs).symm ▸ hs
  let hg := (supported_prime_data p hp hsp).1
  ramifiedErrorCoefficients p hp hg (targetMonoid η p) (actualACube η p)
    (actualSextic (Ideal.span {p}) hg (Ideal.Quotient.mk _ (unitPart u p hp)))
    x z (multiplicity p u.val)

theorem error_packet_coefficient_mass (S : Finset (Ideal O)) (hS : SourceExclusions S)
    (firsteps : ℝ) (hfirst : FirstTail firsteps S) (η : Character) (u : FreeRow)
    (T : Finset PrimeIdeal) (hT : ∀ P ∈ T, Supported P.val)
    (hη : ∀ P ∈ T, IsCoprime P.val η.modulus)
    (x z : ℂ) (alpha eps rho : ℝ) (hQ : ∀ P ∈ T, (4 : ℝ) ≤ P.val.absNorm)
    (halpha : (51 / 100 : ℝ) ≤ alpha) (halpha1 : alpha ≤ 1)
    (heps : 0 < eps) (heps1 : eps ≤ 1 / 1000)
    (hx : x.re = alpha + 16 * eps) (hz : z.re = 17 / 50)
    (hrho : 0 ≤ rho) (hrho1 : rho ≤ 1)
    (hline : 1 - alpha - 6 * eps ≤ 1 / 2 - rho)
    (hleft : -(1 / 100 : ℝ) ≤ 1 / 2 - rho)
    (hmargin : 1 + firsteps ≤ x.re + (1 / 2 - rho)) :
    Summable (fun e : ErrorPacketIndex S u T => ‖errorPacketCoefficient S hS η u T hT x z e‖ *
      (errorPacketScale S u T e : ℝ)^(-(1 / 2 - rho))) ∧
    (∑' e : ErrorPacketIndex S u T, ‖errorPacketCoefficient S hS η u T hT x z e‖ *
      (errorPacketScale S u T e : ℝ)^(-(1 / 2 - rho))) ≤
      (579 ^ (ramifiedPrimes (markExclusions S T) u).card * Real.exp (1 / 2)) *
        errorProductSize u T * errorProductDeficit u T ^ rho
title: error_packet_coefficient_mass

statement:
## B0. The compensated-probe proof

**Theorem B0 (Hecke boundary).** Let
\[
c_0=\frac1{12}+\frac{\ell_0}{4}=0.1251133529600359\ldots,
\quad b_0=1-c_0,
\quad927\ell_0^4-3135\ell_0^3+2433\ell_0^2+275\ell_0-100=0,
\tag{B0.1}
\]
where \(0.16712007850680<\ell_0<0.16712007850682\). Every primitive finite-order Hecke \(L\)-function over \(\mathbb K=\mathbb Q(\omega)\) is zero-free in \(\Re s>b_0\), with its principal pole allowed. In particular, \(\zeta(s)\ne0\) for \(\Re s>b_0\), with its pole at one excluded.

We prove this theorem using the dependency order in T1 and the weaker initialization in T0. Reflection bounds a compensated probe; Poisson summation exposes its reciprocal Hecke principal term. Moments and the exact optimization prevent the remaining rows from cancelling that term. Appendices B1–B4 supply the finite arithmetic, reflection, moments and local factors. Notation in these appendices is local: in particular, \(M_u\) denotes the sextic probe rather than the cubic polynomial in the main text.
title: B0. The compensated-probe proof

statement:
\begin{lemma}\label{count}
Put $c_{\rm sup}=1/185$. Suppose that the available base-$U$ prime
length is at least $7/37+c_{\rm sup}$. Fix positive allowances
$\eps_m,\eps_w,\nu_0,\omega_{\rm slot}$ with
\[
 \eps_w\le10^{-3},\qquad
 \max\{\eps_w,\nu_0,\omega_{\rm slot}\}<c_{\rm sup}/16.
\]
Require $\omega_{\rm slot}$ to be no larger than the mesh supplied by
Lemma~18.1 of \cite{q30} for loss $\eps_m$ and the bounded length
ranges here, and require $\max_i\ell_i/d\le\omega_{\rm slot}$.
For each target with its fixed arithmetic data, final excluded set,
and fixed annular windows, there exist finite $A_{{\rm cnt},\eta}\ge0$,
an integer $L\ge0$, and a constant $C_\eta>0$ such that the following
raw bound holds in every retained nonbottom dynamic and amplitude bin
$\mathcal B$ under the detector's loss and height conditions:
\begin{equation}\label{raw-count}
 \#\mathcal B\le C_\eta(1+\log U)^L(1+H)^{A_{{\rm cnt},\eta}}
 U^{R_*+\eps_m+4\eps_w+6\nu_0+\omega_{\rm slot}}.
\end{equation}
Here $H\ge1$ bounds the retained physical and witness norm-twist
parameters, $\kappa=3/4$, and $1/50<\delta\le3/4$ as above.
The constants and orders may depend on the fixed arithmetic datum,
windows, slot count, strict moment margins, and prescribed losses,
but not on $U,H$, the moving rows or masks, the retained point, or any
later external tail order. They are fixed before a trial exponent in
$T_1=Z^\theta$ is chosen; the sufficiently large threshold may depend
on that exponent. Without selecting any slots, $t=1$ gives the same
type of raw bound with $R_*$ replaced by $1-2\delta/3$ and error
$\eps_m+4\eps_w$, without a prime-supply requirement.
\end{lemma}
title: count

      sourceMultiplier W0 W1 X Y Z (η.excludePrimes S hS) s
        (globalClosedCorrection η S s) (slotMultiplier η J T b s) w z*
      LFunction (fixedSourcePrincipal S hS) (6*z)*LFunction (fixedSourcePrincipal S hS) w)))

statement:
### Section 12: Optimization and limitations

The general low-energy calculation includes the cases \(M+\ell\ne1\). The dual certificate checks the full right-hand sides, not merely coefficient domination.

The lower-bound proposition is explicitly about a restricted exponent program. Its argument uses a valid admissible endpoint and proves a contradiction when the proposed boundary lies below the isolated cubic threshold.

The manuscript does not claim that relaxed energy variables are realized by actual arithmetic rows, or that the restricted lower bound is an absolute barrier for every possible extension of the method.

The final discussion of stronger inverse or mixed moments concerns future improvements, not an assumption needed for the submitted theorem.

---

def product (P Q : WeakFEPair ℂ)
    (hPf : ContinuousOn P.f (Ioi 0)) (hPg : ContinuousOn P.g (Ioi 0))
    (hQf : ContinuousOn Q.f (Ioi 0)) (hQg : ContinuousOn Q.g (Ioi 0)) :
    WeakFEPair ℂ where
  f := fun x => P.f x * Q.f x
  g := fun x => P.g x * Q.g x
  k := P.k + Q.k
  ε := P.ε * Q.ε
  f₀ := P.f₀ * Q.f₀
  g₀ := P.g₀ * Q.g₀
  hf_int := (hPf.mul hQf).locallyIntegrableOn measurableSet_Ioi
  hg_int := (hPg.mul hQg).locallyIntegrableOn measurableSet_Ioi
  hk := add_pos P.hk Q.hk
  hε := mul_ne_zero P.hε Q.hε
  h_feq x hx := by
    rw [P.h_feq x hx, Q.h_feq x hx, Real.rpow_add hx]
    simp only [smul_eq_mul, Complex.ofReal_mul]
    ring
  hf_top := rapid_product_sub P.f Q.f P.f₀ Q.f₀ P.hf_top Q.hf_top
  hg_top := rapid_product_sub P.g Q.g P.g₀ Q.g₀ P.hg_top Q.hg_top
title: product
